programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
programs.institution: Berklee College of Music — Valencia Campus
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — Valencia campus of a private US college (Berklee, Boston). Legally registered in Spain as a 'Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música' (authorisation Resolution no. 6844 of the Director General de Universidades, Estudios Superiores y Ciencia, 8 Aug 2012).
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.M.) — a UNITED STATES degree. It is NOT a Spanish 'Máster Universitario Oficial' and NOT a Spanish título propio. Berklee's own accreditation page shows that only the MA in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the MM in Scoring for Film, TV and Video Games are 'implemented under affiliation with the Universitat Politècnica de València' (i.e. carry Spanish accreditation). MPTI carries NO such statement — it is NECHE-accredited (USA) only.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL in the USA / NOT a Spanish official degree. Accrediting body: New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE), USA. In practice: a respected, genuine US master's degree; it does NOT automatically appear in Spain's RUCT as a Spanish official master, so it does not by itself give access to a Spanish doctorate without a separate equivalence procedure. The institution itself IS an officially authorised Spanish higher-education centre, which is what matters for the student visa.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Berklee Valencia is an officially authorised Spanish higher-education centre and enrols non-EU students full-time on campus every year, issuing the admission letter required for the type-D student visa. This is the single most visa-reliable private option in Spain in this subject area.
programs.focus: Music production, electronic music production and performance, DJing, audio engineering, sound design, music video, interactive media, artist/producer career development.
programs.whatYouStudy: Core: Audio Engineering; Studio Music Production; Music Video Production; Interactive Media; Electronic Music Production and Performance; Career Preparation. Electives (choose 4+ credits) include mixing, DJing, advanced video production, synthesizer design and sound design. Final Project module: three seminars (Past/Present/Future) plus a Culminating Experience proposal, development and public defence. Minimum 32–33 credits, maximum 37–38 with the optional internship semester. Software taught: Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere.
programs.durationEcts: One full academic year = three consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer; summer term 6–7 weeks). Optional fourth internship semester. 32–38 US credits (US credit system, not ECTS).
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September (fall start).
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD 50,430 tuition for the full 2026/2027 graduate programme (per-credit rate USD 1,615). Same figure = whole programme, since the master is one year.
programs.tuitionTotal: USD 50,430 total tuition for the whole programme, academic year 2026/2027, as published on the Berklee Valencia graduate tuition page. Non-EU students pay the same as everyone else — Berklee has a single international fee.
programs.otherFees: Application fee USD 150 (non-refundable; waived for Berklee alumni). Non-refundable tuition deposit USD 2,500. Comprehensive fee USD 1,600. Student Health Insurance Plan — amount 'varies' (UNVERIFIED). Required software bundle USD 800 for the Music Production programme. Professional Recording Services USD 2,990 — this applies to the Scoring programme ONLY, not MPTI.
programs.equipmentRequired: Yes. Required software bundle USD 800 (music production programme). Laptop estimated at USD 3,000 by Berklee (the page notes it 'may be waived' if you already own a suitable machine). Studios and hardware are provided on campus.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year direct cost to the college: approx. USD 52,980 (tuition 50,430 + comprehensive fee 1,600 + software 800 + application 150) plus health insurance (UNVERIFIED amount). Adding Berklee's own published indirect estimates — housing USD 10,000–12,000, books USD 300–800, local transport USD 300–600, personal USD 1,000, laptop USD 3,000 — a realistic all-in first year is approximately USD 67,000–71,000 (roughly EUR 62,000–66,000 at mid-2026 rates). This is by far the most expensive option in this slice.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Berklee's entrance-requirements page states MPTI applicants 'should possess a bachelor's degree in music while demonstrating technological proficiency… Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship.' Transcripts from outside the US/Canada must be assessed by an approved third-party credential evaluation service (extra cost, UNVERIFIED).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, conditionally. Published wording: 'Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship.' A BSc in Software Engineering is explicitly acceptable as the degree — but the burden of proof shifts entirely to demonstrated musicianship and production ability. The 'technological proficiency' criterion is where his software background is a genuine asset.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio/supporting materials are submitted through the online graduate application. The public entrance-requirements page does NOT itemise the portfolio contents — UNVERIFIED; must be requested from admissionsvalencia@berklee.edu. Selection criteria published: 'excellent musicality', 'facility with technology', 'success in both artistic and academic settings', leadership, motivation, intellectual curiosity.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition is required for MPTI. Selected applicants are invited to an INTERVIEW. (Auditions apply to the Contemporary Performance programme.)
programs.englishTest: Required if English is not your first language. Berklee accepts TOEFL, IELTS and Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) / C1 Business Higher or above. The exact minimum IELTS band for MPTI is not published on the Valencia entrance-requirements page — UNVERIFIED; the only published number found was TOEFL 80 for the Contemporary Performance programme (pre-21 Jan 2026 test versions). Requirement may be waived if the bachelor's was completed at an English-medium university. He must confirm the exact IELTS band directly with admissions before booking the test.
programs.applicationOpens: Applications open in the autumn preceding entry (the Early Action deadline is 1 November). Exact 2027-entry opening date UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: Three rounds, recurring annual dates: Early Action — application 1 November, scholarship 15 November, decision by 15 December. Regular Action — application 15 January, scholarship 1 February, decision by 15 March. Extended Action — application and scholarship 10 March, decision by 20 April. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start these map to 1 Nov 2026 / 15 Jan 2027 / 10 Mar 2027. PRIOR CYCLE pattern — confirm the exact 2027-entry dates when the cycle opens. Note: scholarship deadlines differ from application deadlines in the Early and Regular rounds.
programs.scholarships: Non-EU/Tunisian applicants ARE eligible for most awards. Berklee General Scholarship (all master's applicants, amount varies). Outstanding Women Scholarship — up to 70% of tuition + mentorship, includes MPTI (not applicable to him). Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship — up to 50% of tuition, for demonstrated leadership supporting under-represented communities and first-generation students (he may qualify as first-generation — worth testing). Berklee Global Partners USD 18,000 (students/alumni/faculty of partner schools — check whether SMU MedTech is a partner; almost certainly not). Berklee Alumni USD 18,000 (not applicable). CACSA–Palau de les Arts: Valencian residents only — NOT available to him. Berklee Valencia allocated more than EUR 125,000 in scholarships across all master's programmes for 2026/2027. Important limitation published by Berklee: entering international students are NOT eligible for institutional need-based aid. Scholarship deadlines: 15 Nov (early) / 1 Feb (regular) / 10 Mar (extended).
programs.paymentPlans: USD 2,500 non-refundable deposit on acceptance. Instalment/payment-plan terms for graduate students are not detailed on the tuition page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: State-of-the-art recording studios and technology labs on the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía campus, with professional-grade software (Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere) and hardware described as equivalent to professional facilities.
programs.reputationSignals: The strongest global brand in contemporary music education; NECHE-accredited; campus housed inside the Palau de les Arts opera house; two of its four Valencia masters carry Spanish accreditation via Universitat Politècnica de València, showing a real relationship with the Spanish system. MPTI graduates are explicitly positioned toward careers as artists, producers, DJs, electronic composers and technologists. Red flag to weigh: cost is 10–15x the Spanish private-university alternatives, and MPTI specifically is the one Valencia master WITHOUT Spanish accreditation.
programs.recommendation: This is the single best CONTENT fit in Spain for someone who wants to be an international DJ/producer — DJing, electronic music production and performance are core curriculum, not bolt-ons, and the network is real. But be blunt about three things. (1) Cost: roughly USD 67,000–71,000 all-in for one year, with no need-based aid for international students. That is not 'budget-sensitive'. (2) Admissions risk: with no music degree, no conservatory training, no professional audio experience and a portfolio still being built, he is applying against the explicit standard 'a high degree of musicianship'. He would need roughly 12 months of serious portfolio work before the Nov 2026–Mar 2027 deadlines. (3) The MPTI degree is a US master, not a Spanish official title — fine for industry, weaker if he ever wants a Spanish PhD or a title-dependent public-sector role. Verdict: apply, aim for Early Action to maximise scholarship chances, target the Diversity scholarship, but treat it as the aspirational option and have a cheaper Spanish option in reserve. Do not commit self-pay funds to this without a scholarship of 40%+.

programs.program: Master of Music in Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games (SFTV)
programs.institution: Berklee College of Music — Valencia Campus
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — Valencia campus of a private US college; Spanish 'Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música'.
programs.qualification: Master of Music (US degree) which, unlike MPTI, is ALSO accredited in Spain: Berklee's accreditation page states this programme 'has also been implemented under affiliation with the Universitat Politècnica de València'. So it carries both a US award and Spanish official recognition through UPV.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL in both systems. NECHE (USA) + Spanish accreditation via affiliation with Universitat Politècnica de València. In practice: this is the Berklee Valencia master with the strongest legal standing in Spain/the EHEA — valid for further study and unambiguous for visa and title-recognition purposes.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — same authorised centre as MPTI, plus Spanish accreditation through UPV, which removes any residual doubt.
programs.focus: Composition and scoring for film, TV and video games; orchestration; recording and mixing of score; game audio implementation.
programs.whatYouStudy: Scoring, orchestration, conducting, score recording sessions with professional musicians, and game-audio work. Full module list not captured from the official page — UNVERIFIED at this level of detail.
programs.durationEcts: One academic year, three consecutive semesters (US credit system, comparable to MPTI's 32–38 credits). Exact credit count UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September.
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD 50,430 for 2026/2027 (same graduate tuition as MPTI).
programs.tuitionTotal: USD 50,430 total tuition, academic year 2026/2027.
programs.otherFees: Application fee USD 150. Non-refundable tuition deposit USD 2,500. Comprehensive fee USD 1,600. Professional Recording Services fee USD 2,990 — CHARGED TO THIS PROGRAMME SPECIFICALLY. Required software bundle USD 700 for Scoring. Health insurance varies (UNVERIFIED).
programs.equipmentRequired: Yes — USD 700 software bundle; laptop estimated USD 3,000 (may be waived).
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year direct: approx. USD 55,870 (50,430 + 2,990 + 1,600 + 700 + 150) plus insurance. All-in with housing and living costs: approximately USD 70,000–74,000.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree preferred in composition, electronic music production or film scoring; 'performance or other backgrounds considered with strong composition background'.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Weakly. Published wording favours composition/electronic-production/film-scoring degrees, with other backgrounds accepted only 'with strong composition background'. For a software-engineering graduate with no composition training this is a harder entry than MPTI.
programs.portfolioSpec: Composition portfolio required through the graduate application; exact specification not published on the entrance-requirements page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Interview for selected applicants; audition not required for this programme (auditions apply to Contemporary Performance).
programs.englishTest: TOEFL / IELTS / Cambridge C1 accepted; exact minimum band UNVERIFIED — confirm with admissions.
programs.applicationOpens: Autumn preceding entry; exact date UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: Same three rounds as MPTI: 1 Nov / 15 Jan / 10 Mar, i.e. 1 Nov 2026, 15 Jan 2027, 10 Mar 2027 for a Sept 2027 start. PRIOR CYCLE pattern — confirm.
programs.scholarships: Same graduate scholarship set as MPTI, and SFTV is explicitly listed among the four programmes covered by the Outstanding Women scholarship (up to 70%). Diversity scholarship up to 50%. No need-based institutional aid for entering international students.
programs.paymentPlans: USD 2,500 deposit; further instalment terms UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Recording studios at the Palau de les Arts campus; scoring stage sessions with live musicians (the USD 2,990 recording-services fee funds this).
programs.reputationSignals: Spanish-accredited via UPV, which is a meaningful quality signal. Strong pipeline into film/TV/game scoring.
programs.recommendation: Listed for completeness and because it is the Berklee Valencia master with the cleanest Spanish accreditation. But it is the WRONG programme for his stated goal — it is composition-for-picture, not DJ/electronic production, and its entry bar (strong composition background) is the one he is least able to clear. Skip it unless his ambitions shift toward game/film scoring. Also note it is the most expensive Berklee option because of the USD 2,990 recording-services fee.

programs.program: Master of Science in Acoustics, Audio and Vibrations (Máster Universitario en Acústica, Audio y Vibraciones)
programs.institution: La Salle Campus Barcelona — Universitat Ramon Llull (URL)
programs.institutionType: Private university (Universitat Ramon Llull is a private, church-founded Spanish university; La Salle is its engineering/technology campus).
programs.qualification: MÁSTER UNIVERSITARIO OFICIAL. The programme page states the degree certificate is issued by the Ministry of Education. 60 ECTS.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL. Accredited within the Spanish official system (ANECA/AQU Catalunya framework, degree issued by the Ministry of Education) as a Máster Universitario of Universitat Ramon Llull. In practice: valid across the EHEA, valid for PhD entry, unambiguous for the student visa, and recognised by employers as a real engineering master.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Official Spanish master at a recognised private university, full-time on-site in Barcelona — the standard and safest route to a Spanish type-D student visa.
programs.focus: Acoustics engineering, audio signal processing, vibration control, noise control, applied AI in acoustics. This is ENGINEERING, not music production.
programs.whatYouStudy: Noise control, vibration management, audio signal processing, numerical simulation, laboratory experimentation, and application of artificial intelligence to sustainable acoustic solutions across aerospace, automotive, rail, construction, industrial and entertainment sectors.
programs.durationEcts: 60 ECTS, 10 months.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, October. Published start date for the current cycle: 19 October 2026. For a Sept/Oct 2027 entry, expect mid-October 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. La Salle does not publish the tuition figure for this master on its programme page or on its masters index; it directs enquiries to admissions (+34 93 290 2400).
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED — must be requested from La Salle admissions. Do not rely on third-party aggregator figures.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. A pre-enrolment/place-reservation deposit is used at La Salle (a EUR 1,500 pre-enrolment deposit is documented for 2026 admissions in general La Salle admissions material, but this was not confirmed on the master's own page for this programme — treat as UNVERIFIED for this specific master).
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. Work is done in the on-campus Acoustics Lab, so no personal studio purchase is implied.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — tuition is not published. Barcelona living costs must be budgeted on top and the Spanish student visa requires proof of 100% of IPREM per month (EUR 600/month in 2026 per Spanish immigration guidance), i.e. roughly EUR 7,200 for a 12-month stay.
programs.entryRequirements: Published list of accepted bachelor degrees: Mechanical Engineering, Telecommunications Systems Engineering, Industrial Technology Engineering, Audiovisual Systems, Physics, Aerospace Vehicle Engineering, Mathematics, Civil Engineering — 'or similar'. 30 places.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: This programme accepts ONLY non-music (STEM) backgrounds — a music degree would not qualify. Software Engineering is NOT on the published list but plausibly falls under 'or similar' given the signal-processing and AI content. He must get this confirmed in writing by admissions before investing effort. Exact wording: 'Candidates must hold one of the following (or similar) graduate degrees'.
programs.portfolioSpec: None — this is an engineering master. No portfolio required.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.englishTest: No formal English proficiency requirement is published on the programme or requirements page — UNVERIFIED. Given the programme is taught entirely in English, an IELTS score will almost certainly be requested of a non-native applicant; confirm the required band with admissions.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling; enrolment opens through the La Salle admissions portal. Exact 2027 opening date UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: No published application deadline for this master — rolling admission until the 30 places fill. UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle.
programs.scholarships: Substantial published master's scholarship programme, and international students are eligible for most of it. Academic Excellence Scholarship: 50% (GPA 9.5+), 40% (GPA 8.5+), 20% (GPA 8.0+) — 2 to 4 awards per programme; open to international students if the GPA system is comparable. La Salle Boost Scholarships: 10–40% for strong academic/professional record or limited financial resources; 25% for disability ≥33%. Lasallians Scholarship 10% for alumni of any La Salle school worldwide. Partner University Scholarship 15%. 'la Caixa' Foundation international master's grants (70% of registration fee) are also referenced. NOT available to him: Massó Foundation (Spanish/EU/legal residents only), Casa de México (Mexican nationals), Carolina Foundation (Ibero-American), #SheTechs (women; and non-EU candidates need a work permit). CRITICAL RULE published by La Salle: 'Different scholarships, discounts, and financial aid options cannot be combined.'
programs.paymentPlans: Not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. FUNDAE company-subsidised training is referenced but applies to employees of Spanish companies, not to him.
programs.facilities: Acoustics Lab inside the Interactive Arts & Science Laboratory (IASLab) at La Salle–URL, Barcelona (C. Sant Joan de La Salle 42). Numerical simulation and measurement facilities.
programs.reputationSignals: Universitat Ramon Llull is one of Spain's most established private universities; La Salle has a long track record in audio/acoustics engineering and also runs an official Master in Architectural and Environmental Acoustics and an MSc in Digital Arts and Creative Technologies. Taught in English with a 30-student cap. No red flags found.
programs.recommendation: The strongest DEGREE in this slice for him, and the weakest fit for his stated goal. It is an official Spanish master, taught in English, at a serious private university, aimed squarely at engineering graduates — it is the one programme here where his BSc in Software Engineering is an advantage rather than a liability, and where no portfolio and no musicianship proof is needed. It also has real published scholarships (up to 50% on GPA alone) and a clean visa path. But it will NOT make him a DJ or a music producer: it is noise control, vibrations and signal processing for automotive/aerospace/construction. Recommend it only if his priority shifts to 'get to Europe with a real, fundable, visa-safe technical degree and build the music career on the side in Barcelona' — which, given his profile and budget sensitivity, is a genuinely defensible strategy. First action: email admissions to confirm (a) Software Engineering counts as a 'similar' degree, (b) the tuition figure, (c) the IELTS band.

programs.program: Máster de Formación Permanente en Producción Musical (semipresencial)
programs.institution: UCAM — Universidad Católica San Antonio de Murcia
programs.institutionType: Private university (Catholic, private, Murcia).
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — specifically a 'Máster de Formación Permanente'. This is UCAM's OWN diploma, 60 ECTS, NOT an official Máster Universitario. It does not appear in the official RUCT catalogue of official degrees and does not give direct access to a Spanish doctorate.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL as a degree. It is a título propio / Máster de Formación Permanente issued by UCAM. UCAM itself is a fully recognised Spanish private university (so the institution is legitimate and appears in RUCT), but THIS AWARD is not an ANECA-verified official master. In practice: a credible university-branded certificate with industry weight, but legally it is a certificate, not an official master's degree.
programs.visaEligible: PROBABLY, BUT UNVERIFIED AND RISKY. Spanish student visas require full-time study at an authorised centre; UCAM qualifies as an authorised centre. However this programme is SEMIPRESENCIAL (hybrid), and consulates routinely refuse or downgrade visa applications for programmes that are not full-time face-to-face. He must obtain written confirmation from UCAM's international office that this specific programme supports a type-D student visa before paying anything. Do not assume.
programs.focus: Music production, composition techniques, artistic development, recording, mixing and mastering.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition and production techniques, artistic development, all phases of creating and recording a musical work, mixing and mastering. Graduates exit as music producer, mixing specialist, mastering technician or studio assistant engineer. Steinberg Cubase professional certification is awarded on completion.
programs.durationEcts: 60 ECTS, one academic year.
programs.language: Spanish. NOTE: he must be able to study in Spanish — this is a hard blocker if his Spanish is not strong.
programs.intakes: One intake per year (academic year start; UCAM postgraduate courses typically begin in October). Exact 2027 start date UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionPerYear: EUR 3,900 academic fee per course year (published on the UCAM programme page). Same fee applies to non-EU students — UCAM does not publish a separate international rate.
programs.tuitionTotal: EUR 3,900 total tuition for the whole 60-ECTS programme. Academic year of reference: the currently advertised edition (2026/2027) — confirm for 2027/2028.
programs.otherFees: Pre-enrolment fee EUR 235 (non-refundable). School insurance EUR 59.12. No other fees published.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Given the semipresencial format, a capable laptop and a DAW licence should be assumed; Cubase certification is included in the programme.
programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 4,194.12 in institutional costs (3,900 + 235 + 59.12). This is BY FAR the cheapest credible university-branded music-production master in this slice — roughly 1/12 of Berklee Valencia. Add living costs in Murcia and the visa's IPREM proof of funds (EUR 600/month in 2026).
programs.entryRequirements: An official university degree or equivalent higher-education qualification (Grado or official master level). The page explicitly welcomes graduates in Audiovisual Communication, Journalism, Musicology, Music Education, TELECOMMUNICATIONS OR COMPUTER ENGINEERING, and professional conservatory diploma holders. Only 12 places.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly. 'Ingeniería de Telecomunicaciones o Informática' (Telecommunications or Computer Engineering) is named in the published target-profile list. A BSc in Software Engineering maps directly onto this. This is one of the very few programmes in the slice where his degree is named as a welcome background.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio requirement published — UNVERIFIED. Admission is through the UCAM postgraduate admissions portal.
programs.auditionSpec: None published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is in Spanish. No IELTS needed. But Spanish-language capability will be required (level not published — UNVERIFIED).
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling through the UCAM admissions portal (www.ucam.edu/admision). Exact 2027 opening UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: No published deadline; places are limited to 12 so effectively first-come. UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle.
programs.scholarships: No scholarship specifically identified for non-EU applicants on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. UCAM's general postgraduate financing is described as 'payment plans and financing options available through banking entities', which realistically requires a Spanish bank relationship.
programs.paymentPlans: Yes — payment plans and financing through partner banking entities are advertised, terms UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Campus de los Jerónimos, Murcia. Programme partners: Sony Music España and the MasterFather platform. Teaching by working producers including Ludovico Vagnone, Antonio Escobar, Ed Is Dead, Pablo Rous, Baghira and Luis del Toro. Official Steinberg Cubase certification included.
programs.reputationSignals: Real industry partnership with Sony Music España; genuinely well-known Spanish producers on the teaching staff (Ed Is Dead and Baghira are recognised names in Spanish electronic music); Steinberg certification is a concrete, verifiable credential. UCAM absorbed/rebranded its older 'Máster en Ingeniería de Sonido y Producción Discográfica' into this programme (the old URL now resolves to this one) — so treat any listing of the sound-engineering master as superseded. Red flag: only 12 places and a hybrid format; and the award is a certificate, not a degree.
programs.recommendation: The best VALUE in this slice by an enormous margin: EUR 4,194 all-in for a 60-ECTS university-branded music production master with Sony Music involvement and named Spanish electronic producers teaching. His software-engineering degree is explicitly listed as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, and no IELTS is needed. Three serious caveats he must resolve before treating it as a plan: (1) it is a TÍTULO PROPIO, not an official master — legally a certificate; (2) it is SEMIPRESENCIAL, which is the classic reason a Spanish consulate refuses a student visa — get written visa confirmation from UCAM first; (3) it is taught in Spanish. If he can clear the visa and the language, this is the highest return-on-euro option available to him in Spain. If the visa answer is no, it is worthless to him as a relocation route.

programs.program: Postgrado en Producción Musical y Artística (with The Music Station)
programs.institution: Universidad Francisco de Vitoria (UFV)
programs.institutionType: Private university (Catholic, private, Madrid).
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — and note carefully: it is a 'Postgrado', 30 ECTS, THREE MONTHS. THIS IS NOT A MASTER. It is a short postgraduate certificate issued by UFV itself.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. UFV's own título propio at postgraduate-course level. Not ANECA-verified, not an official master, no PhD access, and at 30 ECTS it is half the credit weight of a master.
programs.visaEligible: NO / effectively no. The programme runs September 2026 to January 2027 — approximately four months of evening classes (Mon–Fri 18:00–20:00). A Spanish type-D student visa is for stays over 90 days on full-time study; a part-time evening course of this length will not reliably support a residence permit, and the schedule is not full-time. UNVERIFIED whether UFV would even issue the required documentation. Treat as NOT a relocation route.
programs.focus: Practical music production: audio fundamentals, songwriting, pre-production, production and creative direction, post-production, mixing, mastering, industry contracts.
programs.whatYouStudy: Module 1 — audio fundamentals, music theory, songwriting, Pro Tools training (41 h). Module 2 — pre-production techniques and workflow (22 h). Module 3 — production processes and creative direction (32 h). Module 4 — post-production, mixing, mastering, industry contracts (57 h). Total roughly 152 contact hours.
programs.durationEcts: 30 ECTS, 3 months (September 2026 – January 2027 for the current edition). Classes Monday–Friday 18:00–20:00, face-to-face on the Madrid campus.
programs.intakes: One edition advertised, starting September. A 2027 edition is not yet published — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionPerYear: EUR 6,100 published as the total price. Note a discrepancy in UFV's own published breakdown: reservation fee EUR 960 + enrolment EUR 5,540 = EUR 6,500, which does not reconcile with the EUR 6,100 headline. He must ask UFV in writing which figure is correct.
programs.tuitionTotal: EUR 6,100 headline for the whole 30-ECTS programme (2026/2027 edition), with the internal breakdown inconsistent as noted. Same price for non-EU students — no separate international rate published.
programs.otherFees: Reservation/place fee EUR 960 (part of, or in addition to, the total — see discrepancy above). No separate application, materials or exam fee published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: Software is INCLUDED rather than required-to-buy: the programme includes a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence and official Avid Pro Tools 100-level certification (PT101 + PT110). A personal laptop should be assumed — UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 6,100–6,500 institutional cost for a 3-month, 30-ECTS certificate. Per-ECTS this is the most expensive Spanish-university option in the slice (about EUR 203/ECTS versus UCAM's EUR 65/ECTS), though the included Ableton Suite perpetual licence (~EUR 599 retail) and Avid certification offset part of it.
programs.entryRequirements: Aimed at people with 'formación o experiencia previa en música o sonido' (prior training or experience in music or sound) — musicians, composers, emerging producers, audiovisual professionals, sound technicians. Rolling enrolment, limited places.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PROBLEMATIC for him. The published target profile requires prior training OR experience in music or sound. He has neither a music degree nor professional audio experience. Whether self-taught production work counts is UNVERIFIED — he would need to ask, and a strong portfolio would be the only lever.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published — UNVERIFIED.

programs.englishTest: Not applicable — Spanish-language programme. No IELTS required.

programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
programs.institution: Berklee College of Music — Valencia Campus
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — US private conservatory operating a Spanish campus (Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música, centre code 46061691, authorised by Resolution 6844 of 8 August 2012)
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.M.) — a UNITED STATES degree awarded by Berklee College of Music. It is NOT a Spanish 'Máster Universitario Oficial' and NOT a 'Título Propio' either — it is a foreign degree delivered on Spanish soil.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL IN SPAIN (for this specific programme). Berklee's own accreditation page states plainly that MPTI and the M.M. in Contemporary Performance hold ONLY NECHE (New England Commission of Higher Education, USA) accreditation, while only two other Valencia masters — the M.A. in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the M.M. in Scoring for Film, TV and Video Games — are ANECA-accredited in Spain via a collaboration with Universidad Politécnica de València. Practical meaning: MPTI is a genuine, regionally accredited US master's degree (well recognised by the music industry worldwide), but in Spain/EHEA terms it is a foreign title. To use it for a Spanish public-sector job or a Spanish PhD he would have to go through 'equivalencia/homologación' at the Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades — an uncertain, slow process. Berklee itself warns applicants to 'carefully research degree recognition requirements in their home country'.
programs.visaEligible: YES. The Valencia campus is an authorised Spanish higher-education centre and Berklee explicitly states that all master's participants on the Valencia campus need a visa unless they are EU/EEA/Swiss citizens — i.e. the campus routinely issues the acceptance letters used for Spanish student visas. This is one of the safest visa routes in this slice.
programs.focus: Music production, studio and hybrid recording, electronic music production and live performance, sound design, music video, interactive media, DJing, music technology and innovation.
programs.whatYouStudy: Core module: Audio Engineering; Studio Music Production; Music Video Production; Interactive Media; Electronic Music Production; Career Preparation. Final Project module: three seminars (Past, Present, Future) plus Culminating Experience Project (Proposal, Development, Defense). Elective module: 4 credits chosen from mixing, DJing, video production, interactive media and synthesis. Optional ensembles, private instruction and an optional internship.
programs.durationEcts: One full academic year / three consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer — summer term is 6–7 weeks). 32–33 US credits minimum (33–34 with internship), 37–38 maximum. Credits are US semester-hours, not ECTS.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, starting in the autumn (September).
programs.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree from an accredited institution (diploma required before enrolment). Official transcripts; for non-US/Canadian institutions a credential evaluation is required (SpanTran or Educational Credential Evaluators recommended — a real extra cost and lead time for a Tunisian transcript). Statement of purpose 400–500 words in English. CV in English. One professional letter of recommendation (not from a peer). Berklee describes the target candidate as showing 'excellent musicality', 'facility with technology' and 'success in both artistic and academic settings'.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — the published requirement is only 'a completed bachelor's degree from an accredited institution', with no stipulation that it be in music. A BSc in Software Engineering is formally eligible and 'facility with technology' is explicitly named as a desired trait. HOWEVER, admission is decided on the portfolio: with no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional audio credits, the three recorded projects must carry the entire application. This is a genuinely competitive programme, not an open-enrolment school.
programs.portfolioSpec: MPTI-specific: (1) three recorded projects (audio and/or video); (2) a 3-minute video in which the applicant describes THREE potential thesis projects, with specifics on the personal growth each would deliver; (3) optional scores. All materials must be assembled into a SINGLE PDF with embedded links — external file-sharing platforms (Dropbox/WeTransfer) are explicitly not accepted.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition for MPTI. The 3-minute thesis-concept video functions as the interview substitute. (Contemporary Performance, by contrast, requires performance videos.)
programs.englishTest: IELTS accepted. For MPTI and all programmes EXCEPT Contemporary Performance the bar is high: IELTS 7.5, or TOEFL iBT 100, or Duolingo 130, or Cambridge CAE/C1 Business Higher. (Contemporary Performance only needs IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80 / Duolingo 110 / Cambridge B2 First.) He has NOT taken IELTS — a 7.5 is a serious target and should be booked and prepared for well before autumn 2026.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027 entry cycle. Berklee normally opens the graduate application in the late summer preceding the Early Action deadline.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published cycle structure: Early Action — application 1 November, scholarship 15 November, decisions 15 December. Regular Action — application 15 January, scholarship 1 February, decisions 15 March. Extended Action — application and scholarship both 10 March, decisions 20 April. These dates recur annually but the specific September-2027-entry dates are not yet published. For a September 2027 start he would apply around November 2026 – March 2027. Note the scholarship deadline is DIFFERENT from (and later than) the application deadline for Early and Regular action — missing it forfeits money.
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD $50,430 for the full one-year programme, academic year 2026/2027. Per-credit rate $1,615.
programs.tuitionTotal: USD $50,430 total tuition for the whole programme (2026/2027 figures). Berklee Valencia prices in US dollars, so he also carries FX risk. Non-EU students pay the same tuition as EU students — there is no separate international rate.
programs.otherFees: Application fee $150 (non-refundable; waived only for Berklee alumni). Non-refundable tuition deposit $2,500 to accept the offer (deducted from the first tuition bill). Comprehensive fee $1,600 — mandatory, covers registration into the Spanish educational system, compulsory health insurance and campus services. Required software bundle $200–$850 depending on programme. Professional Recording Services Fee $2,990 — applies to the Scoring programme ONLY, not MPTI. Credential-evaluation fee for the Tunisian transcript (SpanTran/ECE) — amount UNVERIFIED, payable to the third-party evaluator.
programs.equipmentRequired: A laptop is required and budgeted by Berklee at $3,000 (estimated indirect cost). A required software bundle costs $200–$850 on top of tuition. Books $300–$800.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Berklee's own published estimate of total cost of attendance is approximately USD $69,380–$73,370 for the year, comprising tuition $50,430 + comprehensive fee $1,600 + software $200–850 + laptop $3,000 + housing $10,000–12,000 + books $300–800 + local transport $300–600 + personal expenses $1,000. Add the $150 application fee and the health-insurance line. In euros this is roughly €63,000–€67,000 at parity-ish rates — by far the most expensive option in this slice.
programs.paymentPlans: Tuition is divided into three equal parts and billed three times per year to the student's Berklee.edu address. The $2,500 deposit is credited against the first instalment. No published early-bird or referral discounts; the discounting happens through scholarships instead.
programs.scholarships: Berklee Valencia states it offers over $1.5 million in merit- and need-based scholarships to admitted graduate students. Awards a Tunisian non-EU applicant could realistically receive: (1) Berklee General Scholarship — all master's applicants, amount varies, automatic consideration; (2) Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship — UP TO 50% OF TUITION, for demonstrated leadership supporting under-represented communities and for first-generation students; requires a separate submission (3-minute video or 500-word essay) to scholarshipsvalencia@berklee.edu by 1 February (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date); (3) Berklee Outstanding Women Scholarships — up to 70% of tuition, one per programme (not applicable to a male applicant); (4) Berklee Groove Scholarship — up to 90% of tuition but restricted to the M.M. in Contemporary Performance (Production Concentration) with principal instrument drums/bass/rhythm-section/traditional-folk, so not available on MPTI; (5) Alumni and Global Partners scholarships $18,000 each — he qualifies for neither. The CACSA–Palau de les Arts scholarships and the €125,000+ 'Valencian Students' fund advertised for 2026–2027 are restricted to Valencian residents and are NOT open to him.
programs.facilities: Purpose-built campus inside the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía (Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències). Multiple recording studios, scoring stage, production suites, DJ/electronic performance facilities, and a well-known network of visiting industry artists. Berklee's brand recognition among producers and labels is the strongest of any institution in this slice.
programs.reputationSignals: Strongest global brand in contemporary music education; NECHE-accredited US degree; two sister programmes carry ANECA accreditation via UPV, which demonstrates the campus can meet Spanish quality standards even though MPTI itself does not. Extensive alumni network in production and electronic music. RED FLAG for this candidate: the price. Also note the accreditation asymmetry — a student assuming 'a Berklee master in Spain must be a Spanish master' would be wrong, and this is exactly the trap to avoid.
programs.recommendation: The best programme in this slice on craft, network and visa safety — and the one most likely to actually launch an international DJ/producer career. But it is a $70k-a-year decision for someone with no music degree, no audio experience and no IELTS yet. My candid verdict: worth applying to ONLY if he (a) sits IELTS early and clears 7.5, (b) spends the next 12 months building three genuinely strong recorded productions, and (c) applies Early Action AND submits the Diversity Scholarship essay by the separate scholarship deadline. Without a 50%+ scholarship this is not a budget-sensible choice, and he should treat a full-price offer as a decline. Also be clear-eyed: the MPTI degree is a US title, not a Spanish official master.

programs.program: Máster en Producción de Música Electrónica
programs.institution: SAE Institute Spain (SAE Creative Media Education)
programs.institutionType: Specialist audio academy — international chain (SAE Institute, global network); SAE Barcelona additionally holds status as a private higher artistic-education school in music
programs.qualification: DUAL AWARD, both non-official: (1) 'Máster de Formación Permanente' of 25 ECTS accredited by UDIMA (Universidad a Distancia de Madrid, a private university) — i.e. a TÍTULO PROPIO, plus a 'Máster Profesional' route for those without a degree; and (2) a Professional Diploma from SAE Creative Media Education.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. This is a Máster de Formación Permanente / título propio issued under UDIMA's own authority. It is NOT a 'Máster Universitario Oficial', it is NOT ANECA-verified, it does not confer EHEA official master status and it does not give access to a Spanish PhD. NOTE THE ECTS: 25 ECTS is very small — an official Spanish master is 60–120 ECTS. Calling a 25-ECTS course a 'máster' is legal in Spain for a título propio but it is exactly the marketing trap to be sceptical about. Separately, SAE Barcelona's UNDERGRADUATE Título de Grado en Música (240 ECTS, four specialities including Composición de Música Electrónica) IS official — authorised by the Generalitat de Catalunya and validated by AQU Catalunya — but that is a bachelor-level award and is a different thing entirely from this master.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED / LIKELY PROBLEMATIC AS SOLD. SAE Spain publishes an international-students section that explicitly covers 'student visa' guidance for non-EU applicants, and states international applicants need a student visa. However a 25-ECTS, 8-month, non-official título propio is a weak basis for a Spanish student visa, which normally expects a full-time programme of substantial duration at a recognised centre. He must get written confirmation from SAE that THIS specific programme generates a visa-supporting acceptance letter before paying anything.
programs.focus: Electronic music production, sound design, synthesis, live electronics, DJ-adjacent performance, mixing and mastering — the closest published match in Spain to this candidate's stated goal.
programs.whatYouStudy: First semester: sound theory, music theory, MIDI protocol, audio processing, synthesizers, sampling, and mixing in Ableton Live and Logic Pro X. Second semester: advanced production, hardware synthesizers (Moog, Prophet/Dave Smith, Doepfer, Elektron, Roland, Akai), sound design, live performance, mastering, and industry career management. Includes the official Ableton Live Production Certificate.
programs.durationEcts: 8 months full-time; 25 ECTS.
programs.language: Spanish. SAE states Spanish-language proficiency is required for international students — a real obstacle for a Tunisian applicant with no Spanish.
programs.intakes: Two intakes per year. Madrid: February 2026 and October 2026. Barcelona: October 2026 and February 2027. (These are the currently published dates; the SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 intake is not yet published — PRIOR CYCLE pattern, confirm new dates.)
programs.entryRequirements: An official university degree (Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Arquitectura or Diplomatura) for the 60-ECTS Formación Permanente route; alternatively at least 2 years of documented professional experience for the 'Máster Profesional' route. Minimum age 18. Spanish-language proficiency. Completion of an admission questionnaire and an access interview.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly. The stated requirement is 'una titulación universitaria oficial (Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Arquitectura o Diplomatura)' with no subject restriction — a BSc in Software Engineering satisfies it directly. No music degree, conservatory training or prior audio experience is demanded. This is the most accessible entry route in the whole slice for his exact profile.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio is published as a requirement. Admission is by questionnaire plus an 'entrevista de acceso' (access interview).
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. An admission interview only.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS required — and no English-language route either. Instruction and admission are in SPANISH, and SAE states Spanish proficiency is required of international students. He would need to reach a working level of Spanish (realistically B1–B2) before October 2027.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling — SAE runs continuous admissions with Open House Days that carry enrolment discounts.
programs.deadline: No published hard deadline; rolling admission tied to the February and October start dates. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for a 2027 start.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. SAE Spain does not publish the price of this master anywhere on its site. Do not accept a verbal quote — insist on a written fee schedule.
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED. For scale only, and from third-party listings rather than SAE's own pages: SAE's Audio Engineering Diploma (a different, undergraduate-level product) is quoted at around €8,700, ranging roughly €8,000–€10,000 depending on payment plan; SAE's BA/BSc (Hons) Audio Production is quoted at €14,000–€16,000 depending on plan. Neither figure is the price of this master and neither is officially published.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED — enrolment fee, materials fee and exam fees are not published.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED as a formal requirement, but the syllabus is built on Ableton Live and Logic Pro X, so a capable laptop and at minimum an Ableton Live licence should be budgeted. An official Ableton Live Production Certificate is included in the programme.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — SAE publishes no price for this programme. Estimating would be irresponsible.
programs.paymentPlans: SAE España operates a published plan structure: Plan A is a single payment that carries an early-payment discount; Plan C is monthly instalments without the discount. Enrolling during an Open House Day reportedly lets students take monthly instalments at the discounted Plan A price. Exact figures UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: SAE Barcelona publishes an institutional discount schedule, but almost none of it reaches a Tunisian non-EU applicant. Available in principle: Active-student/alumni 40%; family members (siblings/cousins/relatives) 20%; disability ≥33% 30%; large-family status 10%; unemployment/ERTE 10%; excellence (9+ GPA in Spanish bachillerato or in SAE's own first year) 60%. The government routes — MEC scholarships and the Generalitat de Catalunya 2026-2027 non-university grants (income-based €1,700, relocation €2,700, basic €300–350, academic performance €50–125) — are for Spanish/resident students and do NOT apply to a newly arrived non-EU student. The Yamaha Europe Foundation grant (€1,000–€2,000, musicians under 25 at recognised European institutions) is the one realistically open award. Net realistic scholarship for this candidate: close to zero, other than possibly the Yamaha grant.
programs.facilities: Barcelona campus: 2,700 m², seven professional audio studios, a production studio with an ICON D-CONTROL digital console, three post-production suites with colour correction, MIDAS F-16 analogue routing stations, MIDI stations with analogue and digital synthesizers, and a cinema mixing suite with 7.1 JBL monitoring and surround panner. Madrid campus: Solid State Logic 4000G+ console and a RAVEN MTX II Slate Digital console (SAE claims to be the only school in Europe with it). Official certification partners: Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Cubase, Ableton Live, Wwise, Autodesk, Adobe.
programs.reputationSignals: SAE is a large, long-established international audio-school chain with genuinely serious studio infrastructure — the equipment list is among the best in this slice. Positive signal: SAE Barcelona's undergraduate degree is officially recognised by the Generalitat and AQU, which shows the institution can meet Spanish quality standards. RED FLAGS: no published price for the master anywhere; a 25-ECTS award marketed as a 'máster'; the UDIMA título propio branding is easy to mistake for an official university degree; and a heavy discount architecture that is essentially inaccessible to non-EU students.
programs.recommendation: The best CRAFT fit in Spain for his stated goal — this is literally an electronic-music-production master taught on Ableton and hardware synths, with no music degree required and his software-engineering BSc accepted outright. But three things make me cautious. First, it is a 25-ECTS título propio, not an official master: he must not be sold it as a Spanish degree. Second, the price is not published anywhere, which for a budget-sensitive self-payer is a serious governance problem — get it in writing before engaging. Third, it is taught in SPANISH and he has none, so he would need a year of language work before October 2027. My verdict: pursue it as a strong second option behind Berklee, but treat the unpublished fee and the visa question as blockers to clear in writing first.

At 60 ECTS it is at least the right size for a master-level award, unlike SAE's 25-ECTS electronic-music master, but the legal status is the same: it is a school/private-university diploma, not an official Spanish degree.

programs.tuitionTotal: €5,900 (single payment) or €6,100 (instalments) for the whole 9-month programme. No separate non-EU rate is published — non-EU students pay the same.
programs.otherFees: The €1,200 'matrícula' (enrolment) is charged on top of tuition and is included in both totals above. No other application, materials or exam fees are published. Whether the €1,200 is refundable is UNVERIFIED.

Total first-year outlay realistically €18,000–€22,000 including living expenses. This is one of the cheapest master-branded options in the slice.
programs.paymentPlans: Two published options: single payment (€1,200 + €4,700) or 10 monthly instalments of €490 after the €1,200 enrolment. No interest is mentioned. No early-bird, alumni or referral discount is published. International students without a Spanish bank account are told to contact admissions for alternative payment arrangements — arrange this before committing.
programs.scholarships: None published. No bursary, fee waiver or non-EU award is advertised.
programs.facilities: In-person only at Calle Pilar de Zaragoza 63, Madrid. Access to Ableton Live, Logic Pro, FL Studio and Reaper; a virtual learning platform; exclusive masterclasses with professional producers; and substantial software discounts (50% Ableton Live Suite, 30–50% plugins).
programs.reputationSignals: DJP is an established Madrid DJ/production school that has also launched an internationally-validated HND in music production, which suggests some quality-assurance discipline. The UDIMA partnership gives a paper trail. RED FLAGS: UDIMA itself labels the associated programme 'sin carácter oficial'; the evening-only schedule undermines any visa story; and the ECTS-to-contact-hours ratio (60 ECTS from Mon–Thu 19:00–21:30 over 9 months) looks generous relative to actual teaching time.
programs.recommendation: Cheap, DJ/producer-relevant, and open to exactly his profile — on content-per-euro it is arguably the best value in this slice. But I would not build an immigration plan on it: the evening-only schedule makes it a weak student-visa vehicle, and the qualification is explicitly non-official. My candid verdict: excellent as a skills purchase if he is already legally in Spain, poor as a route INTO Spain. If he wants both craft and residency he should choose a full-time programme instead. Ask admissions, in writing, one question: 'Does enrolment on this programme support a Spanish student visa for a Tunisian national?' — and act on the answer.

programs.reputationSignals: TAI is a long-established and visible Madrid arts school with a broad performing-arts offer. RED FLAGS: tuition not published anywhere; a €1,440 surcharge applied specifically to non-EU applicants; 'Título Propio' status combined with the name 'Escuela Universitaria', which invites exactly the misreading this candidate must avoid; and an unquantified scholarship claim.

programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED. No duration in months or hours and no ECTS is published on the sources read.

programs.program: Postgrado en Producción Musical y Artística (with Warner Music Spain) — NOT A FULL MASTER

programs.institutionType: Private university postgraduate school with a major-label industry partner

programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. It is a título propio issued by UFV (a private university) — not a Máster Universitario Oficial, not ANECA-verified, no EHEA official status, no PhD access. And it is not sold as a master: UFV correctly calls it a 'Postgrado'. Credit where due — this is more honest naming than several competitors in this slice.
programs.visaEligible: NO / EFFECTIVELY UNUSABLE FOR A VISA. Three months of evening classes (Monday–Friday 18:00–20:00) will not support a Spanish student visa or residence permit for a non-EU national. Spanish student visas for stays over 90 days require substantial full-time study; a 3-month evening certificate does not qualify.
programs.focus: Music production and artistic direction, with direct exposure to Warner Music Spain professionals.
programs.whatYouStudy: Practical training in composition, editing, mixing and artistic direction, with direct collaboration opportunities with Warner Music Spain professionals. Includes Avid Pro Tools official certification at PT101 + PT110 levels and a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence.

programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — the requirement is 'prior TRAINING OR EXPERIENCE in music or sound', not a music degree. programs.tuitionTotal: €6,100 total as headlined by UFV for the whole postgrado. No separate non-EU rate is published.
programs.otherFees: €960 enrolment deposit (included in the headline total). No other application, materials or exam fees are published. The Pro Tools PT101 + PT110 certification and the Ableton Live 12 Suite perpetual licence are INCLUDED — a genuine and unusually transparent inclusion worth several hundred euros.

Crucially, the two big software costs are covered: an Avid Pro Tools official certification (PT101 + PT110) and a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence are both included in the fee. programs.totalCostEstimate: €6,100 in fees for three months, plus Madrid living costs for that period (roughly €3,000–€4,500), plus a laptop. Total around €10,000–€12,000 — but with no visa and no master-level qualification at the end.
programs.paymentPlans: A €960 enrolment deposit followed by €5,540 in tuition fees. No instalment schedule, early-bird or referral discount is published.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published for this postgrado, and nothing specific to non-EU applicants.
programs.facilities: In-person at the UFV Madrid campus, with direct collaboration with Warner Music Spain professionals — the strongest named industry partnership in this slice.
programs.reputationSignals: The Warner Music Spain partnership is a real, checkable industry link rather than vague marketing, and the inclusion of Pro Tools certification plus a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence signals a school that expects students to actually work. UFV is an established private university. Honest naming ('Postgrado', not 'Máster'). RED FLAG: the published cost components (€960 + €5,540 = €6,500) do not match the stated €6,100 total — get the real number in writing.
programs.recommendation: The best industry connection in the slice and refreshingly honest about what it is. But it is THREE MONTHS and 30 ECTS — it cannot be his primary plan. It will not get him a visa, it is not a master, and at €6,100 it costs almost as much as a full 9-month master elsewhere. My verdict: not a route to Spain. Genuinely interesting as a later add-on if he is already resident and wants a Warner-adjacent network plus Pro Tools certification. Listed here so he is not tempted by the 'Warner Music' branding into treating it as a degree.

programs.program: Diploma de Producción Musical (2 years) — NOT A MASTER, undergraduate level

programs.qualification: Microfusa's own DIPLOMA — an UNDERGRADUATE-LEVEL award, not a master and not a postgraduate qualification. Its function is to feed into Level 6 (third and final year) of a UK BA/BSc (Hons) at Solent University or the University of Winchester.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL in Spain. It is a private school diploma with no ANECA verification and no Spanish official status. Its recognised value comes from the UK progression agreements (Solent University, University of Winchester), which are genuine and checkable, but the resulting degree would be a British bachelor's, not a Spanish master. IMPORTANT FOR THIS CANDIDATE: he already holds a BSc, so studying two years towards a route into the final year of ANOTHER bachelor's degree would be a step sideways, not forward.
programs.visaEligible: LIKELY, structurally — this is a two-year, full-time, in-person programme (Monday to Friday, 5–6 hours a day) at an established school, which is the kind of programme Spanish student visas are designed for. Microfusa does not publish visa guidance in the pages read, so UNVERIFIED and must be confirmed.
programs.focus: Music production, DAW craft, songwriting, studio recording, mastering, sound design and music business — with an explicit electronic/contemporary orientation.
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1: fundamentals of digital creation — DAWs (Ableton Live, Logic Pro), music production, songwriting, production analysis and branding. Year 2: advanced studio techniques, mastering, Pro Tools, sound design and music-business fundamentals.

programs.language: Spanish (the Madrid page notes that English-language instruction costs extra).

programs.portfolioSpec: None published.

programs.deadline: No published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for an autumn 2027 start.
programs.tuitionPerYear: PER YEAR, and identical in Barcelona and Madrid: €6,375 paying in full (€300 deposit + €6,075, saving €400); €6,776 on domiciled bank instalments (€300 deposit + €1,420 first payment + 8 monthly payments of €632, quoted at 8.6% APR); or €6,897 on non-domiciled instalments (€300 deposit + three payments of €2,199 due 15 September, 15 December and 15 March). Domiciled instalments require a SPANISH BANK ACCOUNT, which a newly-arrived non-EU student will not have on day one.
programs.tuitionTotal: Two years: approximately €12,750 paying in full each year, up to approximately €13,794 on the non-domiciled instalment plan. No separate non-EU rate.
programs.otherFees: €300 reservation deposit, non-refundable after 14 days, charged each year and included in the totals above. English-language instruction costs extra at the Madrid campus (amount UNVERIFIED). Credit-cost note: the domiciled instalment plan carries an 8.6% APR — that is real interest, not a payment convenience.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED as a hard requirement. The programme runs on Ableton Live, Logic Pro and Pro Tools, so a laptop and licences should be budgeted. Industry partnerships with Steinberg, Ableton, Pioneer DJ and Avid suggest student pricing may be available.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €12,750–€13,794 in tuition across two years, plus laptop and software, plus two years of Barcelona or Madrid living costs (roughly €12,000–€15,000 per year). Realistic total two-year outlay approximately €38,000–€45,000.
programs.paymentPlans: Three clearly published options per year: lump sum €6,375 (saves €400); domiciled 8-instalment plan €6,776 at 8.6% APR requiring a Spanish bank account; non-domiciled 3-payment plan €6,897. This is the most transparent fee publication of any school in this slice — Microfusa deserves credit for it.
programs.scholarships: None published. No bursary, discount or non-EU award is advertised.

Faculty described as having 30+ years of experience. Progression agreements with Solent University and University of Winchester.
programs.reputationSignals: Microfusa is one of the longest-established and most respected specialist production/DJ schools in Spain, with real Pioneer DJ and Ableton industry links and genuine UK degree progression routes. Best-in-slice fee transparency. RED FLAG for THIS candidate specifically: it is an undergraduate-level product and would not advance someone who already holds a bachelor's degree.
programs.recommendation: Excellent school, wrong level. The craft content and the Pioneer DJ / Ableton orientation are close to what he wants, and the pricing is honestly published — but he already has a bachelor's degree, and this diploma exists to route students into the final year of a UK bachelor's. Spending two years and roughly €13,000 to end up with a qualification below the one he already holds makes no sense. Note also that the Microfusa 'Máster en Producción Musical' at €4,700 that still circulates on aggregator sites REQUIRES completion of a Microfusa diploma first, and no longer appears anywhere on Microfusa's own current course listings — treat it as discontinued unless the school confirms otherwise in writing.

Pioneer DJ industry-leading equipment. Guaranteed performance slots at Hotel Mare Nostrum pool parties, the Hard Rock Hotel rooftop, and clubs including Destino Pacha, Café Mambo and Blue Marlin. A complimentary professional media pack is included for every student.
programs.reputationSignals: Point Blank is a genuinely well-regarded electronic music school with a strong reputation in DJ and production education and real Ibiza industry access. The guaranteed club performance slots and media pack are concrete, unusual deliverables. RED FLAGS for this search: it is a short course, not education at any level; it carries no Spanish accreditation; and it cannot support a visa.
programs.recommendation: EXPLICITLY FLAGGED AS NOT A MASTER — a one or two-week intensive. But it deserves a place on his radar for a reason none of the accredited programmes offer: guaranteed performance slots at real Ibiza venues plus a professional media pack, which is exactly the kind of asset that builds a DJ's actual career. My candid verdict: it is not a route to Spain and not a qualification, but as a two-week, roughly £1,700 investment in portfolio, footage and contacts before applying to a real master's programme, it would do more for his stated ambition than several of the five-figure 'másteres' on this list. Treat it as career marketing, not education.

programs.program: MA/MSc Professional Practice in Creative Media Industries — Audio Production specialism
programs.institution: SAE Institute Amsterdam (SAE Institute Netherlands, part of the global SAE / Navitas chain)
programs.city: Amsterdam (delivered fully ONLINE — no campus attendance)
programs.qualification: UK Master's degree (MA or MSc) awarded by the University of Hertfordshire. NOT a Dutch degree, NOT NVAO-accredited. This is the only thing at a private Dutch audio institution that is genuinely a master.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT NVAO. The award is a UK degree 'developed, delivered and assessed by SAE Institute, and awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire' (site footer, 2025/6 programmes). SAE Institute Netherlands itself is only registered with CRKBO (Centraal Register Kort Beroepsonderwijs = short vocational education register) — CRKBO is a VAT/quality register for short vocational training, it is NOT a degree accreditation and confers no Dutch higher-education status. In practice: a UK-recognised master's degree, valid in the EHEA via the UK award, but with zero Dutch legal status. Institution is 'niet-bekostigd' (private, unfunded).
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — specialist audio/creative-media academy (SAE operates ~50 campuses worldwide)
programs.focus: Self-directed, project-based professional practice master. Student develops one major creative project in a chosen specialism; Audio Production is one of the available specialisms (others: Music Business, Film, Game Art, Games Programming, VFX, Web Dev, Content Creation).
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time. ECTS value UNVERIFIED (UK master's, normally 180 UK credits = 90 ECTS).
programs.entryRequirements: Three routes: (1) Bachelor degree with Honours at 2:2 or higher in a RELEVANT field PLUS 1 year work experience; (2) at least five years of professional creative-industry experience; (3) completion of SAE's PGCert Professional Development. SAE states the programme accepts applicants without a media-specific degree.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — SAE states applicants without a media-specific degree are accepted, but the published route reads 'Bachelor degree with Honours (2:2 or higher) in a relevant field, plus 1 year's work experience'. A BSc Software Engineering could plausibly be argued as relevant for games/audio programming, but the candidate has NO professional audio experience and NO work experience, so he fails the '+1 year work experience' element and the 5-year-experience route. Route 3 (SAE's own PGCert Professional Development) is the realistic entry — that is an extra paid course. Confirm directly with SAE.
programs.englishTest: IELTS accepted. Postgraduate: IELTS 6.5 overall with minimum 5.5 in each band. Alternatives listed: TOEFL 79, Cambridge C1 Advanced 176 / C2 180, Duolingo 120, PTE, LanguageCert. He has NOT taken IELTS — this must be booked well before applying.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED on the published pages. The programme is project-based, so a project proposal is likely required; confirm with admissions.
programs.auditionSpec: None published (UNVERIFIED — likely an admissions interview given the self-directed format).
programs.whatYouStudy: No fixed taught curriculum. Student negotiates a personal learning contract and produces a major self-directed creative/professional project in Audio Production, supported by weekly webinars, supervisor meetings and virtual conferences. This is a reflective/professional-practice master, NOT a hands-on studio craft course.
programs.facilities: NONE — the programme is fully online. No studio access, no console time, no Atmos room, no live-electronics lab. SAE Amsterdam's physical facilities (Audient consoles, Pro Tools, Ableton rigs, recording studios) belong to the on-campus diploma/degree programmes, not this master.
programs.equipmentRequired: Own computer and DAW required (implied by online delivery). Exact spec/licence list UNVERIFIED for the master. For SAE's on-campus courses the site says a personal laptop is 'recommended but not required' because campus workstations are provided — that does not apply to an online master.
programs.intakes: Three intakes per year: January, May and September (per SAE UK page). September 2027 intake should exist but is NOT yet published — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the September 2027 intake. Rolling admissions are typical for SAE.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No 2027 deadline published as of the pages read.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED in EUR for the Amsterdam/NL entity. The SAE UK page publishes a single total of £6,750 for the whole programme, stated as the same for domestic and international students. SAE's own Dutch fee page (Course Fees 2026/2027) does NOT list the MA/MSc at all.
programs.tuitionTotal: £6,750 total for the whole programme (SAE UK page; same rate stated for domestic and international students). EUR-denominated NL price: UNVERIFIED — request the Information Pack from SAE Amsterdam.
programs.otherFees: SAE's Dutch fee page states all programmes carry a €500 registration fee — whether this applies to the online master is UNVERIFIED. Application fee, materials fee, exam fees, insurance: UNVERIFIED. No 'comprehensive/services' fee published.
programs.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED for the master. Note that on SAE's Dutch on-campus programmes, longer instalment plans cost materially more than upfront payment (e.g. BA Audio Production Fast Track: €25,630 upfront vs €30,164 over 24 monthly instalments — a ~€4,500 penalty for paying monthly). Assume a similar structure and ask for it in writing.
programs.scholarships: 25% discount for SAE alumni and staff (SAE UK page). UK government master's loans are available in England/Wales/Scotland/NI — IRRELEVANT to a Tunisian national. No scholarship, bursary or fee waiver for non-EU/Tunisian applicants published. SAE Netherlands states explicitly: 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO.'
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately £6,750 (~€7,900 at typical rates) tuition for the whole programme, plus possible €500 registration, plus his own computer/DAW/licences and IELTS fee. This is by far the cheapest 'master' in this slice — because it is online and delivers no studio time. Living costs are NOT incurred since there is no relocation.
programs.visaEligible: NO. Two independent reasons: (1) the programme is fully online, so there is nothing to relocate for; (2) SAE Institute Netherlands states in writing on its entry-requirements page: 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO', and on its course pages: 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands.' Only an IND-recognised sponsor can apply for a Dutch student residence permit, and SAE Amsterdam does not do this.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: SAE is the largest audio-education chain in the world (founded 1976, ~50 campuses), the Amsterdam campus has real professional studios with Audient consoles and Pro Tools/Ableton, and degrees are quality-assured by a real UK university (University of Hertfordshire; Middlesex University for pre-2022 enrolments). RED FLAGS: (a) the awarding partner changed from Middlesex to Hertfordshire in 2022 — validation partnerships at SAE are not permanent; (b) the 'master' has no studio component whatsoever despite being marketed by a studio school; (c) SAE Amsterdam's inability to sponsor a visa is disclosed only in the small print of the entry-requirements page; (d) prices for on-campus programmes are very high relative to Dutch public alternatives (Quora threads flag exactly this). Notable alumni/staff for the Amsterdam campus: UNVERIFIED — the site publishes testimonials rather than named industry staff. Graduate employment outcomes: UNVERIFIED (no published stats).
programs.recommendation: DO NOT ENROL for his stated goal. He wants to become an international DJ/producer and wants hands-on craft — this master delivers zero studio hours, zero console time, zero live electronics, and no relocation to a scene. It is a reflective professional-practice wrapper designed for people who ALREADY have a creative career. He has none, and on paper he does not even meet the entry route (bachelor in a relevant field PLUS one year's work experience). It also cannot support a Dutch residence permit, so it does not get him to Amsterdam. The only scenario where it makes sense is years from now, once he already works in audio and wants a formal master's title cheaply. Skip for September 2027.

programs.durationEcts: 24 months (Fast Track) or 36 months (Standard); four semesters of taught content. ECTS: UNVERIFIED (UK credits, typically 360 UK credits = 180 ECTS for a full honours degree).
programs.entryRequirements: Minimum age 18; 'applicants must have achieved an intermediate level of education'; English at intermediate level. No music qualification required. NOTE: he already holds a BSc, so enrolling in another bachelor is a step sideways/backwards academically.

programs.whatYouStudy: Four semesters: recording studio techniques, mixing and mastering, electronic music production, live sound, audio post-production, collaborative projects, major final project. Tools taught: Pro Tools, Ableton Live, Audient consoles.
programs.facilities: Real professional studios on the Amsterdam-North campus, Audient recording consoles, Pro Tools and Ableton rigs, 'high-end powerful workstations'. The 18-month Audio Production Diploma page also references 3D audio and mastering specialisation, indicating immersive-audio facilities. Full equipment inventory and any Dolby Atmos room: UNVERIFIED — ask for a written kit list on a campus tour.
programs.equipmentRequired: A personal laptop (Mac or PC) is 'recommended but not required' — SAE states modest specifications suffice because students use high-end campus workstations. No compulsory hardware or software purchase published for this programme.
