programs.tuitionPerYear: Published as programme totals rather than annual figures (2026/2027 fee schedule). Fast Track 24 months works out at roughly €12,815/yr upfront; Standard 36 months at roughly €10,637/yr upfront. Same fee for EU and non-EU — SAE publishes no EU/non-EU distinction.
programs.tuitionTotal: 2026/2027 published fees. FAST TRACK (24 months): €25,630 upfront | €27,138 in 2 annual instalments | €28,644 in 4 semester instalments | €30,164 in 24 monthly instalments. STANDARD (36 months): €31,910 upfront | €33,794 in 3 annual | €35,678 in 6 semester | €37,580 in 36 monthly instalments. Paying monthly instead of upfront costs €4,534 (Fast Track) to €5,670 (Standard) extra.
programs.otherFees: €500 registration fee applies to all programmes (2026/2027 fee page). Application fee: none published separately. Materials/equipment fee, exam fees, insurance, comprehensive/services fee: none published — UNVERIFIED whether any exist.
programs.paymentPlans: Four published plans: upfront, annual, per semester, monthly. Instalment plans carry a substantial implicit interest/administration loading (see totals above). Early-bird, alumni or referral discounts: UNVERIFIED — none published on the fee page.
programs.scholarships: NONE published for non-EU applicants. SAE Netherlands states explicitly: 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO.' Dutch DUO loans and grants are unavailable. No Tunisian-specific or non-EU bursary found.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Fast Track, first year, self-pay: roughly €13,300–€15,600 tuition depending on plan, plus €500 registration, plus IELTS (~€250), plus his own laptop if he wants to work at home, plus Amsterdam living costs of roughly €14,000–€18,000/yr (IND's own means-of-support threshold is over €1,100/month and Amsterdam rents are far above that). Realistic first-year outlay if he could actually go: €28,000–€35,000. FULL PROGRAMME tuition alone: €25,630–€30,164 (Fast Track) or €31,910–€37,580 (Standard).
programs.visaEligible: NO. SAE Institute Netherlands states in writing: 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO' and 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands.' Non-EU/EEA applicants must already hold a valid Netherlands visa covering the entire course duration BEFORE enrolment. SAE Amsterdam is not acting as an IND recognised sponsor. For a Tunisian national with no other route to Dutch residence, this programme is effectively unreachable.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: real UK degree via University of Hertfordshire; genuine professional studios; global brand with 50 years of history; graduates work across the industry. RED FLAGS: (a) no visa sponsorship — disclosed only in fine print; (b) very expensive relative to what a Dutch public HBO would charge even at non-EU rates; (c) awarding-university partner changed in 2022; (d) public scepticism about value for money is easy to find (Quora threads on exactly this programme); (e) no published graduate-outcome statistics; (f) no named star faculty on the Amsterdam pages.
programs.recommendation: NOT VIABLE for him, and it would be a mistake even if it were. Two hard blockers: he cannot get a residence permit through SAE, and it is a second bachelor when he already holds a BSc — he would be paying €25k–€37k to move DOWN a level. If he is set on SAE-style training, the honest comparison is that the Conservatorium van Amsterdam's AEMA associate degree (public, English-taught, electronic-music focused, and CAN sponsor a visa) does the same job for a fraction of the price. Cross this off.

programs.program: Advanced Diploma in Music Production & Sound Engineering — Full-time (1 year)
programs.institution: Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam (ARI Education NL — franchise of Abbey Road Studios, London / Universal Music)
programs.city: Amsterdam (Atlantisplein 1, 1093 NE — inside the Q-Factory music-makers centre)
programs.qualification: Advanced Diploma — the institute's OWN qualification. NOT a master, NOT a bachelor, NOT NVAO-accredited, NOT awarded by any university. The institute states plainly: 'the Advanced Diploma is not a 3 year degree programme'.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT NVAO-ACCREDITED. The only registration published is CRKBO — the institute states it 'is registered as short vocational education (CRKBO) in the Netherlands'. CRKBO is a VAT-exemption and quality register for short vocational training; it is NOT higher-education accreditation and gives the diploma no legal status as a Dutch degree. Institution is 'niet-bekostigd' (private/unfunded) — explicitly not eligible for Dutch student loans.
programs.institutionType: International chain campus / specialist audio academy — franchise of the Abbey Road Institute network under Abbey Road Studios (Universal Music Group)
programs.focus: Intensive hands-on music production and sound engineering: studio recording, production technique, mixing, artist relations, industry practice.
programs.durationEcts: 12 months full-time, 48 weeks of tuition. NO ECTS — not a credit-bearing higher-education programme. Timetable: Mon–Thu 10:00–14:00 classroom; Fri workshops; flexible practical studio access Mon–Sat; expected 40 hrs/week total including 20 hrs self-study.
programs.entryRequirements: Music portfolio of 4–8 productions (MP3/WAV) demonstrating different roles (performer, producer, engineer, writer) with your role clearly described per track; academic qualifications documentation; music qualifications OR a motivation letter detailing music knowledge and experience; motivation letter; CV; copy of photographic passport; €200 application fee. No minimum age and no specific prior education is mandated — 'applicants from diverse backgrounds and experience levels' are welcomed.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree is required. Published wording accepts 'music qualifications OR a motivation letter detailing your music knowledge and experience level', and no prior education qualifications are mandated. HOWEVER the 4–8 track portfolio is a HARD requirement and he does not yet have it. This is the single most demanding portfolio requirement in this slice.
programs.englishTest: 'Demonstrated competence in English (for non-English speaking countries)'. No IELTS band published — UNVERIFIED whether a formal test score is required or whether an interview suffices. Worth asking, as it could save him the IELTS fee.
programs.portfolioSpec: EXACT published requirement: 4 to 8 productions in MP3 or WAV format, which must 'demonstrate different roles, such as performer, producer, engineer, writer', with the applicant clearly describing their specific role in each track. This is the requirement to start building now if he pursues Abbey Road anywhere in the network.
programs.auditionSpec: No formal audition or interview is explicitly required. Applicants unsure of eligibility are invited to contact the institute.
programs.whatYouStudy: Hands-on, industry-developed curriculum in music production and sound engineering delivered in bespoke studio spaces with integrated classrooms. Named module list is NOT published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; request the full syllabus.
programs.facilities: Bespoke studio spaces with integrated classrooms inside Q-Factory, described as 'top-of-the-range, industry-standard equipment in professional studios'. Flexible practical studio access Monday to Saturday — this is unusually generous and is the programme's main selling point. Detailed console/monitor/outboard inventory and any Dolby Atmos room: UNVERIFIED — demand a written kit list.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — no compulsory laptop, software licence or hardware purchase is published. Confirm before budgeting.
programs.intakes: One full-time intake per year, starting October (not September). Published: 5 October 2026. A comparable October 2027 start is expected — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — applications appear to be rolling until the deadline.
programs.deadline: 5 September 2026 for the 5 October 2026 intake — i.e. roughly one month before start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for the 2027 intake; expect an early-September 2027 deadline.
programs.tuitionPerYear: The 1-year full-time programme total IS the annual fee. €18,860 (upfront) to €20,160 (monthly plan). Same for EU and non-EU — no differential published. Fees quoted are current on the institute's fees page.
programs.tuitionTotal: Three published plans, whole programme: PLAN A monthly — €20,160 (12 × €1,680); PLAN B per term — €19,380 (3 × €6,460, terms of 16 weeks); PLAN C upfront — €18,860 single payment. Paying monthly costs €1,300 more than paying upfront.
programs.otherFees: €200 application fee — REFUNDED if the applicant does not complete the admission process successfully. No enrolment/matriculation fee, materials fee, exam fee, insurance or comprehensive/services fee is published — UNVERIFIED whether any exist. Payment to ARI Education NL, IBAN NL12 RABO 0158 1674 57, BIC RABONL2U.
programs.paymentPlans: Three plans as above (monthly / termly / upfront). NO early-bird, alumni, referral or sibling discount is published. The only 'discount' available is the €1,300 saving from paying upfront.
programs.scholarships: NONE published — no scholarship, bursary or fee waiver of any kind for non-EU or Tunisian applicants. Not eligible for Dutch undergraduate student loans (the institute states the course is 'not eligible for any kind of student loan' as it is not a 3-year degree). The only financial relief mentioned is a Dutch INCOME TAX deduction on study costs — which requires Dutch taxable income and explicitly 'does not apply to those receiving governmental benefits or who aren't yet employed', so it is worthless to a new international student. The institute also warns the rules changed in 2022 and it cannot guarantee eligibility.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €19,060–€20,360 for the year (tuition + €200 application fee), plus Amsterdam living costs of roughly €14,000–€18,000, plus flights. Realistic first-year outlay if attendance were possible: €33,000–€39,000 — for a non-accredited private diploma.
programs.visaEligible: NO — explicitly and in writing. The institute's FAQ states: 'Currently, we are not able to assist non-EU residents with their visa application to study in the Netherlands.' Elsewhere: 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a VISA or a student loan.' It adds that applicants may still study there 'if you have a personal means of obtaining a VISA, for example, a family connection or registration at a university.' Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is NOT an IND recognised sponsor and cannot host a student residence permit. For a Tunisian national with no other Dutch residence route, this programme is unreachable.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: the Abbey Road brand is the strongest in the industry; genuine link to Abbey Road Studios London and to Universal Music; located inside Q-Factory, a real working music hub; industry-practitioner teaching staff; unusually generous six-day-a-week studio access; a real portfolio-based selection process, which means cohorts are self-selecting and serious. RED FLAGS: (a) NOT NVAO-accredited and NOT a degree — you pay near-degree money for a private certificate; (b) cannot sponsor a visa, and this is buried in an FAQ rather than stated on the fees or course pages; (c) no named teaching staff, no named alumni and no graduate-employment statistics published anywhere on the site; (d) no accreditation statement at all on the course or home pages; (e) the only 'funding' offered is a Dutch tax deduction that by the institute's own admission does not apply to people who are not yet employed — that is close to misleading for the international audience the page addresses; (f) the fee pages have a history of being out of date (a €16,400 figure from a 2022 update was still circulating). No formal published complaints or regulatory actions were found.
programs.recommendation: OUTSTANDING SCHOOL, WRONG COUNTRY, AND NOT A MASTER. On craft, this is the best hands-on music production and sound engineering training in this entire Dutch slice — real studios, six days a week, Abbey Road pedigree, and a portfolio-selected cohort. But three things kill it for him: it CANNOT get him a Dutch residence permit (stated in writing), it is NOT a master or any accredited degree, and at €19,000–€20,400 tuition plus roughly €16,000 living costs it is one of the most expensive options here for the least formal recognition. He also does not currently have the required 4–8 track portfolio. MY ADVICE: do not apply to Amsterdam. If the Abbey Road brand appeals to him, look at Abbey Road Institute campuses in countries where a private school CAN sponsor a student visa — but even then, understand he would be buying training, not a qualification. The portfolio spec (4–8 tracks showing different roles) is worth adopting as his personal build target regardless of where he applies.

programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL but at the WRONG LEVEL, and OUT OF SCOPE as a private institution. Herman Brood Academie is not an independent private school — it is an academy WITHIN MBO Utrecht, a government-funded ('bekostigd') public ROC. Tuition is set by the national government ('Jaarlijks wordt de hoogte van het lesgeld vastgesteld door de Rijksoverheid'), which is the definitive marker of public funding. NVAO does not accredit MBO — MBO is regulated by the Inspectie van het Onderwijs and registered in CREBO, not NVAO/CROHO. So: publicly funded, sub-bachelor, and therefore excluded on two independent grounds.
programs.institutionType: PUBLIC — academy within a government-funded ROC (MBO Utrecht). NOT a private institution despite its distinct branding.

programs.englishTest: IELTS is IRRELEVANT here — instruction is in Dutch. He would need Dutch (typically NT2 Programma II) instead. This is a multi-year obstacle.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — artist tracks at MBO music academies normally require an audition and/or demo, but nothing is published on the pages read.

programs.program: MARKET-LEVEL FINDING — no private NVAO-accredited master in sound design or music production exists in the Netherlands
programs.institution: Netherlands private higher-education sector (systematic check across NVAO/CROHO-registered private institutions and all named specialist audio providers)
programs.qualification: NONE EXISTS. After searching in both English and Dutch ('master muziekproductie', 'opleiding sound design particulier', 'niet-bekostigde opleiding', 'master sound design Nederland particuliere hogeschool NVAO'), I found NO privately-run, NVAO-accredited master's degree in sound design, music production, audio engineering, music technology, immersive audio or electronic music performance anywhere in the Netherlands.
programs.accreditationStatus: DEFINITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING. In the Netherlands the audio/music education market splits cleanly in two, with nothing in between. (1) ACCREDITED = PUBLIC. Every NVAO-accredited master in this field belongs to a government-funded ('bekostigd') public institution: HKU Utrecht (Master of Music pathway Music Design; Sound Design and Audio Design at bachelor level), Conservatorium van Amsterdam / AHK (Master Immersive Audio — NVAO-assessed; plus the AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians, English-taught), Codarts Rotterdam, and the Institute of Sonology at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague. These are all excluded from this brief as public. (2) PRIVATE = UNACCREDITED. Every private audio provider in the country (SAE, Abbey Road Institute, Sound Education, Pro Audio Education, DDMA, Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, DJ School Amsterdam, Music Production Academy) holds at most CRKBO and/or NRTO registration. CRKBO is a short-vocational-education register that governs VAT exemption; NRTO is a private-training trade association quality mark. NEITHER IS AN ACCREDITATION AND NEITHER CONFERS DEGREE STATUS. The sole exception — SAE's MA/MSc — is a UK University of Hertfordshire award delivered fully online, with no Dutch status and no campus component. Meanwhile private institutions that DO hold NVAO accreditation (Tio, Wittenborg, Nyenrode) operate exclusively in business and hospitality.

programs.focus: Sound design, music production, electronic music production, audio engineering, recording arts, music technology, film and game audio, immersive audio, DJ and electronic performance.

programs.scholarships: SECTOR-WIDE FINDING: NOT ONE private Dutch audio provider publishes any scholarship, bursary, fee waiver or discount available to a non-EU or Tunisian applicant. The only financial mechanisms found were (a) upfront-payment savings of €1,300–€5,670 versus instalment plans, (b) alumni/staff discounts of 25% at SAE UK, (c) 35–50% student software discounts at Sound Education and AV Sound Education, and (d) a Dutch study-cost INCOME TAX deduction promoted by Abbey Road Institute and Pro Audio Education, which requires Dutch taxable income and by Abbey Road's own admission 'doesn't apply to those receiving governmental benefits or who aren't yet employed'. That last one is effectively worthless to an incoming international student and should be discounted entirely when comparing prices. Dutch DUO student finance is unavailable at every private provider without exception.
programs.totalCostEstimate: For orientation: private Dutch audio tuition ranges from €699 (SAE one-month DJ Certificate) to €37,580 (SAE BA Audio Production Standard, monthly plan). The mid-market one-year full-time option is Abbey Road Institute at €18,860–€20,160. Amsterdam living costs add roughly €14,000–€18,000 per year on top.
programs.visaEligible: THE DECISIVE FINDING FOR THIS CANDIDATE — NO. Only an IND recognised sponsor can apply for a Dutch student residence permit on a student's behalf, and the IND study register covers higher professional/university education, senior secondary vocational education (ROCs) and IB schools. NOT ONE private specialist audio provider in the Netherlands is a recognised sponsor. Both of the two credible English-language schools say so themselves, in writing: SAE Institute Netherlands states 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO' and 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands'; Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states 'Currently, we are not able to assist non-EU residents with their visa application to study in the Netherlands' and 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a VISA or a student loan', adding that applicants may only attend if they already have 'a personal means of obtaining a VISA, for example, a family connection or registration at a university'. CONCLUSION: a Tunisian national CANNOT legally relocate to the Netherlands to study at any private audio school. Verify current status yourself at https://ind.nl/en/public-register-recognised-sponsors/public-register-study (updated monthly).
programs.reputationSignals: The Dutch private audio market is small, expensive and structurally unable to serve non-EU students. The two brands worth respecting on teaching quality — SAE Institute Amsterdam and Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam — both disclose their inability to sponsor visas only in fine print (an entry-requirements sub-page and an FAQ respectively) while running international-facing marketing. That is the sector's central red flag. A second recurring red flag is nomenclature: Pro Audio Education titles its diploma 'Master Geluidstechniek' for what it concedes is MBO+/HBO- level work, and 'Master The Mix Academy' will surface in any search for a music-production master. Neither is a master's degree. A third is opacity: three providers (Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, Music Production Academy) publish no prices at all.
programs.recommendation: BOTTOM LINE FOR THE NETHERLANDS: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. There is no private NVAO-accredited master in this field in the country, and no private audio provider can sponsor his residence permit — so the two things he needs (an accredited master + a visa) are simply not purchasable from the Dutch private sector at any price. He should concentrate his accredited-master applications on the Spain/Portugal/Italy slices, or reconsider Dutch PUBLIC institutions, which are outside this brief but are the only Dutch route that actually works: the Conservatorium van Amsterdam's Master Immersive Audio (NVAO-assessed) and its English-taught AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians — where, notably, 'when you enroll in an Associate Degree course, you can apply for a visa' — and HKU's Master of Music pathway Music Design. TWO THINGS HE CAN USEFULLY DO IN THE NETHERLANDS ANYWAY, both on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and neither requiring accreditation: (1) DJ School Amsterdam's Producer Professional Course, ~€2,499 for 20 one-to-one English-language sessions plus 10 studio hours, compressible into two weeks — a direct, efficient way to build the portfolio he lacks; (2) SAE Amsterdam's one-month DJ Certificate at €699–€1,099 (confirm whether the €500 registration fee applies), ideally timed around Amsterdam Dance Event in October for scene contacts. Both are training, not qualifications — but a 4–8 track portfolio built to Abbey Road's published standard is precisely what every accredited master he applies to will ask for, and he does not have one yet. That is the highest-value use of the Netherlands for him.

Year 2 S1: Portfolio and Showreel (3) + Dissertation/Project/Internship (27). Year 2 S2: Dissertation/Project/Internship (30). Selection still rests heavily on the portfolio and interview.

UCP is a State-recognised private university awarding an official 2nd-cycle degree, which is exactly the category that supports a Portuguese D4 residence visa for study (course longer than 12 months). Acceptance letter from UCP + proof of means + accommodation is the standard file.
programs.reputationSignals: The strongest single signal in private Portuguese sound education: A3ES/DGES-recognised degree, a dedicated Sound Design specialisation (rare), a research-active school (Doutoramento em Ciência e Tecnologia das Artes sits above it), motion-capture and surround facilities, and an Erasmus Mundus programme (Digicréa) hosted in the same school. 45 places across all phases, so it is selective but not tiny. No published complaints or red flags found. Caveat: it is a film/media-arts sound school, not a club-music or DJ school — there is one 'Electronic Production' unit (5 ECTS), not an electronic-music pathway.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €7,080–€7,600 (tuition €6,570 + application €50 + enrolment €460, plus unpublished insurance/materials). Full two-year tuition + fees approx. €13,650–€14,500, EXCLUDING living costs in Porto (budget roughly €800–€1,100/month) and excluding a laptop/DAW.
programs.recommendation: STRONGEST PORTUGUESE OPTION FOR HIM — with one hard caveat. It is the only entry in this slice that is simultaneously (a) a genuine A3ES master's degree, (b) explicitly open to an engineering bachelor, (c) visa-safe, and (d) cheap by Western European private standards (€13,140 for the whole degree is less than one year at most Spanish or Dutch private schools). The caveat is language: it is taught in Portuguese, and he does not speak it. If he is willing to spend the coming year on Portuguese to roughly B2, this is arguably the best value-for-money accredited sound-design master in the four target countries. If he is not, it is unworkable and he should look at ReSound instead. Note also that it will NOT make him a DJ — it will make him a film/game sound designer with strong studio craft. He should treat the DJ ambition as something he builds in parallel, not something this degree delivers.

Portuguese State social scholarships (DGES) are not realistically open to a newly arrived non-EU student. Practical route to funding here is ReSound (Erasmus Mundus), not the domestic mestrado. Assume full self-pay.
programs.intakes: One September intake, fed by SEVEN application phases spread across the year (2026 cycle ran to a 7th phase). Multiple phases, single start.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026/27 cycle ran multiple phases across the year; the 5th phase for 2026/27 opened 18 July 2026. Expect the 2027/28 cycle to open in the first months of 2027.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published 2026/27: 5th application period 18 July – 1 September 2026; isolated curricular units 5 January 2026 – 31 March 2027. programs.facilities: Professional multitrack recording studios; specialised acoustic laboratories; cinema post-production facilities; 3D/Dolby Atmos audio system. Faculty are working producers, sound designers, researchers and artists. The department (som.ulusofona.pt) also runs the BSc Ciência e Tecnologias do Som and hosts the ReSound Erasmus Mundus master, and sits inside the FilmEU European University alliance — a genuine international network signal.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Lusófona is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited degree over 2 years, which supports a Portuguese D4 study residence visa. Lusófona operates a formal 'Estudante Internacional' admission statute and a CLAIM migrant-integration service on campus, so it is institutionally set up for non-EU students.
programs.reputationSignals: Positive: A3ES accreditation with a published reference; a dedicated sound department with Atmos and acoustic labs; membership of the FilmEU European University alliance; host of an Erasmus Mundus joint master (ReSound) — you do not get awarded an EMJM without external quality scrutiny. Neutral/negative: Lusófona is a large-volume private university with an admissions funnel of seven phases per year, which is a commercial-intake pattern rather than a selective one; the group has periodically attracted press scrutiny in Portugal over governance. Its Pós-Graduação em Produção e Tecnologia do Som appears to have been withdrawn (see separate entry), so check programme stability before committing.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €4,400–€5,400 (derived tuition €3,800–€4,565 + matrícula €350 + seguro €50 + candidatura €180 or €460), EXCLUDING living costs in Lisbon (realistically €900–€1,300/month, Lisbon is expensive) and equipment. Full-programme tuition + fees roughly €8,200–€10,000. This is one of the cheapest accredited private master's routes in the whole four-country search — but confirm the instalment count in writing.
programs.recommendation: GOOD VALUE, BUT VERIFY THE TUITION IN WRITING BEFORE GETTING EXCITED. The content is the closest fit to what he actually wants of any A3ES-accredited option — synthesis, sound design, studio practice, music computing, Max/MSP, and an evening timetable that lets him produce and gig during the day, in Lisbon, a genuinely live electronic-music city. The published fee structure implies a total cost far below any Spanish or Dutch private equivalent. Three warnings: (1) the annual tuition is not published as a single number and the two conflicting candidatura fees (€180 vs €460) suggest a fee page that is not carefully maintained — get everything in writing; (2) it is taught in Portuguese; (3) 75% of the admission decision is portfolio and interview, and he currently has no portfolio, so he needs twelve months of serious output before applying. Rank this second behind UCP Porto on prestige, first on price.

programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts
programs.institution: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (Ireland) + Universidade Lusófona (Portugal, PRIVATE) + Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (Lithuania), within the FilmEU European University alliance
programs.city: Lisbon (semester 2; semester 1 Dublin, semester 3 Vilnius, semester 4 at any partner)
programs.country: Portugal (one of three countries; the Portuguese partner is the private Universidade Lusófona)
programs.qualification: ERASMUS MUNDUS JOINT MASTER (EMJM) — 120 ECTS joint/multiple master's degree awarded by the consortium partners. A full, official 2nd-cycle degree, not a certificate.
programs.institutionType: International consortium; the Portuguese leg is a private university (Universidade Lusófona / COFAC). IADT is an Irish public institute; LMTA is a Lithuanian public academy.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL and the highest-quality signal available in this slice. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are selected and funded directly by the European Commission (project 101180273) and each partner's award is nationally accredited — Lusófona's contribution sits under A3ES, IADT under QQI/Ireland, LMTA under Lithuanian accreditation. EMJM designation is itself an external quality endorsement.
programs.focus: Sound as an artistic, cultural and technological force across media arts, immersive environments, performance and the audiovisual industries — the most internationally-facing sound master's touching Portugal.
programs.whatYouStudy: Four semesters with structured mobility: Semester 1 at IADT (Ireland); Semester 2 at Universidade Lusófona (Lisbon); Semester 3 at LMTA (Vilnius); Semester 4 master's thesis/project at any partner. Detailed per-semester module lists were not extractable from the pages read — UNVERIFIED; request the full programme handbook from the consortium. The Lisbon semester draws on Lusófona's Atmos/3D audio, multitrack studios and acoustic labs.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time, in-person, with compulsory mobility across three countries.
programs.language: English — this is the decisive difference from every other accredited option in Portugal.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, or media studies. Critically, the published wording states: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience' in areas such as sound, music, film or media. Application pack: academic transcripts, portfolio, TWO recommendation letters, proof of English proficiency. Maximum 24 places per year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CONDITIONALLY YES, and this is the exact clause he must clear. Quote: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience.' A Software Engineering BSc is a 'degree in another field', so admission turns entirely on evidencing 'relevant prior experience' in sound/music/film/media. He currently has NONE — no music degree, no conservatory training, no professional audio work. Between now and a January-2027 deadline he must manufacture that evidence: released tracks, credited sound work on short films or games, live sets, an audio software project. Without it, this is a rejection.
programs.portfolioSpec: Exactly specified, unusually clearly: maximum 3 examples of sound or media-related work; a single hyperlink to a portfolio site or a compiled file is acceptable; each piece needs a short reflective paragraph stating his role; total realistic listening/viewing time 10–15 minutes. Note the discipline this demands — three strong pieces, not a dump.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition or performance test published. Selection is on documents, portfolio and references; an interview stage is UNVERIFIED.
programs.englishTest: YES — and this is his action item. IELTS 6.0 minimum with ALL components at 6.0 or above. Equivalents accepted: TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2, LanguageCert ESOL. Tests must be within 2 years of application. Alternative: completion of an EQF Level 4+ qualification with at least one year taught in English — worth checking whether his SMU MedTech BSc, if English-taught, qualifies him for this waiver, as that would save both the fee and the sitting. He has NOT taken IELTS; on a January 2027 deadline he must book it by roughly October 2027... i.e. autumn 2026, immediately.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €7,500 per year for self-funded students (participation costs), charged as €7,500 at semester 1 and €7,500 at semester 3, per the official consortium site. Non-EU pricing is stated to be IDENTICAL to EU pricing — no partner-country surcharge, which is unusual and favourable.
programs.tuitionTotal: €15,000 total for the four-semester programme (self-funded). CONFLICT FLAG: Universidade Lusófona's own ReSound page instead quotes an average of about €2,250 per month for 30-ECTS semestral units (roughly €9,000 per semester), which does not reconcile with the consortium's €15,000 total. Treat the consortium figure (resound-ma.eu) as authoritative and get the discrepancy resolved in writing before applying.
programs.otherFees: No application fee is mentioned on the application page. Travel, accommodation and living costs are explicitly excluded and estimated by the consortium at €600–€1,000 per month. Because of the three-country mobility, he should also budget for THREE residence-permit processes (Ireland, Portugal, Lithuania) and inter-country relocation — a real, unpublished cost that could easily add €1,500–€3,000 across the two years. UNVERIFIED as a published figure.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. A capable laptop and headphones are a practical necessity for a mobility-based sound programme.
programs.paymentPlans: Self-funded tuition is split into two payments (€7,500 at semester 1, €7,500 at semester 3) rather than four. No instalment, early-bird or alumni discount published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: THE BEST SCHOLARSHIP AVAILABLE ANYWHERE IN THIS SEARCH, and it is open to him as a non-EU national. Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover FULL tuition (he pays €0) plus a stipend of €1,400 PER MONTH, which is explicitly described as contributing to travel, visa and living allowance. Over 24 months that is roughly €33,600 in stipend plus €15,000 in waived tuition — around €48,600 of value. Awarded on merit. Number of scholarships is a limited share of the maximum 24 annual places — so it is genuinely competitive, but EMJM calls typically reserve a substantial quota for Partner Country (non-EU) applicants, which is his category. This is the single item in this whole Portuguese slice that could make his plan free instead of self-funded.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake round opened in autumn 2025. Expect the round for a September 2027 start to open around October–November 2026 — i.e. within months of now. He should be monitoring resound-ma.eu from October 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The last published deadline was extended to 27 January 2026 for the 2026 entry; applications for 2026 are now closed. Expect a comparable late-January 2027 deadline for September 2027 entry. Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadlines are hard and are NOT extended for late portfolios.
programs.facilities: Lisbon semester: Lusófona's professional multitrack studios, acoustic laboratories, cinema post-production and 3D Atmos room. Dublin: IADT's media production facilities. Vilnius: LMTA. Plus the FilmEU alliance network of artists, producers and researchers across Europe.
programs.visaEligible: YES, and better than a single-country route in one respect: Erasmus Mundus students receive structured institutional support for visas at each partner, and the €1,400/month stipend comfortably satisfies proof-of-means tests. Counterpoint: three separate immigration processes in two years is administratively heavy for a Tunisian passport holder, and Ireland is outside Schengen — factor in Irish immigration (IRP) separately from the Schengen leg.
programs.reputationSignals: European Commission selection and funding; FilmEU European University alliance membership; three national accreditations; capped at 24 students a year (so genuinely small cohorts); explicit English-medium delivery. This is the most prestigious sound qualification reachable through a private Portuguese institution. No red flags found. The only structural caveat is that only ONE of four semesters is actually in Portugal, so if his goal is to establish himself in Lisbon specifically, this scatters him across three countries.
programs.totalCostEstimate: With an Erasmus Mundus scholarship: effectively €0 tuition and a net-positive €1,400/month. Without a scholarship: €15,000 tuition + roughly €14,400–€24,000 living over 24 months + relocation/permits, i.e. a realistic all-in €31,000–€42,000 over two years.
programs.recommendation: APPLY. THIS IS HIS SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE SHOT IN THE PORTUGUESE SLICE — and the only one that is taught in English and can be fully funded. The maths is decisive: an Erasmus Mundus scholarship converts a €30k+ plan into a funded one with a €1,400/month stipend, which for a budget-sensitive Tunisian self-payer is transformative. But be blunt with him about the odds and the work: 24 places, worldwide competition, and an admission clause that requires 'relevant prior experience' he does not yet have. His concrete twelve-month plan should be (1) book IELTS now and clear 6.0 in every band — or verify his BSc's English-medium waiver; (2) build the three portfolio pieces the spec asks for, at 10–15 minutes total, ideally one released track, one piece of sound-to-picture, and one audio-software/interactive piece that leverages his engineering background as a differentiator rather than a liability; (3) secure two recommenders now; (4) watch for the call opening around October 2026. If he only does one thing from this entire Portugal report, it should be this application — with UCP Porto and Lusófona's own mestrado as the paid fallbacks.

programs.program: Mestrado em Comunicação Audiovisual e Multimédia
programs.institution: IADE — Faculdade de Design, Tecnologia e Comunicação, Universidade Europeia (Grupo Universidade Europeia; international private group, formerly Laureate, now Ensinus/Global University Systems ownership lineage)
programs.qualification: MESTRADO (2nd-cycle degree, 120 ECTS) — a real degree.
programs.institutionType: International-chain private university (Universidade Europeia group). IADE is its design/technology/communication faculty.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL. A3ES registration R/A-Cr 25/2019/AL03 dated 06/04/2023, Despacho n.º 5028/2023 of 27 April 2023. Fully accredited Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree.
programs.focus: Audiovisual and multimedia communication — NOT a sound programme. Sound design appears only as one of several listed career outcomes.
programs.whatYouStudy: Digital Animation Lab; Living Lab I — Digital Journalism; Audiovisual Projects & New Formats; Web Lab; Living Lab II — Infographics & Information Visualization; Transmedia Project; Artificial Intelligence for Future Scenarios. Students have access to an 'estúdio de som e imagem'. NO dedicated sound-engineering, mixing, mastering or electronic-music modules are published — this is the key disqualifier for his goals.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (30 ECTS per semester).
programs.language: Portuguese. An English option exists for some IADE programmes but is UNVERIFIED for this one.
programs.entryRequirements: Not detailed on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. IADE accepts applications year-round subject to available places.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Almost certainly yes — it is a communication/multimedia master with no music prerequisite, and IADE's admissions are open-access in character (rolling applications, no published selective criteria). But this cuts both ways: low barrier signals low selectivity. Exact wording UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published for this programme — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: None published. UNVERIFIED whether an interview is held.
programs.englishTest: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Programme is Portuguese-medium so IELTS is unlikely to be the relevant test; Portuguese proficiency would be.
programs.tuitionPerYear: 2026/27 published price list: base €509.30 per month × 11 monthly instalments = €5,602.30 per year. A discounted rate of €458.30/month (10% reduction) is published alongside it, subject to limited places allocated in the master's selection process.
programs.tuitionTotal: €11,204.60 total base tuition for the 2-year master's at the 2026/27 rate (€5,602.30 × 2). With the 10% reduction: €10,082.60. NON-EU NOTE: IADE's 2026/27 price list applies a separate, higher non-EU rate ONLY to 'Creative Computing and Artificial Intelligence' (€592.60/month vs €565.60 base). Comunicação Audiovisual e Multimédia carries NO published non-EU surcharge — he would pay the same €509.30/month as a Portuguese student. programs.otherFees: 2026/27 emolumentos for Mestrados, published as a table totalling €880: Candidatura (application) €75; Matrícula (registration) €375; Inscrição (enrolment) €400; Seguro Escolar (school insurance) €30. Materials, equipment and exam fees: not itemised — UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. A design/multimedia school of this type will in practice expect a personal laptop and Adobe Creative Cloud; budget for it.
programs.paymentPlans: Tuition is billed in 11 monthly instalments per year. IMPORTANT CONDITION: payment in 11 instalments and/or the award of any scholarship REQUIRES activation of direct debit (débito direto) — which requires a Portuguese bank account, a real practical hurdle for a newly arrived non-EU student. Discounts published: Early Bird (reduced base annual tuition for first-time registrants who register in advance, amount UNVERIFIED); alumni/final-year 'special conditions' (amount UNVERIFIED, applied for the whole programme duration).
programs.scholarships: MERIT SCHOLARSHIP (Bolsa de Mérito): students with a final bachelor's average of 15.5 or above — or 16.5 or above for students from FOREIGN institutions — receive a 40% reduction on the base tuition fee, renewed annually provided the average is maintained. This is directly usable by him IF his SMU MedTech GPA converts to 16.5+/20 on the Portuguese scale, which is a high bar (roughly a strong first-class equivalent). Applied to this programme, 40% off would bring tuition to about €3,361/year, €6,723 total. IADE's fees page also mentions a 'Merit Students Programme' with reductions up to 50% for averages of 16+, and 'Bolsa Interna' and 'Bolsa de Apoio ao Estudo' categories — the published table's 10% column corresponds to one of these, subject to limited places. Portuguese State DGES social scholarships are listed but are not realistically open to a new non-EU arrival. A 10% discount for international candidates (limited places, first-come order) is referenced in IADE marketing — UNVERIFIED against the official price list.
programs.intakes: Rolling — 'candidatos podem formalizar candidatura ao longo de todo o ano' (applications accepted year-round), subject to available places. Main start is September.
programs.applicationOpens: Open year-round. No fixed opening date.
programs.deadline: No published fixed deadline — applications accepted throughout the year subject to vacancies. For a September 2027 start with a Tunisian visa file, he should still apply by roughly March–April 2027.
programs.facilities: Sound and image studio ('estúdio de som e imagem'), specialised laboratories and studios. No console, monitoring, Atmos or microphone inventory is published for the sound facilities specifically — UNVERIFIED, and notably thinner disclosure than UCP Porto or Lusófona.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Universidade Europeia/IADE is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited 2-year degree, which supports a D4 study residence visa. As an international-chain university it has established international admissions machinery.
programs.reputationSignals: Positive: A3ES accredited with a specific registration reference; IADE is a long-established and well-regarded Lisbon design school; transparent published price list (better fee disclosure than most schools in this search); a clear, quantified merit scholarship. Negative for HIS purposes: this is a communication/multimedia degree with essentially no sound curriculum — the audio content is one studio and a career-outcomes bullet. Also note the commercial signals: rolling year-round admissions, a discount architecture with at least four overlapping scholarship categories, and mandatory direct debit to access instalments or scholarships. That is a sales-led model, not a selective one.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €6,482 (tuition €5,602.30 + emolumentos €880), before laptop/software and Lisbon living costs. Two-year total tuition + fees approx. €12,085 at base rate; approx. €7,600 if he secures the 40% merit scholarship.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT PRIORITISE — WRONG SUBJECT. The accreditation is genuine, the fees are transparent and the merit scholarship is real and quantified, so it is not a bad institution. But he wants music production, mixing, sound design and electronic music, and this degree teaches digital journalism, infographics, transmedia and web labs. Paying €11,200 for a communication master that touches sound once, in a language he does not speak, would be a poor use of a budget-sensitive candidate's money. Include it only as a distant fallback if UCP, Lusófona and ReSound all fail AND he decides he wants a Portuguese accredited degree for immigration reasons more than he wants sound training. If he does pursue it, the 40% merit scholarship at 16.5+/20 is the only thing that makes the price sensible.

No red flags found. Weakness: no published graduate-outcome data, no named notable alumni or staff.

Its real use to him is as PORTFOLIO FUEL, not as a destination: the piece he is missing for UCP, Lusófona and above all ReSound is demonstrable sound work, and €2,125 of hands-on Pro Tools, microphone technique and mixing would produce it. But he could get equivalent portfolio material in Tunisia or online for far less, and the €5,000+ of Lisbon living costs to attend a non-visa-eligible certificate makes no financial sense for a budget-sensitive candidate. Verdict: skip unless he is already in Portugal for another reason.

programs.whatYouStudy: Producer I: DAW introduction, MIDI manipulation, beat construction, musical composition (scales, chords, progressions), analogue and digital synthesis, audio engineering fundamentals (compression, EQ, mixing), introduction to mastering. Producer II: advanced production processes, mixing techniques, sound design, vocal treatment, compression variations, sidechain effects, professional mastering. Plus 40 hours of professional studio access bookable online and usable up to 3 months after the course ends, 20 hours of 'LAB' Q&A sessions with instructors, four video tutorials with instructor corrections, and access to online classes from other timetables.
programs.durationEcts: 200 hours over approximately 10 months. No ECTS. Multiple weekly timetable options in both cities.
programs.language: Portuguese — UNVERIFIED whether any English-medium delivery exists.

Total realistic outlay: €2,955 upfront (€2,490 + €420 + €45) or up to roughly €3,665 on the 10-month plan. No insurance or materials fee published — UNVERIFIED.

Although the 10-month duration is longer than most courses in this slice, it is still under the 12-month threshold for a D4 study residence visa, and vocational OFP training at a non-higher-education academy is not a recognised visa-sponsoring category. ProDJ publishes nothing about visa support for non-EU students. He CANNOT move to Portugal on this.
programs.reputationSignals: Positive and genuinely relevant: DGERT certification (it claims to be the only DGERT-certified DJ/production academy in Portugal), instructors holding CCP pedagogical credentials, two campuses, included studio hours, and a syllabus squarely aimed at electronic music and DJing — which is what he actually wants. Negative: age-14 minimum and no selection whatsoever; the 'Master Producer' name invites exactly the confusion this report exists to prevent; a separate €45 charge to issue the diploma; an enrolment fee (€420–€520) that varies by payment method, which is an odd and slightly opaque practice; and instalment plans that increase the total cost without this being flagged. No independent graduate-outcome data or notable alumni published.

Plus living costs if attending in person in Lisbon or Porto (~€900–€1,300/month for 10 months = €9,000–€13,000) — which dwarfs the tuition and is unfunded and visa-less.
programs.recommendation: CLOSEST TO WHAT HE WANTS TO DO, FURTHEST FROM WHAT HE NEEDS INSTITUTIONALLY. Be direct with him: if the only goal were 'learn to produce electronic music and DJ', this is the most on-target training in Portugal, and €2,955 is not unreasonable for 200 hours plus 40 studio hours. But it is not a master's despite its name, it confers no academic credit, and critically it CANNOT get him a residence permit — so he would be paying €12,000+ including living costs to sit in Lisbon on a tourist footing with no legal study status. The rational play is the inverse: use an accredited master's (UCP Porto, Lusófona, or funded ReSound) to obtain the visa and the residence permit, and then, once legally resident, add a ProDJ or ETIC specialisation as a cheap evening top-up. Never the other way round.

But it is not a qualification, not a degree, and not a visa. Flag the enrolment-fee inconsistency (€520 vs €420) to him as a small sign of loose administration, and tell him to get the total written down before paying. Negative and significant: NO published pricing whatsoever on the Lisbon site; no accreditation in Portugal; no ECTS; the BA (Hons) route is dangled in marketing but is not obtainable in Lisbon; no visa eligibility; no equipment list; no published graduate outcomes. The pattern of an international chain advertising a UK degree pathway that is not actually available at the campus being marketed is precisely the kind of marketing framing to be sceptical of.

programs.recommendation: TREAT WITH SCEPTICISM AND DO NOT COMMIT WITHOUT A WRITTEN QUOTE. On content and probable language of delivery it is attractive: English-medium electronic music production in Lisbon, with an EP as the output and Ableton certification — arguably closer to 'international DJ/producer' than any accredited degree here. But it publishes no prices, holds no Portuguese accreditation, offers no ECTS, cannot support a visa, and advertises a BA (Hons) pathway that is not delivered at the campus he would attend. For a budget-sensitive applicant, an unpriced, unaccredited certificate from an international chain is the highest-risk item in this report. If he is curious, the correct approach is a written quotation for the 120-hour Electronic Music Producer Program including all fees, plus an explicit written statement of what he receives and whether any UK degree route is available in Lisbon. Expect the answer to the second question to be no.

programs.program: Biennio Accademico di II livello in Sound Design & Post Produzione Audio
programs.institution: Saint Louis College of Music (Saint Louis Music Center srl)
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di II livello in Sound Design — MUR-recognised AFAM second-level academic diploma (equivalent to a laurea magistrale). This is the OFFICIAL Italian award, not a private certificate and not a 'Master universitario di I/II livello'.
programs.institutionType: Private specialist music academy (Saint Louis Music Center srl). Site states it is 'la prima Istituzione di Alta Formazione Artistica Musicale in Italia autorizzata dal MUR al rilascio di diplomi accademici di I e II livello'. Listed in MUR's USTAT register of 'AFAM istituzioni autorizzate'.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL. MUR (Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca) — authorised AFAM institution, Diploma Accademico di II livello, legally equivalent to a Laurea Magistrale. In practice: valid across the EHEA, valid for doctoral/AFAM III-level entry, valid for Universitaly pre-enrolment and a type-D study visa.
programs.focus: Sound design and audio post-production for film, TV series, gaming, animation, media and advertising; audio restoration and forensic audio.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years. Credits: 120 CFA is the standard AFAM II-livello load; the page does not state the credit figure explicitly — UNVERIFIED on-page. Lessons fortnightly, concentrated in two consecutive days (compatible with part-time work).
programs.language: Italian and English (both used). NOT an English-only programme — Italian will be needed in practice.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, October. Numero chiuso: max 20 students per year.
programs.applicationOpens: Applications for academic courses open 3 February each year (international applicants: from 1 January). PRIOR CYCLE — confirm new date for 2027/28.
programs.deadline: 30 April (hard deadline for international applicants; late applications only at the Direzione's discretion subject to places). Admission tests June and September; international candidates can sit them online between January and June. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.entryRequirements: Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (or equivalent) obtained in Italy or abroad + minimum 15 years of schooling. A BSc in Software Engineering satisfies the formal requirement (16 years). Foreign degree must be submitted with certified translation + Dichiarazione di Valore from the Italian Embassy/Consulate, OR a CIMEA Diplome statement.
programs.auditionSpec: Selection is by audition/admission test for external candidates (the biennio is reserved to Saint Louis I-livello graduates or externals selected by audition). Pre-selection for the Composizione/Musica Elettronica/Musica Applicata family is by portfolio link rather than performance video. Admission tests are held over two consecutive days; content is published in the Catalogo dei Corsi. The attitudinal interview also tests English (or Italian).
programs.portfolioSpec: For Composizione / Musica Elettronica / Musica Applicata streams: 'Prepara un link contenente il Portfolio (video, audio, spartiti) dei tuoi lavori più indicativi e recenti.' No fixed number of works published. For performance streams a 4-track video (3 in ensemble) is required — not applicable to sound design.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS requirement published. Language ability (English or Italian) is checked in the attitudinal interview. Teaching is in Italian and English.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound Design (recording, construction and manipulation of sound effects for film/TV/games, Pro Tools workflow); Audio Interattivo non Lineare with Audiokinetic Wwise (implementation, events, spatialisation, non-linear mixing, game-engine integration); Campionamento audio e post produzione (custom sample-library building, mapping, modulators, envelopes); Tecnologie e tecniche del Restauro Audio (digitisation, remastering, forensic audio); Tecniche di ripresa e registrazione; Storia del Sound Design. Original projects developed jointly with Saint Louis's Composizione and Musica Applicata departments and in collaboration with RUFA and Vigamus (Rome video-game museum).
programs.facilities: Recording studios at the Rome campus (via Baccina 47 plus operational sites in via Boschetto, via Urbana, via Cimarra); Pro Tools certification pathway; Saint Louis in-house record labels that publish the best student work on international streaming platforms; Dolby Atmos short course available separately; Erasmus+ partner network since 2012. Also runs a Milan operational site (viale L. Bodio 37).
programs.tuitionPerYear: INTERNATIONAL STUDENT RATE (defined as EU non-Italian OR non-EU resident abroad at time of enrolment), Accademico II livello, per year: Very Early Bird €7,230 (15% off, admission completed + single payment by 30 April); Early Bird €7,650 (10% off, admission completed by 15 June, payable in 2 instalments June+September); Regular Upfront €7,900 (single payment by 5 September); Regular 3 instalments €8,500 (5 Sept / 5 Dec / 5 March). Note: the separate ISEE income-banded price list applies ONLY to Italian students — a Tunisian applicant pays the international rate.
programs.tuitionTotal: 2-year tuition at the international rate: €14,460 (Very Early Bird) to €17,000 (Regular 3 instalments). Rates as published on the current Iscrizioni page (2026/27 cycle) — PRIOR CYCLE for a Sept-2027 start, confirm.
programs.otherFees: Annual enrolment fee (quota annuale di iscrizione): €240 if paid by 30 May, €290 thereafter — non-refundable. Deposit (acconto) €250, deducted from the annual tuition. Annual regional 'Diritto allo studio' tax: €140 (paid to Regione Lazio via LazioDisco). One-off second-level diploma examination fee: €500. Out-of-course (fuori corso) year: €380. The admission process itself is free.
programs.equipmentRequired: Explicitly stated: 'Per i Bienni in Sound Design e Mix & Mastering, eventuali Corsi di Pro Tools aggiuntivi saranno calcolati a parte, in aggiunta ai presenti costi' — additional Pro Tools courses are billed separately; amount UNVERIFIED. A personal laptop and DAW licences are not itemised on the fee page — UNVERIFIED, budget for a Mac + Pro Tools/Logic licences.
programs.paymentPlans: Very Early Bird 15% discount (single payment by 30 April); Early Bird 10% discount (admission by 15 June, 2 instalments); Regular 3 instalments (Sept/Dec/March). Extra 8% discount for wind instruments (not applicable here).
programs.scholarships: Saint Louis publishes a 'Borse di studio, finanziamenti, agevolazioni e convenzioni' page; no specific award amount for non-EU applicants was published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. The Early Bird / Very Early Bird discounts (10–15%) are the reliably documented saving.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. As a MUR-authorised AFAM institution Saint Louis can host non-EU students: the site details the dual procedure (Universitaly/Italian diplomatic mission pre-enrolment for the type-D study visa + institutional admission), and states the acceptance letter needed for the visa is issued at the end of the admission process. Note the school warns visa procedures can be very long.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay (international, Regular Upfront): €7,900 tuition + €240–290 enrolment + €140 regional tax = approx. €8,280–8,330, before laptop/software and any extra Pro Tools course. Two-year total incl. €500 diploma exam fee and both years' enrolment/tax: approx. €16,900–17,900 tuition-and-fees, plus Rome living costs (not published).
programs.reputationSignals: MUR/AFAM authorisation (the strongest possible signal for a private Italian music school); operating since 1976; Erasmus+ participant since 2012; in-house record labels; partnership with RUFA and Vigamus for game-audio projects; visiting artists include Paolo Fresu, Vince Mendoza, Gianluca Petrella, Aaron Parks (jazz department). No published complaints found. Red flag for this candidate: heavy Italian-language component and a music-conservatory audition culture.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes: entry requires only 'il Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente)' plus 15 years of schooling — a BSc in Software Engineering qualifies on paper, and there is no stated requirement for a music degree. BUT admission is by audition/portfolio and the pre-selection expects 'i tuoi lavori più indicativi e recenti' — a candidate with no portfolio would fail selection. The site also states that candidates judged not ready for direct academic-level entry 'potranno accedere ai Corsi di livello pre-accademico' (a pre-academic year first).
programs.recommendation: STRONGEST ITALIAN OPTION IN SCOPE, but not for a September 2027 start without a year of preparation. This is the only Italian private route that gives him a genuinely OFFICIAL degree (MUR Diploma Accademico di II livello) in exactly his craft (sound design, Wwise, Pro Tools) at a price a self-payer can survive — about €8.3k a year against NABA's €22k. His software-engineering degree formally qualifies him, and the Live Electronics/Wwise/SuperCollider content plays directly to his coding background. The two real obstacles are (1) a portfolio-based audition he cannot currently pass, and (2) teaching partly in Italian. Realistic plan: build a serious sound-design portfolio during 2026, apply by 30 April 2027 for the Very Early Bird rate, and be prepared for Saint Louis to route him into a pre-academic year (which, usefully, is itself visa-valid as a Foundation Course).

programs.totalCostEstimate: Approx. €8,280–8,330 first-year outlay; approx. €16,900–17,900 total tuition and fees over two years, excluding equipment and Rome living costs.

programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally a non-music bachelor is acceptable ('diploma accademico triennale di primo livello... o equivalente'), but the audition demands three ensemble performances — effectively this course expects a playing musician. For this candidate the Sound Design or Live Electronics biennio is a far more realistic entry point than Music Production.
programs.recommendation: AVOID AS FIRST CHOICE — the ensemble-performance audition is a hard gate he cannot clear. Excellent value and a real degree, but the wrong door. If he wants Saint Louis, go through Sound Design or Live Electronics, both of which pre-select on portfolio rather than instrumental performance.

programs.reputationSignals: The most technically serious electronic-music offer among Italian private institutions found; curriculum names real tools (Max8, Kyma, Pure Data, SuperCollider, Arduino, C++) rather than marketing abstractions. Institutional MUR/AFAM authorisation.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes (any three-year degree). This is also the course whose SUBJECT MATTER most rewards a software-engineering background — SuperCollider, C++, Processing, Arduino, machine learning. Selection is still portfolio-based, so creative work must exist.
programs.recommendation: THE BEST STRATEGIC FIT IN ITALY FOR THIS SPECIFIC CANDIDATE. It is an official MUR degree, it costs roughly a third of NABA, it is in his declared field (electronic music and live performance), and uniquely it converts his existing software-engineering skill into an admissions and coursework advantage rather than a handicap. Caveats: it is oriented toward electroacoustic art music and installation rather than club/DJ culture — if his goal is strictly commercial dance-floor production this is intellectually adjacent, not identical. He must build a portfolio of electronic pieces and patches during 2026, and be ready for Italian-language teaching.

The International Postgraduate Scholarship competition awards partial first-year tuition of €2,200–€6,000 depending on programme and category; 'Non-EU (residence outside EU)' applicants to Master of Arts programmes receive UP TO €6,000. First academic year only; regional tax and thesis fee excluded. Deadline for the Oct-2026 intake was 27 May 2026; a further European postgraduate competition closed 24 July 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027 dates. Selection is portfolio-based.

programs.totalCostEstimate: First year: €22,250 tuition (regional tax included) less up to €6,000 scholarship = €16,250–€22,250, plus an unpublished application fee, thesis fee, equipment and Milan living costs (Milan is among the most expensive Italian cities). Two-year total: roughly €38,500–€44,500 in tuition alone.
programs.reputationSignals: MUR/AFAM-recognised; internationally marketed with a large non-EU cohort; part of Galileo Global Education. Course leadership/area leadership named for the sister programme (Vincenzo Cuccia, a former SAE Institute coordinator, is Media Design area leader). Red flags: the non-EU price is roughly triple the EU-banded floor and there is no income banding for non-EU students; no equipment or studio inventory is published for a course that claims sound design as a strand; several key fees (application, thesis) are simply not disclosed.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, in practice the most open door in this list. Entry needs 'Bachelor's degree/academic diploma' with no subject restriction, no audition, no music prerequisite — only a portfolio, a motivation letter and IELTS 5.0. A BSc in Software Engineering is a normal profile for a creative-technology MA.
programs.recommendation: ACADEMICALLY REACHABLE, FINANCIALLY BRUTAL, AND NOT REALLY MUSIC PRODUCTION. This is the easiest official Italian second-cycle degree for him to be admitted to — no audition, no music degree, IELTS 5.0. But at €22,250/year for a non-EU student it costs nearly three times Saint Louis for a course that is about performance and interaction design with sound as one component, not about producing records or DJing. If he applies, apply through the scholarship competition (up to €6,000, portfolio-assessed) and treat the award as decisive: without it, the two-year €44,500 bill is not defensible for someone whose stated goal is club/electronic production.

But there is no sound design or music production master here, and the one course closest to his skills is taught exclusively in Italian with mandatory in-person attendance. Only worth pursuing if he commits to learning Italian to working level and reframes his goal toward multimedia/creative-AI design. For audio specifically, his own Saint Louis partnership is the better door.

(2) Billboard Italia 'Women in Music' with Amazon Music: 50% tuition, for Electronic Music Production and Urban Music Production, women prioritised — not applicable to this candidate. UNVERIFIED at institution level — SAE publishes an Internationalization page but the pages read did not state visa sponsorship explicitly.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First year, Audio Production, lowest bracket: €8,100 tuition + €1,200 enrolment = approx. €9,300 (approx. €8,085 with the 15% early bird). Top bracket first year: approx. €16,700. Three-year total: approx. €25,500–€47,700. Note the income brackets are designed for Italian household declarations — establish in writing which bracket applies to a non-resident.
programs.reputationSignals: Global SAE brand with a 40-year audio-education history; MUR authorisation by named ministerial decree; named industry partners (Yamaha Professional Audio, BASE Milano, Amazon Music/Billboard Italia, IGDA Milan). Red flags: no master-level offer at all; Italian B2 required; non-EU scholarship eligibility unstated; published fees are for a prior cycle.

programs.recommendation: STRONG SCHOOL, WRONG LEVEL, AND ITALIAN B2 IS THE KILLER. SAE Milan is probably the most genuinely hands-on audio training in this whole list, and its Yamaha and BASE Milano relationships are real. But its top Italian award is a bachelor-level diploma he already out-ranks, it offers nothing at master level, and it demands certified Italian at B2 from international students — a year of language study before he could even apply. If he wants SAE specifically he should look at SAE campuses in countries where the delivery is in English, not Milan.

Negatives and RED FLAGS: (1) the 'Laurea Europea / Bachelor of Arts recognised in EU, UK and USA' claim is made without naming an awarding body — this is exactly the marketing pattern the accreditation check exists to catch; (2) the only concrete Italian credential is a regional attestation; (3) fees are not transparently published; (4) no AFAM status means no clear visa route.

The syllabus is the closest match in Milan to what he actually wants to do — but it is an undergraduate course for someone who already has a degree, it is taught in Italian, its 'Bachelor of Arts' claim is unsubstantiated on the pages published, and without AFAM status there is no reliable student-visa route for a non-EU national. If he ever asks about Mohole, the single question to put to them in writing is: which body awards the Bachelor of Arts, and can you sponsor a type-D study visa? Until both are answered in writing, treat this as unusable.

programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
programs.institution: Berklee College of Music – Valencia Campus (private, US chain operating in Spain)
programs.qualification: US 'Master of Music' awarded by Berklee College of Music (NECHE-accredited, USA). It is NOT one of the two Berklee Valencia masters that carry Spanish ANECA verification. In Spanish terms this is delivered by an authorised centre but the award itself is a US degree, not a 'Máster Universitario Oficial' español.
programs.institutionType: International chain campus – US private conservatory operating a Spanish campus
programs.focus: Music production, electronic music production and performance, DJing, sound design, studio and hybrid recording, interactive media (Max/MSP), music video, emerging/AI tools
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified from the programme page: core = Audio Engineering (hybrid recording), Studio Music Production, Music Video Production, Interactive Media (Max/MSP fundamentals), Electronic Music Production and Performance, Career Preparation seminar, plus three proficiency courses (Pro Tools, analog audio, music theory). Electives (min. 4 credits) include advanced mixing, DJing, live performance, sound design, synthesizer programming and AI tools. Culminating experience: proposal → development → defence. Software named: Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere.
programs.durationEcts: 3 consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer) = 1 academic year, September start. 32–33 US credits minimum (33 with internship), max 37–38. ECTS equivalence not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT an official Spanish master. Berklee Valencia is registered with the Generalitat Valenciana as a 'Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música' (centre code 46061691, Resolution no. 6844 of 8 Aug 2012). Berklee's own accreditation page lists ANECA-verified reports (2017) ONLY for the MA in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the MM in Scoring for Film, TV and Video Games, both 'implemented under affiliation with the Universitat Politècnica de València'. MPTI is not on that list. The degree is accredited in the USA by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE). Practical meaning: internationally respected US master's, but if he later needs an EHEA-official Spanish qualification (e.g. for a Spanish public-sector post or a Spanish PhD), this one would need a homologación/equivalencia process and is not automatically official in Spain.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Berklee Valencia runs a dedicated student-visa process: non-EU students apply for the Spanish 'visado de estudios' at their consulate (recommend starting ~4 months ahead), the visa is typically issued for 90 days and master's students then apply for the student residence card (TIE) within the first 30 days in Spain. This is the only entry in this slice with a documented, functioning non-EU visa pathway plus in-house support.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes on paper. Berklee's graduate eligibility page states only that applicants must have 'earned a bachelor's degree from an accredited college, conservatory, or university' — no field restriction and no stated minimum prior music training. BUT the MPTI page says the ideal candidate shows 'excellent musicality', 'facility with technology', 'success in artistic and academic settings' and 'prior accomplishment'. A software-engineering BSc is genuinely accepted; the filter is the creative portfolio, not the degree subject.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution (any field); official transcripts with credential evaluation for non-US/Canada degrees; résumé; statement of purpose; creative works; $150 application fee; interview (MPTI requires interview only, no audition). Interviews scheduled in CET.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'Creative works' submitted with the online application. Exact number of tracks, format and length not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; confirm with admissionsvalencia@berklee.edu.
programs.auditionSpec: Interview only (no audition) for MPTI. Confirmed on the graduate admissions page: audition + interview are required only for Contemporary Performance.
programs.englishTest: IELTS accepted. Berklee graduate requirement: IELTS 7.5 or higher recommended; TOEFL iBT 100 (exams before 21 Jan 2026); PTE Academic 73; Duolingo 120. Waivable if the bachelor's was taught in English. NOTE: IELTS 7.5 is a demanding target and he has not sat the test — this is the single biggest practical obstacle for this programme.
programs.intakes: One intake per year. All Valencia graduate programmes begin in September and finish in one year.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published on the deadlines page — UNVERIFIED. Berklee typically opens the graduate application in the late summer preceding the Early Action deadline.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published rounds (page does not state an entry year): Early Action — application 1 November, scholarship 15 November, decision 15 December. Regular Action — application 15 January, scholarship 1 February, decision 15 March. Extended Action — application 10 March, scholarship 10 March, decision 20 April. For a September 2027 intake expect 1 Nov 2026 / 15 Jan 2027 / 10 Mar 2027, but confirm.
programs.tuitionPerYear: $50,430 USD tuition for the whole 3-semester programme, i.e. for the single academic year, 2026–2027. Same figure for EU and non-EU — Berklee does not differentiate. Per-credit rate $1,615.
programs.tuitionTotal: $50,430 USD (2026–2027), the programme being one year long. Note: billed in USD, so he carries EUR/TND–USD exchange risk.
programs.otherFees: Application fee $150 (non-refundable, waived for Berklee alumni). Non-refundable tuition deposit $2,500 (credited to first payment). Comprehensive Fee $1,600 — mandatory, covers registration into the Spanish educational system, compulsory health insurance administration and campus services. Student Health Insurance Plan — amount varies, not fixed on the page (UNVERIFIED exact figure). Required software bundle for MPTI $800. Late payment fee $250. Late check-in fee $250. Thesis continuation fee $400 if the culminating experience is not submitted on time.
programs.equipmentRequired: Required MPTI software bundle $800 (charged by the school). Laptop listed as an indirect cost at $3,000 — page notes it 'may be waived', so it is not an absolute purchase requirement but is budgeted. Studios and labs are provided.
programs.paymentPlans: Not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. The costs page describes a deposit and a due date with a $250 late fee, implying lump-sum/semester billing rather than monthly instalments. Confirm with student accounts.
programs.scholarships: Real and substantial, and open to a Tunisian applicant. Berklee Valencia allocated over €125,000 in scholarships for 2026–27 master's entrants. Relevant awards: Berklee General Scholarship (all master's applicants, no nationality restriction, amount varies, automatic consideration); Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship — up to 50% of tuition, requires a 3-minute video or 500-word essay to scholarshipsvalencia@berklee.edu, deadline 1 February; Outstanding Women Scholarships (up to 70%) — not applicable to him; Berklee Groove Scholarship (up to 90%) — Contemporary Performance only; Alumni and Global Partner scholarships $18,000 — he qualifies for neither. Scholarship deadlines are tied to the application round (15 Nov for Early Action, 1 Feb for Regular). CACSA–Palau de les Arts is Valencian-students-only. Realistic target for him: General + Diversity, i.e. plausibly 25–50% off tuition, not guaranteed.
programs.facilities: Recording studios described as matching 'any other top professional facility', technology labs with Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools and Adobe Premiere, a scoring stage, and a dedicated DJ lab. Campus sits inside the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía complex in the Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències.
programs.reputationSignals: Strongest brand in this entire slice. NECHE-accredited US degree; member of AEC (European Association of Conservatoires); authorised by the Generalitat Valenciana; two sister programmes carry ANECA verification via UPV, which shows the institution can and does clear Spanish official-degree scrutiny. Graduate career paths explicitly listed by the school include 'artists, technologists, producers, DJs, electronic composers'. No published complaints or red flags found. Main caveat is price and the fact that MPTI itself is not the ANECA-verified one.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year direct cost ≈ $52,980 USD (tuition $50,430 + comprehensive $1,600 + MPTI software $800 + application $150), before health insurance. Adding Berklee's own indirect estimates — laptop $3,000, housing $10,000–12,000, books $300–800, local transport $300–600, personal $1,000 — the realistic all-in outlay is roughly $67,000–$71,000 USD for the single year. A 50% Diversity Scholarship would bring the direct cost to about $27,800 and the all-in to roughly $42,000–46,000.
programs.recommendation: This is the single best-matched programme in the whole international-chain slice for him, and the only one that is simultaneously a genuine master's degree, taught in English, aimed squarely at producers and DJs, and able to support a Spanish student visa. The curriculum literally lists DJing, electronic music production and performance, and it explicitly names DJs among its graduate outcomes — that is his stated goal. His software-engineering background is an asset here (Max/MSP, app development, hardware/software tool design are core), not a liability. Two hard blockers: (1) money — roughly $67k–71k all-in for one year is a very large self-pay outlay, and it is priced in dollars; (2) IELTS 7.5, which he has not yet attempted and which is a serious study target from a standing start. Do not apply without a scholarship plan: the Diversity Scholarship (up to 50%) is the realistic lever and it requires a deliberate 3-minute video by 1 February. Verdict: worth the money ONLY if he lands 40–50%+ in scholarship and spends the next 12 months building a portfolio strong enough to justify it. At full sticker price it is poor value versus the alternative of building a portfolio independently.
