programs.program: Máster en Producción de Música Electrónica
programs.institution: SAE Institute Spain – Madrid campus (SAE Institute, Navitas group – global chain)
programs.qualification: NOT an official Spanish master. Students receive a 'Diploma Profesional' issued by SAE Creative Media Education PLUS, from UDIMA (Universidad a Distancia de Madrid, a private university), either a 'Máster de Formación Permanente' worth just 25 ECTS or a 'Máster Profesional'. Both UDIMA routes are TÍTULO PROPIO — the university's own diploma — not a 'Máster Universitario Oficial'. 25 ECTS is a fraction of the 60–120 ECTS an official Spanish master carries.
programs.institutionType: International chain campus – specialist audio academy (SAE, worldwide chain owned by Navitas)
programs.focus: Electronic music production, sound design, synthesis, mixing, mastering, live electronic performance
programs.whatYouStudy: Semester 1: sound theory fundamentals, MIDI protocol, audio processing, synthesizers, samplers, voice recording, mixing in Ableton Live and Logic Pro X; assessed by 1 exam and 4 practical projects. Semester 2: advanced mixing, hardware synthesizers (Moog Sub 37, Prophet 12, Doepfer), sound design, live performance, mastering, plus music industry and artist management. DAWs: Ableton Live, Logic Pro X, FL Studio. Hardware: Moog, Roland, Akai, Elektron, Dave Smith, Doepfer. Plugins: Native Instruments, Universal Audio. Includes official Ableton Live Certification delivered by a certified official trainer.
programs.durationEcts: 8 months. Roughly 8 contact hours per week spread over 4 days, fully in person. The UDIMA 'Máster de Formación Permanente' route is 25 ECTS.
programs.language: Spanish. The course page requires demonstrated Spanish-language ability for international applicants. This is a hard barrier — no English-taught version.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. This is the classic Spanish 'título propio' trap: it is marketed as a 'Máster' but the accrediting route is UDIMA's own non-official award (Máster de Formación Permanente / Máster Profesional), not ANECA. No ANECA verification. It does not give access to a Spanish doctorate and is not automatically recognised outside SAE and UDIMA. SAE Spain's own FAQ separates its offering into 'proprietary training (private degrees without official recognition)' and the separate official Grado en Música (Barcelona only) — the masters sit in the first category.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED for this specific course, and doubtful. SAE Spain does operate a real non-EU visa support process: it issues an Admission/Acceptance Certificate containing the information needed for the visa, matriculation only begins after a favourable visa resolution, and it publishes a detailed visa page (consulate route ≥3 months ahead, or in-country route). Required documents: valid passport, SAE admission certificate, private Spanish health insurance, proof of monthly means (page still cites €537.94/month, a 2019 figure), plus for courses over 6 months a medical certificate and criminal-record check. HOWEVER this course runs only ~8 contact hours per week, which is well below the full-time intensity a Spanish 'estancia por estudios' normally requires. SAE's visa page does not state a minimum weekly hours threshold. He must get this confirmed in writing before paying anything.

SAE's own Barcelona-campus discounts are: academic excellence 60% (requires 9.0+ Bachillerato GPA or 9.0+ after year 1), unemployment/ERTE 10%, large family 10%, disability ≥33% 30%, current/former SAE student 40%, relative of a student 20%, gender-violence survivor 40%, Ukrainian refugee 100%. But the reputational signals here are mixed and the price opacity is itself a red flag — a school that will not publish a number before an advisor call is optimising for sales pressure. Broader SAE review evidence (Glassdoor, student forums, aggregator reviews) repeatedly raises: credits not transferring to other accredited institutions, disorganisation, and instructors' qualifications not matching the price. Specific complaints about the Madrid/Barcelona campuses were not found — UNVERIFIED. Note the contrast: SAE Barcelona also runs an official 'Título de Grado en Música' (Enseñanzas Artísticas Superiores), which shows SAE Spain CAN hold official accreditation — it simply has not sought it for the masters.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — impossible to state. No tuition, pre-enrolment or fee figure is published by SAE Spain for any programme. He must request a written quote before this can be compared to anything. Do not treat any third-party figure as reliable.
programs.recommendation: Content-wise this is one of the closest matches to what he says he wants — Ableton, hardware synths, sound design, live performance, DJ-adjacent, taught on real Moogs and Prophets, with an Ableton certification thrown in. Three things kill it. First, it is taught in SPANISH and requires demonstrated Spanish ability, which he does not have and cannot realistically acquire to class level by September 2027 while also preparing IELTS. Second, the award is a título propio dressed as a 'Máster' — a 25-ECTS UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente is not a master's degree in any meaningful sense and will not be recognised as one outside Spain. Third, at ~8 contact hours a week over 8 months, the student-visa case is weak and unproven. Refusing to publish a price compounds all of this. Verdict: do not commit. If he still wants it, treat it as a skills course, get the price and the visa position in writing first, and never call it a master's degree on a CV.

A software-engineering BSc far exceeds the academic bar — but the visa position makes this academic.

Against that: no NVAO accreditation, no Dutch degree status, explicit inability to support a visa, and the recurring global SAE criticisms that credits do not transfer to other accredited institutions and that teaching quality is inconsistent relative to price. Amsterdam is, however, a genuinely strong electronic-music city (ADE, a dense club and label scene).
programs.totalCostEstimate: €16,210 total for 18 months if paid upfront (registration fee included), rising to €19,040 on the monthly plan. Even setting the visa aside, €16,210–€19,040 buys an internal school diploma with no NVAO accreditation and no degree status — poor value against a real accredited master. Credit where due: the fee transparency is exemplary and shames SAE Spain. But this is not a route he can take.

But note the number: €4,910 for 8 months of electronic music production, taught in English, with no IELTS and no portfolio required, is by far the best price-to-content ratio of anything with a published fee in this entire slice. It is the benchmark he should measure Berklee's $50,430 against. If he ever holds an EU residence permit through another route, this becomes genuinely interesting. As things stand, list it as a price anchor, not a plan. Also worth knowing: the €699 one-month DJ Certificate is the cheapest branded DJ training found in the four countries.

The degree's standing comes entirely from the UK: 'developed, delivered and assessed by SAE Institute, and awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire.' (Students enrolled before 1 January 2022 were under Middlesex University.) So the award is a recognised UK bachelor's degree, but the Dutch delivery site has no Dutch higher-education status.

Non-EU students must already hold a valid visa covering the entire course before enrolling. This is the crucial trap: the degree is real, the residence permit is not available.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — SAE weighs creative potential over academic history; his BSc more than satisfies entry. But entering a bachelor's with a bachelor's already in hand is the wrong move.

programs.reputationSignals: The University of Hertfordshire validation is a genuine, verifiable quality anchor and puts this well above SAE's unvalidated diplomas. Fee transparency is excellent. Against it: no Dutch accreditation at all, no visa, the change of awarding body from Middlesex to Hertfordshire in 2022 (institutional churn), and the recurring global SAE complaints about credit transfer and value.

He already has a bachelor's; paying €25,000–€37,000 for a second one is not a rational use of the budget, and the Netherlands route is closed to him anyway because SAE cannot sponsor a residence permit. The one genuinely useful data point here is the English requirement: IELTS 6.0 with 5.5 per band. That tells him what a realistic private-school English bar looks like, versus Berklee Valencia's 7.5 — a difference that should shape how much time he budgets for test prep.

programs.program: Advanced Diploma in Music Production and Sound Engineering (full-time)

programs.institutionType: International chain campus – specialist audio academy owned by/branded with Abbey Road Studios
programs.focus: Music production and sound engineering — studio craft, recording, mixing, production
programs.whatYouStudy: Music production and sound engineering across a one-year intensive. Detailed module breakdown not captured — UNVERIFIED. The Abbey Road brand association centres on classic studio recording and engineering practice rather than club/electronic production.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time. No ECTS, no credit — it is outside the Dutch credit system.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. No NVAO accreditation. The Netherlands registration is as CRKBO-approved short vocational education under ARI Education NL B.V., which is a VAT/quality register for private training providers, NOT a higher-education accreditation. The institute is NIET-BEKOSTIGD (private, unfunded). Its own funding page states the Advanced Diploma 'is not eligible for NL undergraduate student loans' and that being short vocational education 'does not entitle study finance'. Outside the school, the qualification's value rests entirely on the Abbey Road brand, not on any academic recognition.
programs.visaEligible: NO — stated by the institute itself. From its entry-requirements page: 'Currently, we are not able to assist non-EU residents with their VISA application to study in the Netherlands.' As a private institute its students cannot access government student visas or loans; non-EU applicants must already have residence secured by some other means. For a Tunisian national this is a hard blocker.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Effectively yes on paper — the application asks for 'documentation of any academic qualifications' and either formal music credentials OR 'a written statement of your music knowledge and experience level'. There is no requirement for a music degree. BUT the portfolio requirement below is the real gate, and he does not currently have the material to meet it.
programs.entryRequirements: Music portfolio of 4–8 productions; documentation of academic qualifications; formal music credentials or a written statement of music knowledge/experience; motivation letter; CV; English competency; passport photo page; €200 application fee.
programs.portfolioSpec: Exactly as published: 4–8 productions in MP3 or WAV format, showing 'different roles, such as performer, producer, engineer, writer etc.', each with a description of your specific contribution to the track. This is the most concrete portfolio specification found in this entire slice — and it is a hard requirement he cannot currently meet. It is, however, an excellent target to build towards: 4–8 finished tracks with documented role attribution.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. Selection is on portfolio, motivation letter, CV and academic/music documentation.
programs.englishTest: English competency required for non-English speakers, but NO IELTS score or standardised test is specified on the entry-requirements page — UNVERIFIED. This is unusually lenient compared with Berklee (7.5) or SAE degrees (6.0).

programs.applicationOpens: Rolling — applications were open well ahead of the October 2026 start.
programs.deadline: No published deadline — rolling until the cohort fills. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionPerYear: 2026 fees, no EU/non-EU distinction — the same fees apply to all applicants. One-year full-time: €18,860 upfront, or €19,380 in 3 term instalments of €6,460, or €20,160 in 12 monthly instalments of €1,680.
programs.tuitionTotal: €18,860 (upfront) to €20,160 (monthly), plus the €200 application fee, for the one-year full-time Advanced Diploma. Monthly payment costs €1,300 more than upfront.
programs.otherFees: €200 application fee (refundable only if admission is incomplete). No materials, exam, insurance or equipment fees published — UNVERIFIED whether any exist.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not specified on any page read — UNVERIFIED. Given the portfolio requirement, he would need his own production setup before applying regardless.
programs.paymentPlans: Three, all published exactly: Plan A €200 + €20,160 in 12 monthly instalments of €1,680; Plan B €200 + €19,380 in 3 instalments of €6,460; Plan C €200 + €18,860 upfront. Payments to ARI Education NL, IBAN NL12 RABO 0158 1674 57. No early-bird, alumni or referral discounts published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None published — UNVERIFIED. The only financial relief mentioned is a Dutch income-tax deduction on study costs (with unused deductions carried forward to the first earning year), which is worthless to someone who will not be a Dutch taxpayer. No student loans, no study finance.
programs.facilities: Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam campus; equipment inventory not captured — UNVERIFIED. The brand connection to Abbey Road Studios is the principal draw.
programs.reputationSignals: The Abbey Road name is the strongest studio brand in the world and carries genuine weight with engineers and producers. The institute is a legitimate registered Dutch entity (ARI Education NL B.V., CRKBO-approved) with transparent pricing and a clear, professional admissions specification. The honest counterweights: no academic accreditation whatsoever, an explicit inability to help non-EU students with visas, and a €19,000–€20,000 price for a one-year non-degree diploma. No published complaints or red flags found.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €19,060–€20,360 for the year (tuition plus the €200 application fee), before living costs. Amsterdam housing is expensive and scarce; the institute publishes no living-cost estimate (UNVERIFIED). Realistic all-in for one year: comfortably over €35,000.
programs.recommendation: Blocked for him, but the portfolio spec is the single most useful thing to take from this research. The institute states outright that it 'cannot assist non-EU residents with their VISA application', which closes the Netherlands to a Tunisian applicant just as SAE Amsterdam does — note that BOTH Dutch private chains in this slice are visa-dead. On value: €19,000–€20,000 for a one-year non-accredited diploma is expensive for what it is, and it is a studio-engineering course rather than a DJ/electronic one, so it is also off-target for his goal. What he should actually take away is the entry specification: 4–8 finished productions in MP3/WAV, each documented with his exact role. That is a concrete, achievable 12-month portfolio target that would also strengthen a Berklee Valencia application. Build to that spec; apply elsewhere.

programs.program: Produzione Audio / Audio Production and Music Technologies — Diploma Accademico di Primo Livello
programs.institution: SAE Institute Milano (SAE Italia S.R.L. International Technology College — SAE / Navitas global chain)
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di PRIMO livello — a first-level (bachelor-equivalent) AFAM academic diploma, legally recognised by the Italian Ministry of University and Research. This is a genuine, official Italian qualification — but it is BACHELOR level, not a master. SAE Milano is authorised for first-level diplomas only; it is NOT authorised to award a Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello.
programs.institutionType: International chain campus – specialist audio academy operating as a legally recognised non-state AFAM institute in Italy
programs.focus: Audio production and music technologies: acoustics, recording, mixing, mastering, sound for film, live sound, game audio, immersive/spatial audio, AI in music production
programs.whatYouStudy: Three years, 180 CFA credits. Core areas per the official course page: acoustics, recording, mixing, mastering, sound for film, live performance, game audio and immersive spaces. Lab-based, project-driven, with explicit coverage of AI in music production and spatial audio systems. Career outcomes listed: recording engineer, music producer, sound designer, live sound engineer, audio programmer for games.
programs.durationEcts: 3 years, 180 CFA (the AFAM credit unit, equivalent in weight to ECTS).
programs.language: Italian. International applicants must hold certified Italian language proficiency at minimum B2 CEFR. This is a hard barrier.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — and this is the exception in the whole slice. SAE Italia is a non-state institution operating inside the national AFAM framework, ministerially authorised to award official first-level academic diplomas under Ministerial Decree 280/2017 pursuant to Art. 11 of DPR 212/2005. It appears in MUR's official list of legally recognised AFAM institutes. The authorised programmes are the Diploma Accademico in Produzione Audio and the Diploma Accademico di Primo Livello in Produzione Cinetelevisiva e Nuovi Media. An AFAM first-level diploma is equated to a three-year laurea within the Italian higher-education qualifications framework. CRUCIAL CAVEAT: this official status covers the FIRST-LEVEL diploma only. Any SAE Italy course not on that ministerial list — including the short courses below — is a purely private certificate with no legal academic value.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — a MUR-recognised AFAM institution delivering a 180-CFA three-year official diploma is exactly the kind of programme that supports an Italian study visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio, normally via the Universitaly pre-enrolment portal. SAE Italy runs an 'Internationalization: Calls and Procedures' page. However SAE Italy's own visa procedure and the Universitaly pre-enrolment route were not verified on the pages read — UNVERIFIED in specifics; confirm directly.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Not applicable in the way he needs — this is an undergraduate entry. Requirement is a high-school diploma (or foreign equivalent, translated and validated for Italy), not a bachelor's. His BSc would over-qualify him for entry to a programme that is below his current level.
programs.entryRequirements: Age 18+; high-school diploma or foreign equivalent with certified Italian or English translation validated for Italy; certified Italian at B2 CEFR for international students; aptitude interview and possible skills assessment.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio required — admission is by aptitude interview and possible skills assessment.
programs.auditionSpec: Aptitude interview ('colloquio attitudinale'), with the academic direction reserving the right to request additional skills assessments.
programs.englishTest: IELTS is NOT the relevant test. The published requirement is certified ITALIAN at B2 CEFR. English proficiency is not an entry route for the Milan campus.
programs.intakes: One per year, October. The course page currently advertises an October 2027 start — which is the correct cycle for his target.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. Non-EU applicants must in practice work backwards from Italian pre-enrolment (Universitaly) timelines, which typically run in the spring/early summer preceding an October start.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no application deadline published on the course page. Non-EU visa pre-enrolment deadlines are set nationally and are typically earlier than the school's own; confirm both.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. SAE Italy does not publish its rette on the course or course-listing pages. Confirmed structure only: the fee can be paid annually or per teaching cycle.

programs.recommendation: Officially accredited but at the wrong level and in the wrong language. This is the only SAE programme in the four countries that is a genuinely official, MUR-recognised qualification — and it is a three-year BACHELOR-equivalent that he does not need, taught entirely in Italian with a certified B2 entry requirement he does not have. Two things are worth extracting: first, it proves SAE CAN hold real accreditation when it chooses to seek it, which throws the Spanish 'másters' into unflattering relief; second, its AFAM status opens Italian regional right-to-study grants to non-EU students, the only state funding available anywhere in this slice. If he were 18 and spoke Italian this would be a serious option. He is neither. Rule out, but note that SAE Milano has NO second-level (master) authorisation at all — so there is no Italian SAE master to wait for.

programs.program: Electronic Music Production (SAE Certificate)
programs.institution: SAE Institute Milano
programs.qualification: 'SAE Certificate' — a purely private school certificate. NOT a master, NOT a Diploma Accademico, NOT AFAM-recognised. This course is NOT on SAE Italia's ministerial authorisation, which covers only Produzione Audio and Produzione Cinetelevisiva at first level.
programs.institutionType: International chain campus – specialist audio academy (SAE / Navitas)
programs.focus: Electronic music production, sound design, remixing, artistic identity, release-ready output
programs.whatYouStudy: Two 4-month cycles. First: electronic music production fundamentals — composition, programming and arranging with hardware and software, developing a personal workflow, integrating external hardware with DAWs and plugins. Second: refining artistic identity, advanced production techniques and remixing. Capstone deliverable is an EP of original productions plus a remix, mastered and publication-ready. Project-based throughout with no traditional exams. Interdisciplinary collaboration with SAE video, music-business and games students.
programs.durationEcts: 8 months (two 4-month quadrimesters). No CFA, no ECTS — carries no academic credit.
programs.language: Italian. International students must have Italian at B2 CEFR.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. A private SAE Certificate with no MIUR/AFAM recognition. It is neither a Diploma Accademico di II livello nor a Master universitario di I/II livello — it is not in the Italian academic system at all. The fact that SAE Milano holds genuine AFAM recognition for its three-year diploma makes this distinction easy to blur; do not blur it.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED and unlikely. An 8-month unaccredited private certificate is a weak basis for an Italian study visa, and it falls outside the AFAM recognition that gives the three-year diploma its standing. Do not assume a permesso di soggiorno is obtainable on this course.

programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — rolling.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published deadline.

programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED.

programs.reputationSignals: Genuinely good course design for a producer — no exams, entirely project-driven, and it ends with a finished, mastered, release-ready EP including a remix. That output is precisely what a portfolio-less applicant needs. The Ableton and Pioneer DJ partnerships are real. The red flags are the unpublished price and the fact that it sits outside the AFAM recognition that makes SAE Milano credible.

programs.recommendation: Right content, wrong language, wrong status. The syllabus is arguably the best-designed short electronic-production course found in this research — no exams, pure project work, ending in a mastered EP with an original remix, which is exactly the deliverable his empty portfolio needs. But it is taught in Italian with a certified B2 requirement, it carries no academic recognition of any kind, the price is unpublished, and it cannot be relied on for a visa. Rule out for September 2027. Note the structural lesson for him though: an 8-month project-based course whose output is a finished EP is a better portfolio-building instrument than a year of lectures — that is a criterion he should apply when choosing between any of these.

programs.program: Sound Design for Live, Studio and Interactive Media
programs.institution: ETIC – Escola de Tecnologias, Inovação e Criação (private school, Lisbon; Pearson BTEC Accredited Centre since 2016)
programs.qualification: Pearson BTEC Level 5 Professional Certification, 240 CATS credits, regulated by Ofqual under the UK Regulated Qualifications Framework. NOT a mestrado, NOT a pós-graduação, NOT a Portuguese degree. ETIC states plainly on its own page: 'ETIC is not a higher education institution.'
programs.institutionType: Private art/technology school in Portugal delivering a qualification from an international awarding body (Pearson/Edexcel) — the closest thing to an international chain qualification available in Portugal for this subject
programs.focus: Sound design for live performance, studio and interactive media — the most sound-design-specific offering found in Portugal
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound design across live, studio and interactive/games contexts, taught in computer labs with individual Apple iMac workstations and headphones. Maximum 16 students per class. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED. Students may apply for international internships through Erasmus+ on completion, subject to performance.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (optional 3rd year). 240 CATS credits (a UK credit unit — NOT ECTS; 240 CATS is nominally 120 ECTS but the award is a BTEC Level 5, i.e. below bachelor's).
programs.language: English — this is an international programme delivered in English. That is a significant advantage over every Spanish- and Italian-language option in this slice.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT a Portuguese degree. It is NOT accredited by A3ES or DGES and is NOT a 'mestrado'. Nor is it a 'pós-graduação' in the Portuguese academic sense. It is a UK Pearson BTEC Level 5 vocational qualification, Ofqual-regulated, delivered by a DGERT-certified Portuguese training provider. ETIC's own words: 'ETIC is not a higher education institution.' It describes the programmes as 'internationally recognised, enabling direct entry into the labour market as well as progression to further studies' — 'progression to further studies' is the operative phrase: a BTEC Level 5 is a stepping stone toward a bachelor's, not a postgraduate award. For someone who already holds a BSc, this is a step DOWN in level.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED — the page does not specify visa sponsorship or restrictions on international students. Portuguese study visas generally require enrolment at a recognised education establishment; a DGERT-certified vocational provider outside the higher-education system is a weaker case than a university. Verify in writing before committing.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, comfortably. No degree, no music background and no formal prior qualification is required — entry is by motivation letter, optional portfolio and interview. His BSc is far above the entry bar.
programs.entryRequirements: Motivation letter outlining professional goals; portfolio/showreel (OPTIONAL — one of very few programmes in this research where the portfolio is not mandatory); attendance at an interview; recommended English level B1.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio or showreel is OPTIONAL. This is notable: with no portfolio yet built, this is one of the very few audio programmes in the four countries he could actually get into today.
programs.auditionSpec: Interview. No audition or test.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS required. The published requirement is a recommended English level of B1 — dramatically softer than Berklee Valencia's IELTS 7.5 or SAE's IELTS 6.0. No standardised test is demanded at all.
programs.intakes: One per year, September. Published cohort: September 2026 – July 2028. For a September 2027 start, PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published application deadline; class capped at 16 students, so places are limited and effectively first-come.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €5,600 per year, published, with no EU/non-EU distinction. Payable in 10 instalments of €560.
programs.tuitionTotal: €11,200 for the full 2-year programme (Year 1 €5,600 + Year 2 €5,600). By some distance the cheapest structured, published-price, English-taught sound-design programme found in any of the four countries.
programs.otherFees: No application, enrolment, materials or exam fees published — UNVERIFIED whether any exist. Ask specifically about the Pearson registration/certification fee, which BTEC centres sometimes charge separately.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated — labs provide individual Apple iMac workstations with headphones. UNVERIFIED whether students must buy software or headphones.
programs.paymentPlans: 10 monthly instalments of €560 per year, built into the standard price with no surcharge — unusually fair compared with SAE's and Abbey Road's instalment premiums. Financing available through several Portuguese banks (not accessible to a non-resident — UNVERIFIED).
programs.scholarships: None published — UNVERIFIED. Erasmus+ internship mobility is available after completion, subject to performance, but that is a placement scheme rather than a fee reduction.
programs.facilities: Computer labs with individual Apple iMac workstations and headphones; classes capped at 16. Full studio/equipment inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.reputationSignals: ETIC is a long-established, DGERT-certified Portuguese creative school and a Pearson BTEC Accredited Centre since 2016, which means external UK quality assurance of the qualification. Small class sizes (max 16) and Erasmus+ internship access are genuine positives. Transparent, low, published pricing with fair instalments. The decisive negative is level and status: not higher education, not a degree, not a master. No published complaints or red flags found. Worth stating plainly: Portugal has essentially NO international private chain campus offering master-level music production or sound design — SAE, Abbey Road, Berklee, Point Blank and dBs all have zero presence there, so this is the strongest chain-adjacent option the country offers.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €11,200 tuition across two years, plus Lisbon living costs (Lisbon is the cheapest of the four capitals in this slice but has become expensive for housing). Realistic all-in over two years, tuition plus modest living: roughly €30,000–€36,000 — though ETIC publishes no living-cost estimate (UNVERIFIED).
programs.recommendation: Cheap, English-taught and genuinely accessible — but it is a step DOWN from the degree he already holds, and that is disqualifying for his stated purpose. A Pearson BTEC Level 5 sits below bachelor's level; ETIC says outright it is not a higher education institution. Paying €11,200 and two years to obtain a sub-bachelor vocational certificate when he already has a BSc makes no sense as a qualification strategy. What makes it worth listing: it is the ONLY entry in this entire slice with (a) a published, low price, (b) English-language delivery, (c) NO IELTS requirement — B1 recommended only, and (d) an OPTIONAL portfolio. If his real constraint turns out to be that he cannot reach IELTS 7.5 or cannot build a portfolio in time for a 2027 master's, this is the fallback that would still accept him. Also flag the honest structural finding: Portugal has no international private chain master's in this field at all, so if Portugal matters to him, the search must move to private Portuguese universities (e.g. Universidade Católica Portuguesa's Som e Imagem mestrado) rather than chains.

The useful conclusion for him: the international-chain landscape at genuine master's level in these four countries is far thinner than the marketing suggests — it is essentially Berklee Valencia, and everything else is diplomas, certificates and título propio.

programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
programs.institution: Berklee College of Music — Valencia Campus
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — Valencia campus of a private US college (Berklee, Boston), legally registered in Spain as a 'Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música'.
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.M.) — a UNITED STATES degree. VERIFIED on Berklee Valencia's own accreditation page: only the MA in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the MM in Scoring for Film, TV and Video Games carry the sentence 'This program has also been implemented under affiliation with the Universitat Politècnica de València.' MPTI and Contemporary Performance are listed WITHOUT that sentence. So MPTI is NOT a Spanish Máster Universitario Oficial and NOT a Spanish título propio — it is a US master only.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL IN THE USA / NOT a Spanish official degree. Accrediting body: New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE), USA. CONFIRMED by comparison with the sister SFTV programme, whose page publishes a Spanish RUCT code (4313419) and UPV affiliation — the MPTI page publishes no RUCT code and no UPV affiliation. In practice: a genuine, respected US master's degree, but it does not appear in Spain's RUCT, so it gives no direct access to a Spanish doctorate without a separate equivalence procedure. The INSTITUTION is an officially authorised Spanish higher-education centre, which is the part that matters for the visa.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Berklee Valencia is an authorised Spanish higher-education centre delivering a full-time, on-campus, three-semester programme, which satisfies Spain's estancia-por-estudios tests under RD 1155/2024 (duration over 91 days, enrolment in at least 90% of credits, and a weekly teaching load comfortably above the 20-hours-per-week guideline). Note also that Spain's official management criteria (June 2025) confirm that BOTH títulos oficiales and títulos propios are admissible for a student authorisation — and a foreign-recognised degree taught by an authorised centre in Spain is explicitly contemplated under art. 52.1.a in fine. This is the most visa-reliable private option in this slice.
programs.focus: Music production, electronic music production and performance, DJing, audio engineering, sound design, music video, interactive media, artist/producer career development.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED four-part structure. Core Module: Audio Engineering; Studio Music Production; Music Video Production; Interactive Media; Electronic Music Production and Performance; Career Preparation; proficiencies. Elective Module: 4 credits chosen from tracks that explicitly include MIXING, DJing and SOUND DESIGN. Final Project Module: three seminars (Past/Present/Future) plus culminating experience proposal, development and public defence. Optional non-degree courses: research principles, ensembles, private instruction. Software taught includes Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools and Adobe Premiere.
programs.durationEcts: One full academic year = three consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer; summer term 6–7 weeks), plus an optional fourth internship semester. VERIFIED: minimum 32–33 credits (33–34 with internship), maximum 37–38 (38–39 with internship). US credit system, not ECTS.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September (fall start).
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD 50,430 for academic year 2026/2027, VERIFIED on the official graduate tuition page. Per-credit rate USD 1,615. Because the master is one year, this is also the whole-programme figure. Berklee charges a single rate — non-EU students pay the same.
programs.tuitionTotal: USD 50,430 total tuition for the whole programme, academic year 2026/2027. VERIFIED. Expect an increase for 2027/2028 — confirm when published.
programs.otherFees: ALL VERIFIED on the official graduate tuition page for 2026/2027: Application fee USD 150 (waived for Berklee alumni). Non-refundable tuition deposit USD 2,500 (credited toward the first payment). Comprehensive fee USD 1,600 (charged at fall enrolment; covers registration into the Spanish educational system, compulsory health insurance administration and campus services). Required software bundle USD 800 — this is the MPTI-specific figure. Student Health Insurance Plan: 'cost varies' — still UNVERIFIED as an amount. CORRECTION CONFIRMED: the Professional Recording Services fee of USD 2,990 applies ONLY to the Scoring programme and is NOT charged to MPTI. Separately, transcripts from outside the US/Canada must go through a paid third-party credential evaluation service (SpanTran or ECE, course-by-course) — cost UNVERIFIED, typically USD 150–250.
programs.equipmentRequired: Required software bundle USD 800 (MPTI rate, verified). Laptop estimated by Berklee at USD 3,000, and the page states it 'may be waived' if the student already owns a suitable machine. Studios, consoles and hardware are provided on campus.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Direct cost to the college, first year: USD 52,980 (tuition 50,430 + comprehensive fee 1,600 + software 800 + application 150), plus health insurance (amount UNVERIFIED) and credential evaluation. Adding Berklee's OWN published indirect estimates — housing USD 10,000–12,000, books USD 300–800, local transport USD 300–600, personal USD 1,000, laptop USD 3,000 — a realistic all-in first year is approximately USD 67,000–71,000, roughly EUR 62,000–66,000 at mid-2026 rates. By a wide margin the most expensive option in this slice: about 5.5x the La Salle official master and about 15x the UCAM certificate.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Supporting materials VERIFIED from the official 'How to Apply' page: statement of purpose (400–500 words), résumé/CV, ONE letter of recommendation, official transcripts (credential evaluation required for non-US/Canada institutions), English language exam if applicable, bachelor's diploma on admission, and programme-specific portfolio materials.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, conditionally. Exact published wording VERIFIED: 'Music production, technology, and innovation applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music while demonstrating technological proficiency, musical excellence in performance and/or composition, leadership, motivation, intellectual curiosity, and promise of great achievement in their area of study. Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship.' A BSc in Software Engineering is therefore explicitly admissible as the degree, but the burden shifts entirely to demonstrated musicianship. The 'technological proficiency' criterion is where his software background is a real, scoreable asset.
programs.portfolioSpec: Programme-specific portfolio materials are submitted through the online graduate application — confirmed as a required component on the How to Apply page, but the itemised contents for MPTI are NOT published anywhere on the public site. STILL UNVERIFIED; must be requested from admissionsvalencia@berklee.edu. Published selection criteria: excellent musicality, facility with technology, success in both artistic and academic settings, leadership, motivation, intellectual curiosity.
programs.auditionSpec: CORRECTION TO PRIOR DATA: the official interviews page states that ALL graduate programmes require an interview — not merely 'selected applicants'. An AUDITION is required only additionally for the Contemporary Performance (Production Concentration) programme. So for MPTI: interview required, audition not required.
programs.englishTest: CORRECTION — the prior figure was wrong. VERIFIED from Berklee's official graduate eligibility page: an English test is required only 'if English is your second language AND your undergraduate degree was earned at an institution where the language of instruction was not English.' Accepted tests: TOEFL, IELTS, Pearson Test of English Academic, and Duolingo. Recommended scores: IELTS 7.5 or higher; TOEFL 100 (for exams before 21 January 2026); PTE Academic 73; Duolingo 120 or higher. Note: Cambridge C1 is NOT listed among accepted tests, contrary to the prior data. IELTS 7.5 is a demanding band and he has not yet sat the test — this is a real planning item, not a formality. He should also check whether SMU MedTech's language of instruction exempts him entirely.

Berklee Global Partners USD 18,000 and Berklee Alumni USD 18,000 (neither applies unless SMU MedTech is a Global Partner — almost certainly not). programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL AS A DEGREE. It is a título propio / Máster de Formación Permanente issued by UCAM under its own authority. The INSTITUTION is legitimate — UCAM is a recognised Spanish private university listed in RUCT and legally entitled to issue títulos propios under art. 7 of Ley Orgánica 2/2023. But THIS AWARD is not ANECA-verified and is legally a university certificate, not an official master's degree. programs.visaEligible: HIGH RISK — probably NOT, on the verified schedule. This is the decisive finding and it corrects the prior reasoning in both directions. First, the good news: Spain's official management criteria for student authorisations (Ministerio de Inclusión, June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) state explicitly that for higher education 'existen los títulos oficiales y los títulos propios. Ambos son admisibles para la obtención de una autorización de estancia por estudios' — and universities are named as centres entitled to offer them. So being a título propio is NOT itself disqualifying, contrary to the earlier assumption. Semipresencial delivery is also permitted, provided at least 50% of the programme is taught in person. Now the bad news, which is decisive. The same criteria set a weekly teaching load of 'un mínimo de 20 horas semanales' as the general rule, with an exception for intensive or concentrated programmes only where the applicant can justify that 'al menos 12 horas son presenciales' with the remainder being assessed coursework. UCAM's own official brochure publishes the timetable: Fridays 16:30–20:30 and Saturdays 09:30–13:30 and 15:30–19:30 — a total of 12 contact hours per week, delivered at weekends, in a SEMIPRESENCIAL format meaning not all 12 are in person. That falls far below the 20-hour general rule and sits exactly at, and realistically below, the 12-in-person-hour exception floor. The 50%-in-person test is also unverified and doubtful for a weekend hybrid course. CONCLUSION: he must not assume this supports a residence permit. He must obtain written confirmation from UCAM's international office, stating the in-person percentage and weekly presencial hours, before paying anything. On the published evidence the answer is likely to be no.

programs.reputationSignals: Genuine industry partnership with Sony Music España; recognised Spanish producers on the teaching staff, with Ed Is Dead and Baghira being real names in Spanish electronic music; Steinberg Cubase certification is a concrete, verifiable, portable credential. The brochure name-checks Bizarrap, Baghira, Pablo Rous, Zef, Marz and Dani Ruiz as the model of the modern producer the course is aimed at, which is well aligned with his ambition. UCAM absorbed its older 'Máster en Ingeniería de Sonido y Producción Discográfica' into this programme, so any listing of that older master should be treated as superseded. RED FLAGS: only 12 places; the award is a certificate, not a degree; the timetable is weekend-only at 12 contact hours per week; over a third of the credits are TFM plus work placement rather than taught content; and the visa position is weak.
programs.recommendation: On paper the best value in this slice by an enormous margin — EUR 4,194.12 all-in, verified to the cent, for a 60-ECTS university-branded music production master with Sony Music España involvement, named Spanish electronic producers teaching, an included Cubase licence and Steinberg certification. His software-engineering degree is named explicitly as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, no IELTS is needed, foreign degrees are accepted without homologation, and it starts in September, matching his target. If he were already living legally in Spain, this would be the clear recommendation. But he is not, and that is where it breaks. THREE ISSUES, in order of severity. (1) THE VISA. I verified Spain's actual rules rather than assuming: títulos propios ARE admissible for a student authorisation, which is better than feared — but the binding constraint is the teaching load, and UCAM's own brochure publishes a weekend-only timetable of 12 contact hours per week in a semipresencial format. The requirement is 20 hours per week, or at minimum 12 hours that are genuinely in person for concentrated programmes, plus at least 50% in-person delivery overall. This programme sits at or below that floor. On the published evidence it likely does NOT support a student residence permit. (2) LANGUAGE. It is taught entirely in Spanish, including a 16-ECTS final project. (3) THE AWARD is a certificate, not a degree — acceptable for industry, worthless for a future PhD or any title-dependent role. VERDICT: outstanding return on euro, but probably not a relocation route. ACTION: before anything else, email UCAM's international office and ask three specific questions in writing — what percentage of the programme is delivered in person, how many presencial hours per week, and has UCAM successfully supported non-EU students onto a student visa for THIS programme. If the answers are weak, this option is worth nothing to him as a route to Europe, however cheap it is.
programs.verificationNotes: Fetched the official UCAM programme page and, critically, extracted the full text of UCAM's official downloadable brochure PDF. Also extracted and read the Spanish Ministerio de Inclusión 'Criterios de gestión sobre autorizaciones de estancia por estudios' (signed 23 June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) directly from the PDF, plus Instrucción SEM 3/2025. ALL MONEY CONFIRMED EXACTLY: EUR 3,900 tuition, EUR 235 pre-enrolment, EUR 59.12 school insurance — total EUR 4,194.12. Award confirmed as Máster de Formación Permanente (título propio), 60 ECTS, semipresencial, 12 places, Murcia. NEWLY VERIFIED AND DECISIVE: the September start; the three-cuatrimestre calendar (Sept-Dec, Jan-Apr, May-Jul); the exact class timetable of Fridays 16:30–20:30 plus Saturdays 09:30–13:30 and 15:30–19:30, i.e. 12 contact hours per week; the full module credit breakdown showing 16 ECTS TFM and 10 ECTS work placement; the verbatim entry-profile sentence naming 'Ingenierías en Telecomunicaciones e Informática'; the no-homologation provision for foreign degrees; and the full named teaching roster. VISA ANALYSIS CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the prior data implied título propio status was itself a visa problem — the official criteria say the opposite ('Ambos son admisibles'), and semipresencial study is permitted with at least 50% in-person delivery. However the verified 12-hour weekend timetable falls below the 20-hours-per-week general rule and at/below the 12-presencial-hour intensive exception, which is a stronger and better-evidenced objection than the prior speculation. Rating lowered to C on that basis despite the excellent price and content fit. STILL UNVERIFIED: in-person percentage, Spanish level required, portfolio requirement, scholarships, 2027 dates.

programs.program: Postgrado en Producción Musical y Artística (with The Music Station)
programs.institution: Universidad Francisco de Vitoria (UFV)
programs.institutionType: Private university (Catholic, private, Madrid).
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO, and specifically a 'Postgrado' of 30 ECTS lasting THREE MONTHS. VERIFIED on the official UFV page, which labels it 'Título Propio', '30 CTS', 'Duración 3 meses'. THIS IS NOT A MASTER. It is a short postgraduate certificate issued by UFV under its own authority.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. A UFV título propio at postgraduate-course level. Not ANECA-verified, not an official master, no RUCT entry, no doctoral access. At 30 ECTS it carries half the credit weight of a 60-ECTS master and one quarter of a 120-ECTS one. It should not be compared with the master's-level programmes elsewhere in this slice despite being marketed alongside them.
programs.visaEligible: NO. This is now established on the regulation rather than inferred. Spain's official management criteria for estancia por estudios (Ministerio de Inclusión, June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) require studies of at least 91 calendar days, full-time enrolment defined as at least 90% of the credits, and a weekly teaching load of 'un mínimo de 20 horas semanales', with a narrow exception for intensive or concentrated programmes only where at least 12 of those hours are delivered in person. UFV publishes the timetable as Monday to Friday, 18:00 to 20:00 — exactly 10 contact hours per week. That fails the 20-hour general rule outright AND falls below the 12-in-person-hour exception floor. The programme's four-month span (September 2026 to January 2027) does clear the 91-day minimum, but the teaching load does not clear either threshold. He should treat this as definitively NOT a relocation route, not as an open question. Its only viable use is as a paid short course taken while already legally resident in Spain on some other basis.
programs.focus: Practical music production: audio fundamentals, songwriting, pre-production, production and creative direction, post-production, mixing, mastering, industry contracts.
programs.whatYouStudy: Module 1 — audio fundamentals, music theory, songwriting, Pro Tools training (41 hours). Module 2 — pre-production techniques and workflow (22 hours). Module 3 — production processes and creative direction (32 hours). Module 4 — post-production, mixing, mastering and industry contracts (57 hours). Roughly 152 contact hours in total. Taught inside a working production facility.
programs.durationEcts: 30 ECTS over 3 months. Advertised edition runs September 2026 to January 2027, face-to-face on the Madrid campus and at The Music Station, Monday to Friday 18:00–20:00.
programs.language: Spanish (castellano). No English option. HARD BLOCKER unless his Spanish is strong.
programs.intakes: One edition per year, starting in September. The advertised edition is September 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; a September 2027 edition is not yet published.
programs.tuitionPerYear: EUR 6,100 published as the total price. DISCREPANCY CONFIRMED on the official page: UFV separately publishes 'Reserva de plaza 960 €' and 'Matrícula 5.540 €', which sum to EUR 6,500 — EUR 400 more than the EUR 6,100 headline. This inconsistency is genuinely present on UFV's own live page and he must get the correct figure in writing before paying anything.
programs.tuitionTotal: EUR 6,100 headline for the whole 30-ECTS programme (2026/2027 edition), with UFV's own internal breakdown reconciling to EUR 6,500. No separate non-EU rate is published.

programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 6,100–6,500 institutional cost for a three-month, 30-ECTS evening certificate — plus Madrid living costs, which are among the highest in Spain. On a per-credit basis this is the most expensive Spanish option in the slice at roughly EUR 203–217 per ECTS, against UCAM's EUR 65 and La Salle's EUR 199 for an OFFICIAL degree. The included perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence (around EUR 599 retail) and the Avid certification offset perhaps EUR 800–1,000 of that.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED wording: aimed at people with 'formación o experiencia previa en música o sonido que deseen profesionalizarse' — prior training or experience in music or sound who wish to turn professional. Target profile: musicians, composers, producers, sound technicians and audiovisual professionals wanting to add music production to their projects. Rolling enrolment, limited places. Notably there is no stated requirement to hold a university degree at all, which underlines that this is a professional short course rather than a postgraduate qualification.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PROBLEMATIC. The published target profile requires prior TRAINING OR EXPERIENCE in music or sound. He has neither a music qualification nor professional audio experience. Whether self-taught production work would satisfy 'experiencia previa' is UNVERIFIED — he would have to ask, and a strong portfolio would be his only lever. Note the contrast with UCAM, which names computer engineering graduates as a welcome profile, and with La Salle, which requires no music background at all.

programs.facilities: Taught inside The Music Station, a professional production facility in Madrid, with practical work alongside industry professionals from Warner Music Spain. Includes Avid Pro Tools 100-level certification (PT101 + PT110) and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence.
programs.reputationSignals: Genuine industry setting (The Music Station) and a real Warner Music Spain collaboration, plus two concrete, portable, vendor-recognised credentials — the Avid Pro Tools certification and the Ableton licence are worth having in their own right. RED FLAGS: it is marketed alongside master's programmes but is a 30-ECTS, three-month, two-hours-a-night evening certificate; UFV's own published price breakdown does not add up (EUR 6,100 headline versus EUR 6,500 in components); and there is no degree at the end of it.
programs.recommendation: AVOID for his purposes, and the reason is now legal rather than a judgement call. This is not a master — it is a 30-ECTS certificate delivered over three months of two-hour evening classes, and at 10 contact hours per week it falls below BOTH thresholds in Spain's student-authorisation criteria (20 hours per week generally, or at minimum 12 in-person hours for concentrated programmes). It therefore cannot support a student residence permit, which makes it useless as a September 2027 relocation plan regardless of its merits. Compounding that: its published entry profile expects prior music or sound training that he does not have; it is taught entirely in Spanish; it costs more per credit than La Salle's official Máster Universitario; and UFV's own page contradicts itself on the price by EUR 400. On the positive side it is a genuinely good short skills course — real facilities, Warner Music Spain professionals, and two portable certifications (Avid PT101/PT110 and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence) that he would otherwise pay for separately. The only scenario where it makes sense is as a paid upskilling course taken once he is already legally resident in Madrid on some other basis. Do not build a relocation plan around it, and if he does ever enrol, get the correct total price in writing first.
programs.verificationNotes: Fetched the official UFV programme page and cross-checked the visa position against the Spanish Ministerio de Inclusión 'Criterios de gestión sobre autorizaciones de estancia por estudios' (June 2025, RD 1155/2024), whose PDF text I extracted directly. CONFIRMED EXACTLY: Título Propio; 30 ECTS; 3 months; September 2026 to January 2027; Monday–Friday 18:00–20:00; presencial Madrid; taught in castellano; total price EUR 6,100 with reserva EUR 960 and matrícula EUR 5,540; perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence; Avid Pro Tools PT101 + PT110 certification; Warner Music Spain collaboration. programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
programs.institution: Berklee College of Music — Valencia Campus
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — Valencia campus of a private US college (Berklee, Boston). VERIFIED on the official accreditation page: Berklee Valencia is a Spanish 'Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música', 'officially recognized by Resolution of the General Director of Universities, Higher Studies and Sciences no. 6844, dated August 8, 2012.'
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.M.) — a UNITED STATES degree. VERIFIED: it is NOT a Spanish 'Máster Universitario Oficial' and NOT a Spanish título propio. Berklee's own accreditation page states verbatim: 'All Berklee degrees are accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE) in the United States' and then, separately, 'The Master of Arts in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the Master of Music in Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games are accredited in Spain, in collaboration with the Universidad Politécnica de Valencia.' MPTI is NOT in that list. Cross-check confirms it: the MPTI programme and courses pages quote credits only in the US system (32–38 credits) and carry NO ECTS figure and NO RUCT code, whereas the SFTV page states '60 ECTS' and 'RUCT código 4313419'. The absence is decisive.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL in the USA / NOT a Spanish official degree. Accrediting body: New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE), USA. VERIFIED by direct comparison of the MPTI and SFTV pages: SFTV publishes a RUCT code and ECTS, MPTI publishes neither. In practice: a genuine, respected US master's degree, but it does not appear in Spain's RUCT register of official degrees, so it does not by itself give access to a Spanish doctorate or to title-dependent public-sector posts without a separate homologación/equivalencia procedure. What matters for the visa is the INSTITUTION's authorisation, which is confirmed.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Berklee Valencia is an officially authorised Spanish higher-education centre (Resolution 6844, 8 Aug 2012, verified on the accreditation page) and enrols non-EU students full-time, on campus, for three consecutive semesters. It issues the admission letter required for the Spanish type-D student visa. This is the most visa-reliable private option in this batch.
programs.focus: Music production, electronic music production and performance, DJing, audio engineering, sound design, music video, interactive media, artist/producer career development.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module-by-module from the official courses page. Core Module: Audio Engineering (3 cr), Studio Music Production (2 cr), Music Video Production (3 cr), Interactive Media (2 cr), Electronic Music Production and Performance (3 cr), Career Preparation (1 cr), Proficiencies (0 cr). Final Project Module: three MPTI Seminars (2 cr each) plus three Culminating Experience courses (2, 2 and 4 cr). Elective Module: minimum 4 credits chosen from audio engineering, production, theory, DJing, video, interactive media or electronic music. Additional optional courses (research, rhythm studies, ensembles, private instruction) do NOT count toward the degree. Optional 4th-semester Graduate Internship. DJing is a named elective area — verified, not inferred.
programs.durationEcts: One full academic year — 'a consecutive fall, spring, and summer' (three semesters). Total Minimum Required Credits: 32, or 33 with internship. Total Maximum Allowed Credits: 37, or 38 with internship. US credit system. NO ECTS equivalence is published for MPTI — verified absence, and this is itself the accreditation signal.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September (fall start). Curriculum published for the 2026–2027 academic year.
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD 50,430 — VERIFIED on the official graduate tuition page for 2026/2027. Per-credit rate USD 1,615. Because the master is one year, this is also the whole-programme figure. Non-EU students pay the same as everyone else; Berklee publishes a single rate.
programs.tuitionTotal: USD 50,430 total tuition for the whole programme, academic year 2026/2027. VERIFIED at https://valencia.berklee.edu/tuition-fees-payment/tuition-and-related-costs-for-graduate-programs
programs.otherFees: ALL VERIFIED on the official 2026/2027 graduate tuition page: Application fee USD 150 (waived for Berklee alumni); non-refundable Tuition Deposit USD 2,500; Comprehensive Fee USD 1,600 (mandatory for all students — it covers registration into the Spanish educational system and compulsory health insurance among other services); required Software Bundle for MPTI USD 800 (purchased directly from Berklee). CORRECTION CONFIRMED: the Professional Recording Services Fee of USD 2,990 applies to the Scoring programme ONLY and is NOT charged to MPTI. Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP): students 'must accept enrollment in Berklee's Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP) or submit a waiver request' — standalone amount NOT published, UNVERIFIED (note the comprehensive fee is stated to include compulsory health insurance, so double-counting is a risk). Third-party credential evaluation of non-US transcripts is required and carries an external cost — amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: VERIFIED: required Software Bundle USD 800 for MPTI, purchased directly from Berklee. Laptop estimated at USD 3,000 in Berklee's own indirect-cost table, annotated 'may be waived' (i.e. if he already owns a suitable machine — as a software-engineering graduate he almost certainly does, so treat this as avoidable). Studios, consoles and hardware are provided on campus.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Direct cost billed by the college, all figures verified: USD 50,430 tuition + 1,600 comprehensive fee + 800 software + 150 application = USD 52,980 (the 2,500 deposit is credited against tuition, not additional). Adding Berklee's own published indirect estimates — housing USD 10,000–12,000, books USD 300–800, local transport USD 300–600, personal USD 1,000 — gives a realistic all-in first year of approximately USD 65,000–68,000 WITHOUT the laptop, or USD 68,000–71,000 with it (roughly EUR 60,000–66,000 at mid-2026 rates). Add credential evaluation and any SHIP premium. This is by far the most expensive option in this batch — roughly 12–16x the UCAM alternative.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED exact wording from the official entrance-requirements page: 'Applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music while demonstrating technological proficiency, musical excellence in performance and/or composition, leadership, motivation, intellectual curiosity, and promise of great achievement in their area of study.' Ideal candidates demonstrate: 'Excellent musicianship; Facility with technology; Success in both artistic and academic settings; A strong work ethic, including prior accomplishment; and The motivation to make massive progress in one year.' Application package (verified): online application + USD 150 fee, statement of purpose 'between 400 and 500 words' in English, résumé/CV in English, ONE letter of recommendation (from a professional, not a peer), official transcripts with third-party credential evaluation for non-US/Canada qualifications.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, conditionally. VERIFIED published wording: 'Applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music. Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship.' A BSc in Software Engineering is therefore an acceptable degree — but the entire burden shifts to demonstrated musicianship and production output. His software background maps directly onto the separately-listed criterion 'facility with technology', which is a genuine and unusual asset here.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW FULLY VERIFIED (previously marked unverified — corrected). MPTI applicants must submit: (1) a self-produced video, maximum three minutes, describing 'three projects you feel passionate about, and that you would like to develop as part of your Culminating Experience (thesis) project' — with the explicit constraint 'you should not talk about projects that you have already completed'; (2) 'Three recorded musical projects, audio or video files of your work, including a short description of your role in each project'; (3) optionally, the corresponding musical scores if available. All materials must be organised 'in one PDF document with all links properly embedded and sections clearly labeled'. This is a concrete, buildable target: three finished tracks plus a forward-looking three-minute pitch video. He can start today.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition for MPTI — auditions apply to the Contemporary Performance programme only. Selected applicants are invited to an INTERVIEW.
programs.englishTest: IELTS IS ACCEPTED, AND THE MINIMUM IS NOW VERIFIED — THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST CORRECTION IN THIS BATCH. Berklee Valencia publishes two tiers: Contemporary Performance requires Duolingo 110 / TOEFL iBT 80 (pre-Jan-2026 scale) / IELTS 6.5. ALL OTHER PROGRAMMES, INCLUDING MPTI, REQUIRE Duolingo 130 / TOEFL iBT 100 / IELTS 7.5. IELTS 7.5 is a demanding band — well above the 6.0–6.5 typical of European master's entry. He has not sat IELTS yet. This should be treated as a hard gate and planned for now: it realistically needs months of preparation, and the test must be in hand before the November 2026 / January 2027 deadlines. The requirement applies only if English is not his first language; a waiver may apply if his bachelor's was taught and examined in English — confirm his SMU MedTech medium of instruction with admissions in writing, because that waiver could remove the gate entirely.
programs.applicationOpens: Applications open in the autumn preceding entry (the Early Action deadline is 1 November). Exact 2027-entry opening date not published — UNVERIFIED.

Regular Action — application 15 January, scholarship 1 February, decisions by 15 March. Extended Action — application 10 March, scholarship 10 March, decisions by 20 April. programs.scholarships: VERIFIED against the official graduate scholarships page. Applicable to him: Berklee General Scholarship — all master's applicants, amount varies, deadline 15 Nov (early) or 1 Feb (regular). Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship — 'Up to 50 percent of the tuition', all graduate programmes, 'Up to four awardees per academic year', for 'demonstrated leadership or support for historically underrepresented or culturally diverse communities'; CORRECTION: the deadline is 1 FEBRUARY ONLY, not 15 November — so applying Early Action does not advance this one. Berklee Global Partners Scholarship USD 18,000 — only for students/alumni/faculty of Berklee Global Partner schools; he must check whether SMU MedTech is one (unlikely). NOT applicable to him: Outstanding Women Scholarships (up to 70% of tuition plus mentorship — MPTI is one of the four covered programmes, but the award is for women); Berklee Alumni Scholarship USD 18,000; Berklee Groove Scholarship (up to 90% of tuition — Contemporary Performance/Production only); CACSA–Palau de les Arts (Valencian students only, deadline 1 April). The scholarship application is submitted inside the admissions portal. The claim that entering international students are barred from institutional NEED-BASED aid is not stated on the Valencia scholarships page — UNVERIFIED there; the page only directs US citizens and permanent residents to FAFSA and gives no need-based route for international applicants, which points the same way in practice. Realistic ceiling for him: the Diversity Scholarship at up to 50%, competing for one of four awards campus-wide.
programs.paymentPlans: USD 2,500 non-refundable deposit on acceptance (verified). Instalment terms are handled on a separate 'Paying Your Tuition (Graduate Programs)' page and are not itemised on the tuition page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Campus inside the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía opera house, Valencia. Recording studios and technology labs; professional software stack taught across the curriculum (Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere).
programs.reputationSignals: Strongest global brand in contemporary music education; NECHE-accredited; landmark campus. Genuine relationship with the Spanish system is demonstrated by two sister programmes (GEMB and SFTV) carrying full Spanish accreditation through UPV. Curriculum is explicitly aimed at artists, producers, DJs and electronic composers. RED FLAGS to weigh honestly: (1) MPTI is specifically the Valencia master WITHOUT Spanish accreditation; (2) cost is an order of magnitude above the Spanish private-university alternatives; (3) the IELTS 7.5 bar and the 'high degree of musicianship' standard are both real filters, not formalities.
programs.verificationNotes: Verified across five official pages: the MPTI programme page, the MPTI courses page, the graduate tuition and related costs page (2026/2027), the graduate entrance-requirements page, the how-to-apply page, the application-deadlines page, the graduate scholarships page, and the accreditation page. CORRECTIONS APPLIED: (1) English requirement is now confirmed — IELTS 7.5 / TOEFL iBT 100 / Duolingo 130 for MPTI, previously marked UNVERIFIED and materially underestimated; (2) the portfolio spec is now fully itemised and verified (three-minute forward-looking video + three recorded projects with role descriptions + optional scores, all in one PDF with embedded links); (3) the Diversity Scholarship deadline is 1 February only, not 15 November, and is capped at four awardees per year; (4) the accreditation gap is now positively evidenced, not inferred — SFTV publishes RUCT 4313419 and 60 ECTS while MPTI publishes neither; (5) only ONE letter of recommendation is required, and the statement of purpose is 400–500 words. programs.recommendation: The best CONTENT fit in this batch for an aspiring international DJ/producer — Electronic Music Production and Performance is a required core course and DJing is a named elective area, verified in the official course list, not marketing copy. The network and the brand are real. But three hard facts must govern the decision. (1) COST: roughly USD 65,000–71,000 all-in for one year, with no need-based aid route published for international students. That is irreconcilable with 'budget-sensitive' unless he wins a large award, and the only award realistically open to him is the Diversity Scholarship at up to 50%, capped at four recipients campus-wide. (2) TWO GATES HE HAS NOT CLEARED: IELTS 7.5 — now verified, and a high band he has not yet attempted; and the published standard 'a high degree of musicianship', against which he brings no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional audio work. The portfolio spec is at least now precise and achievable: three finished, well-produced tracks with a clear account of his role in each, plus a three-minute video pitching three UNBUILT projects. Working backwards from a 1 Nov 2026 Early Action deadline, he has roughly twelve months — enough, but only if he starts now and treats it as the priority. (3) The degree is a US master, not a Spanish official title — fine for industry, a real limitation if he ever wants a Spanish PhD or a title-dependent role. VERDICT: apply, aim for Early Action for the General Scholarship and target the Diversity Scholarship at the 1 February deadline, but treat this as the aspirational option. Do not commit self-pay funds without an award of 40%+, and keep a cheaper Spanish option live in parallel.

programs.program: Master of Music in Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games (SFTV)

programs.qualification: DUAL AWARD, NOW POSITIVELY VERIFIED. A US Master of Music (M.M.) AND a Spanish official Máster Universitario. Berklee's accreditation page states: 'The Master of Arts in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the Master of Music in Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games are accredited in Spain, in collaboration with the Universidad Politécnica de Valencia.' The programme page confirms the mechanics: 'RUCT código 4313419', 60 ECTS, 'valid throughout the European Higher Education Area (EHEA)'. Cross-checked against UPV's own 2026/2027 places offer, where it appears under the official Spanish title 'Máster Universitario en Composición Musical para Cine, Televisión y Videojuegos (Scoring for Film, Television and Video Games)' with 40 official places, taught at the Berklee Valencia campus.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL IN BOTH SYSTEMS — the strongest legal standing of any programme in this batch. NECHE (USA) plus a Spanish Máster Universitario Oficial registered in RUCT under code 4313419, delivered in affiliation with Universitat Politècnica de València. In practice: 60 ECTS, valid across the EHEA, valid for PhD entry, and unambiguous for visa and title-recognition purposes. This is emphatically NOT a título propio.
programs.visaEligible: Yes, unambiguously. Same authorised centre as MPTI, plus registration in RUCT as an official Spanish Máster Universitario through UPV — which removes any residual consular doubt. The cleanest visa position in this batch.
programs.focus: Composition and scoring for film, television and video games; orchestration; conducting; recording and mixing of score with live musicians; game-audio work.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED structure from the official programme page: Core Module — visual media languages, orchestral techniques, visual media technology and recording, career seminar. Final Project Module — directed studies plus culminating experience. Elective Module — one elective course. Score recording sessions with professional musicians are funded by the dedicated recording-services fee.
programs.durationEcts: One academic year, three consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer; summer term 6–7 weeks). VERIFIED: 39–40 US credits, stated as 60 ECTS. Intake capped at 30 students annually on the Berklee page (UPV's 2026/27 offer lists 40 official places).
programs.language: English — 'all classes are taught in English' (verified).
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September (fall start).
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD 50,430 for 2026/2027 — VERIFIED, same graduate tuition as MPTI.
programs.tuitionTotal: USD 50,430 total tuition for the whole programme, academic year 2026/2027. Non-EU students pay the same rate.
programs.otherFees: ALL VERIFIED on the official 2026/2027 graduate tuition page: Application fee USD 150; non-refundable Tuition Deposit USD 2,500; Comprehensive Fee USD 1,600; Professional Recording Services Fee USD 2,990 — explicitly and exclusively 'Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games only', described as contributing 'to a fraction of the extraordinary studio and recording expenses unique to the scoring program'; required Software Bundle USD 700 for the Scoring programme (note: LOWER than MPTI's USD 800). programs.equipmentRequired: Software bundle USD 700 (verified). Laptop estimated USD 3,000 in Berklee's indirect-cost table, 'may be waived'. Scoring stage, studios and live musicians provided.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Direct cost billed by the college: USD 50,430 + 2,990 + 1,600 + 700 + 150 = USD 55,870 (deposit credited against tuition). With Berklee's published indirect estimates (housing 10,000–12,000, books 300–800, transport 300–600, personal 1,000) the all-in first year is approximately USD 68,000–71,000 without a laptop purchase, or up to USD 74,000 with it. programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED, AND STRICTER THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Exact published wording: 'Applicants are required to hold a bachelor's degree in music composition, electronic music production, or film scoring.' This is 'required to hold', NOT 'preferred'. Ideal candidates must 'Demonstrate a strong compositional foundation from their studies and/or professional experience; Possess the ability to notate one's ideas competently, follow an orchestral score, and conceive material in an orchestral context; and Exhibit passion for musical storytelling and a demonstrated aptitude for visual music.'
programs.acceptsNonMusic: EFFECTIVELY NO — CORRECTION. The verified wording is mandatory, not preferential: 'Applicants are required to hold a bachelor's degree in music composition, electronic music production, or film scoring.' A BSc in Software Engineering does not satisfy this on its face. On top of the degree bar, applicants must be able to 'notate one's ideas competently, follow an orchestral score, and conceive material in an orchestral context' — score-reading and orchestral literacy he does not have and could not credibly acquire by autumn 2026. This is the hardest entry in the batch for his specific profile.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED. Required: (1) a self-produced introductory video, maximum three minutes; (2) 'Three video files of original compositions for picture. Submit the three corresponding scores for the original compositions. Each file should not exceed two minutes.' Note the SCORES are mandatory here (unlike MPTI, where they are optional) — written notation is a hard deliverable. Berklee does provide a workaround for the picture requirement: applicants without film-scoring experience 'may extract clips from existing films and television shows via a number of available applications, import them to your music sequencing program, and create original compositions for the purposes of this application.' Applicable in principle: Berklee General Scholarship (amount varies, 15 Nov / 1 Feb) and the Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship (up to 50% of tuition, up to four awardees per year, deadline 1 February). programs.verificationNotes: Verified on the official programme page, the accreditation page, the entrance-requirements page, the how-to-apply page, the deadlines page, the scholarships page, the 2026/2027 tuition page, and cross-checked against UPV's published 2026/2027 master's places offer. programs.recommendation: AVOID — for fit, not quality. On paper this is the best-credentialled programme in the batch: a real Spanish Máster Universitario Oficial (RUCT 4313419, 60 ECTS) stacked on top of a US Master of Music, with the cleanest possible visa position. But it is the wrong instrument for him on two counts, and the second is disqualifying. First, it is composition-for-picture — orchestration, notation, conducting, scoring stages — not DJing, not electronic production, not club music. It does not serve his stated goal. Second, and decisively, the entry bar is now verified as mandatory: applicants are REQUIRED to hold a bachelor's in music composition, electronic music production or film scoring, and must be able to notate ideas, read an orchestral score and think orchestrally. He has none of that and cannot acquire it by autumn 2026. The mandatory portfolio of three original compositions to picture WITH written scores makes the gap concrete. It is also the most expensive option here — USD 55,870 in direct college costs because of the USD 2,990 recording-services fee, approaching USD 74,000 all-in. Listed for completeness and because it usefully proves that Berklee Valencia CAN deliver a Spanish official degree (which is exactly what MPTI does not). Skip it unless his ambitions genuinely shift to film and game scoring, in which case it becomes a multi-year plan, not a 2027 one.
