programs.qualification: MÁSTER UNIVERSITARIO OFICIAL — VERIFIED. The official programme page states the status is 'Oficial' and that the degree certificate is issued by the Ministry of Education. 60 ECTS. This is an official Spanish degree, NOT a título propio.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL. A Máster Universitario Oficial of Universitat Ramon Llull, within the Spanish official system (ANECA/AQU Catalunya framework), degree issued by the Ministry of Education, confirmed on the programme page as 'Oficial'. In practice: 60 ECTS valid across the EHEA, valid for PhD entry, unambiguous for the student visa, and recognised by employers as a real engineering master. programs.visaEligible: Yes, in principle — an official Spanish Máster Universitario at a recognised private university, delivered on-site in Barcelona, is the standard and safest route to a type-D student visa. ONE POINT TO CHECK: the official page describes the modality as on-site with classes on 'weekday afternoons' plus some online sessions. That is normal for a Spanish official master and should be fine, but because a partly-online component exists he should get written confirmation from La Salle's international office that the programme is classified as full-time on-site for visa purposes before committing.

programs.englishTest: UNVERIFIED — no English proficiency requirement is published on either the programme page or the requirements page. programs.scholarships: VERIFIED against La Salle's official master's scholarship programme page. programs.verificationNotes: Official status, ECTS, duration, language, start date, places, modality and the accepted-degrees list were all verified on La Salle's official programme and requirements pages, and the scholarship set was verified verbatim on the official master's scholarship-programme page. programs.recommendation: The strongest DEGREE in this batch and the weakest fit for his stated goal — and the trade-off is worth taking seriously rather than dismissing. On the plus side: it is a genuine Máster Universitario Oficial, 60 ECTS, taught entirely in English, at a serious private university, with a clean visa path, real published scholarships (up to 50% on GPA alone), NO portfolio requirement and NO musicianship test. It is the one programme here where his BSc is an asset rather than a liability and where his complete absence of music credentials costs him nothing. The verified IELTS bar is also almost certainly lower than Berklee's 7.5, though it is not published. On the minus side: it will not make him a DJ or a producer. It is noise control, vibration management and signal processing for automotive, aerospace, rail and construction — the entertainment sector is one application area among six. Three blockers must be resolved before it can even be costed: (1) SOFTWARE ENGINEERING IS NOT ON THE PUBLISHED ADMISSIONS LIST — get written confirmation it qualifies, or the rest is moot; (2) TUITION IS NOT PUBLISHED ANYWHERE — he cannot compare this against Berklee or UCAM until he has the number in writing; (3) the English requirement is unpublished. All three are answered by one email to Sardor Abdullaev or Iona Marie Lafont Amado. Recommend it only under a specific strategy: 'get to Barcelona on a real, fundable, visa-safe technical degree in English, and build the music career on the side in one of Europe's best electronic-music cities.' Given his profile and budget sensitivity that is a genuinely defensible plan — but he should choose it with his eyes open, not mistake it for a music production master.

programs.program: Máster de Formación Permanente en Producción Musical (semipresencial)
programs.institution: UCAM — Universidad Católica San Antonio de Murcia
programs.institutionType: Private university (Catholic, private, Murcia). The institution itself is a fully recognised Spanish private university.
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — VERIFIED. Specifically a 'Máster de Formación Permanente en Producción Musical Semipresencial', 60 ECTS. This is UCAM's OWN diploma. It is NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial, it does not appear in the RUCT register of official degrees, and it does not give direct access to a Spanish doctorate. THIS IS EXACTLY THE TRAP THE SPANISH PRIVATE SECTOR IS KNOWN FOR — the word 'Máster' in the title does not make it an official degree.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL as a degree. It is a título propio / Máster de Formación Permanente issued by UCAM under its own authority. The INSTITUTION is legitimate and recognised (UCAM is a real Spanish private university), but THIS AWARD is not ANECA-verified and is not an official master. In practice: a credible university-branded certificate with genuine industry weight and a real Steinberg Cubase professional certification attached — but legally a certificate, not a degree. He must not describe it as a master's degree on a CV in a jurisdiction that distinguishes the two.
programs.visaEligible: PROBABLY, BUT UNVERIFIED AND GENUINELY RISKY — DO NOT ASSUME. Spanish student visas require full-time study at an authorised centre. UCAM qualifies as an authorised centre, but the modality is confirmed SEMIPRESENCIAL (blended). Consulates routinely refuse, shorten or downgrade visa applications for programmes that are not full-time face-to-face, and a título propio adds no help. He must obtain written confirmation from UCAM's international office, naming this specific programme, that it supports a type-D student visa and residence permit for a Tunisian national — BEFORE paying the EUR 235 pre-enrolment fee. If the answer is no, the programme is worthless to him as a relocation route regardless of how good the content is.
programs.focus: Music production, composition techniques, artistic development, recording, mixing and mastering.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition and production techniques, artistic development, and all phases of creating and recording a musical work, through to mixing and mastering. programs.tuitionTotal: EUR 3,900 total tuition for the whole 60-ECTS programme. Verified for the currently advertised edition — confirm the figure for the 2027/2028 edition, as UCAM revises fees annually.
programs.otherFees: VERIFIED on the official page: pre-enrolment fee EUR 235 (non-refundable); school insurance EUR 59.12. No other institutional fees are published. That is an unusually clean and transparent fee structure by the standards of this sector.

programs.recommendation: The best VALUE in this batch by an enormous margin, and the decision hinges entirely on one unanswered question. For EUR 4,194.12 all-in — every euro verified — he gets a 60-ECTS university-branded music production programme with Sony Music España involvement, named Spanish electronic producers teaching masterclasses, and an official Steinberg Cubase certification. His software-engineering degree is EXPLICITLY listed as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, and no IELTS is needed. Compare that with Berklee: he would pay roughly twelve to sixteen times as much and face an IELTS 7.5 gate and a musicianship bar he currently cannot clear. But three caveats must be resolved in order, and the first is decisive. (1) THE VISA. It is semipresencial, and this is precisely the format Spanish consulates refuse. Get written confirmation from UCAM's international office, naming this programme and his nationality, before paying anything. If the answer is no, this programme cannot relocate him and its value collapses to zero for his stated purpose. (2) THE LANGUAGE. Teaching is entirely in Spanish, with no English track. If his Spanish is not already functional, twelve months of language work must run in parallel — which is still cheaper and more achievable than IELTS 7.5 plus USD 65,000. (3) THE AWARD. It is a título propio, legally a certificate, not an official degree — fine for an industry career where the Cubase certification and the Sony connection carry more weight than the parchment, but useless if he ever wants a Spanish PhD or a title-dependent role. If the visa answer comes back yes and his Spanish holds up, this is the highest return-on-euro option available to him in Spain and should be the pragmatic core of his plan, with Berklee as the aspirational stretch.

programs.scholarships: THIS ENTRY EXISTS BECAUSE IED'S DSU BANDO IS THE CLEAREST PUBLISHED PROOF THAT A NON-EU STUDENT AT AN ITALIAN PRIVATE ACADEMY CAN WIN REGIONAL STATE AID. Key provisions of the Bando DSU 2025/26 (BAN 8203 rev 06, 4 September 2025), total fund €354,392.15 from MUR and Regione Lombardia: ELIGIBILITY expressly includes 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' alongside Italians and EU citizens, for students admitted or enrolled on a Diploma Accademico di Primo or Secondo Livello at Milan, Rome, Turin, Cagliari or Florence. INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario must not exceed €26,516.70 AND ISPE must not exceed €57,645.03 — both jointly. MERIT for a 1st-year II livello student: simply be regularly enrolled by 31 October and hold the first-level title by 31 January; confirmation of the full benefit then requires 40 credits by 10 August. AMOUNTS (including €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance): in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114 by income band 1/2/3; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; FUORI SEDE €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776. THE DECISIVE DETAIL: under Art. 13(3) DPCM 9/4/2001, NON-EU FOREIGN STUDENTS ARE AUTOMATICALLY CLASSIFIED 'FUORI SEDE' regardless of where they live in Italy (unless their family lives in Italy), provided the accommodation is paid for — so a Tunisian student is placed in the HIGHEST bracket, €5,776 to €8,134 per year. NON-EU DOCUMENTATION: an 'ISEEU-ISPEU parificato' is required, built from foreign family-composition certificate, income declarations from the official tax agency of the country of residence (employer documents are NOT accepted, self-certification is NOT accepted), property and movable-asset statements, all translated into Italian by a recognised translator and legalised; Tunisia is NOT on the exemption or Apostille list published in the bando, so full consular legalisation applies. A floor applies: non-EU students' declared income cannot be counted below €7,002.97/year (the visa subsistence minimum). Free ISEEU assistance is via CAAF CGIL Lombardia under an IED agreement. DEADLINES 2025/26: applications 9 September to 7 November 2025; rent contract for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025. EXCLUSIONS THAT MATTER: anyone already holding an equal or higher qualification is excluded (a BSc does not block a II livello application); anyone receiving another income/merit-based grant for the same year is excluded; FOUNDATION course students are excluded; and the bando covers ONLY Diploma Accademico I/II livello — IED's one-year 'Master' courses are NOT covered. IED separately runs a commercial scholarship competition: 114 scholarships/tutorships covering 50% of tuition for Master of Arts and Master programmes 2025/26 across Italian campuses and Accademia di Como, rising to 127 for 2026/27 across Italy and Spain, open to local and international students including non-EU, covering partial tuition only and NOT living costs or enrolment fees.
programs.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — not published in the DSU bando. Note that DSU is not a fee waiver: 'Le tasse di iscrizione e di contributo accademico dovranno comunque essere interamente versate' — fees must be paid in full and the scholarship arrives afterwards, in instalments.

Also note IED's dedicated SOUND DESIGN programme is a FIRST-level diploma (BA equivalent), not a master.
programs.visaEligible: Yes for the Diploma Accademico route — the bando references 'permesso di soggiorno' for extra-EU students as a routine document, and the visa subsistence figure of €7,002.97 is built into the income rules, confirming this is a standard non-EU pathway.

programs.reputationSignals: IED is a major international private design chain with campuses across Italy, Spain and Brazil, operating inside the AFAM system, with a substantial published DSU fund (€354,392.15 for 2025/26) and a formal CAAF agreement to help foreign students obtain the ISEE parificato. programs.recommendation: IED itself does not offer what he wants at master level — its Sound Design programme is an undergraduate diploma. Include IED in his research NOT as a destination but as the clearest published evidence of how the Italian DSU route works for a non-EU student: he can win €5,776–€8,134 a year at an Italian PRIVATE academy because non-EU students are automatically classed 'fuori sede'. programs.scholarships: NO INSTITUTIONAL SCHOLARSHIP IS PUBLISHED on the pages read for this programme, and the national scheme is CLOSED TO HIM. Portuguese DGES bolsas de ação social direta require Portuguese nationality, or foreign nationality with a PERMANENT residence permit in Portugal, or coverage by a cooperation agreement, or reciprocity, or stateless/refugee status. Under Decreto-Lei 36/2014 as amended by Decreto-Lei 62/2018, 'estudantes internacionais' benefit ONLY from indirect social action (canteens, facilities) — they are EXCLUDED from the direct monetary grant. The one exception is students granted humanitarian-emergency status, who receive both direct and indirect support. DGES does note that some private higher-education institutions offer their own bolsas to economically disadvantaged students whose nationality is not covered by the DGES scheme — i.e. all foreign students without a residence title — so it is worth ASKING Lusófona directly whether such an internal fund exists for this programme. Status: UNVERIFIED. Erasmus+ mobility funding may be available once enrolled, but it is not entry funding.
programs.paymentPlans: MONTHLY BY DEFAULT — this is the key financial advantage. Tuition is billed as mensalidades due by the 8th of each month. International/foreign students must settle the FIRST TWO MONTHLY INSTALMENTS at the moment of matrícula/inscrição (Ordem de Serviço nº 8/2019). So the up-front outlay at enrolment is application €450 + inscrição/matrícula €300 + seguro €47 + 2 × €365.40 = approximately €1,527. Payment methods: credit card and PayPal online; Multibanco or cash in person. No interest or finance charge is mentioned — this is a genuine instalment arrangement, not a loan, which contrasts sharply with microFusa's 8.95% APR scheme in Spain.

An A3ES-ACCREDITED master's — a real degree, not a certificate — in exactly his subject, at a private university, for roughly €7,300 in tuition over two years, with monthly interest-free instalments and no non-EU tuition premium. The curriculum (acoustics, digital audio computing, synthesis, Max/MSP, Arduino) is arguably BETTER suited to a software engineer than any music-conservatory route, and the 75% portfolio-and-interview weighting means his portfolio matters more than his lack of a music degree. The one real obstacle is LANGUAGE: it is taught in Portuguese, and he has 13 months. programs.scholarships: TWO ABSOLUTE EXCLUSIONS HE MUST UNDERSTAND BEFORE CHOOSING SPAIN. (1) TITLE-TYPE EXCLUSION: Becas MEC can be requested only for official undergraduate (grado) and OFFICIAL master's studies. They CANNOT be requested for a 'título propio' or a permanent-education programme. Third-cycle studies, specialisation studies and títulos propios are all outside the scheme. Fees must be paid to a Spanish centre. This alone kills MEC funding for Universidad Europea's Máster en Producción Creativa de la Música, TAI's Máster en Producción Musical, SAE Spain's UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente, and every microFusa diploma. (2) NATIONALITY/RESIDENCE EXCLUSION: non-EU foreigners must hold LEGAL RESIDENCE ('residencia legal') in Spain to qualify. The situation of 'estancia' — which is exactly what a study authorisation confers — does NOT give any right to a university grant. Holding an authorisation of stay is expressly not sufficient. EU citizens must be permanent residents or prove employment. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded even if he chose an OFFICIAL master's. (3) COMUNIDAD DE MADRID: its student grants target students enrolled at MADRID PUBLIC universities on official grado or master's studies in disadvantaged socio-economic situations; and its Becas de Excelencia expressly EXCLUDE 'estudios de máster, especialización o títulos propios'. No Comunidad de Madrid route exists for a private-university título propio. (4) GENERALITAT DE CATALUNYA non-university grants (€300–350 basic, €50–125 performance, €1,700 income-based, €2,700 relocation, 2026-2027) are tied to Catalan income/academic and residence conditions and are not reachable by a newly arrived non-EU student. (5) WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN TO HIM IN SPAIN: only institution-level commercial discounts (early place-reservation, alumni, referral) and one genuinely nationality-blind private award found in this research — the YAMAHA MUSIC EUROPE FOUNDATION grant of €1,000–2,000 per year for students under 25 enrolled at a recognised European music institution, distributing roughly €66,000 a year.
programs.paymentPlans: Not applicable — but note the consequence: because no state aid reaches him, every Spanish private option must be financed entirely from savings, family, or a commercial instalment plan (which in the microFusa case carries 8.95% APR and requires a Spanish bank account he cannot open before arrival).
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL / NOT APPLICABLE — this entry documents an exclusion rule, not a programme.
programs.visaEligible: Not applicable, but the interaction is the key insight: the very visa status that lets him study in Spain ('estancia por estudios') is the status that disqualifies him from Spanish state grants.
programs.applicationOpens: Annual call, normally spring. Not relevant to him given the exclusions.
programs.deadline: Not relevant given the exclusions. PRIOR CYCLE dates not tracked.
programs.reputationSignals: This is the single most important structural finding for Spain: the country with the most heavily marketed private 'másteres' in music production is also the country where none of them attracts state support for a non-EU student.
programs.recommendation: Treat Spain as a FULLY SELF-FUNDED market. There is no scenario in which a Tunisian on a study visa receives Spanish state or regional aid for a private-sector music-production programme — he fails the title-type test and the residence test independently. Therefore: (a) ignore any school that gestures vaguely at 'becas del ministerio'; (b) judge Spanish options purely on sticker price minus the school's own commercial discount; (c) if he is under 25, apply to the Yamaha Music Europe Foundation, which is the only nationality-blind award found; and (d) always ask the school in writing whether the programme is a 'Máster Universitario Oficial' or a 'Título Propio / Máster de Formación Permanente' — and get the answer in an email, not a phone call.

programs.scholarships: THE DECISIVE MECHANISM: NON-EU STUDENTS ARE ELIGIBLE, AND THEY LAND IN THE HIGHEST-VALUE BRACKET. (1) ELIGIBILITY: the IED bando states plainly that applications may be made by Italian citizens, EU citizens, AND 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' (under DPR 394/1999 arts. 44-bis and 46(5), and D.lgs 286/1998). Non-EU students at a PRIVATE academy are explicitly in scope. (2) THE 'FUORI SEDE' RULE: under Art. 13(3) DPCM 9/4/2001, non-EU foreign students are AUTOMATICALLY treated as 'fuori sede' regardless of where they live in Italy (unless their family lives in Italy), provided they pay for accommodation. Fuori sede is the top payment band. (3) AMOUNTS (IED, Lombardy, 2025/26, including €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance): fuori sede €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776 by income band 1/2/3; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114. NABA quotes a range of roughly €2,000 to €8,000 including a free daily meal. So a Tunisian student renting a room in Milan is looking at €5,776–€8,134 per year. (4) INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario ≤ €26,516.70 AND ISPE ≤ €57,645.03 — both must be satisfied. Income bands: 1st €0–13,258.35; 2nd €13,258.36–17,677.80; 3rd €17,677.81–26,516.70. (5) MERIT FOR A FIRST-YEAR SECOND-LEVEL STUDENT: essentially just enrolment plus holding the first-level title; full confirmation then requires 38–40 credits by the following 10 August. (6) THE NON-EU PAPERWORK — THIS IS THE HARD PART: he needs an 'ISEEU-ISPEU parificato' built from (a) a certificate of current foreign household composition, (b) income declarations for each household member for the reference calendar year issued by the OFFICIAL GOVERNMENT TAX AGENCY of the country of residence — employer documents are expressly NOT accepted and self-certification is expressly NOT valid, (c) property holdings with square metres or a certificate of no property for every member aged 18+, (d) movable assets (securities, dividends, shareholdings, company net-worth fractions, accounts). Everything must be translated into Italian by a recognised translator and LEGALISED. TUNISIA IS NOT on the bando's legalisation-exemption list and NOT on the Apostille list — so full consular legalisation applies. A floor also applies: non-EU declared income cannot be treated as below €7,002.97/year, the visa subsistence minimum. IED has a convention with CAAF CGIL Lombardia to help foreign students obtain the parificato. (7) COMPETITION IS THE RISK: for 2025/26 NABA Milano put just ONE scholarship to competition for first-year second-level students (and one at NABA Roma); IED pooled €354,392.15 across four ranking lists proportional to applicant numbers. Ranking for first-year students is purely a function of ISEE — a lower ISEE ranks higher. (8) INCOMPATIBILITY: receiving any other income- or merit-based grant for the same year is an automatic exclusion, so DSU cannot be stacked with the institution's own scholarship. (9) PAYMENT: two instalments (roughly February and July/September); second-assignment winners get one payment around December. Paid ONLY by bank transfer to an Italian or SEPA account in the student's name — he will need a European bank account.
programs.paymentPlans: Not applicable. Note the cash-flow trap: fees must be paid in full BEFORE the scholarship is awarded, and the first instalment does not arrive until around February. He must be able to fund the whole first term unaided.
programs.accreditationStatus: Applies ONLY to Diploma Accademico di PRIMO or SECONDO livello courses. It does NOT apply to one-year 'Master' courses at IED, and Foundation-course students are excluded. This is another reason to choose a biennio (II livello) over a 'Master di I livello'.
programs.visaEligible: Not applicable directly, but the scheme presupposes a valid permesso di soggiorno for extra-EU students and builds the €7,002.97 visa subsistence minimum into its income rules — confirming it is designed for genuine non-EU students.
programs.applicationOpens: IED 2025/26: applications from 9 September 2025. NABA 2025/26: online form by 22 September 2025. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027/28 dates (expect early September 2027).
programs.deadline: IED 7 November 2025 (rent contract for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025); NABA 22 September 2025 online / 25 September 2025 documents. Provisional rankings by 31 October, appeals within 15 days, final rankings by 30 November. ALL PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
programs.reputationSignals: This is genuine public money (MUR plus regional funds) flowing to students at PRIVATE academies — an arrangement that has no equivalent in Spain, Portugal or the Netherlands for a non-EU student. IED alone put €354,392.15 to competition for 2025/26. RED FLAGS: brutal documentation requirements for a Tunisian; very small numbers of second-level awards at some campuses; no automatic renewal; and the cash arrives months after fees are due.
programs.recommendation: THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FINANCIAL FINDING FOR HIM. Italy is the only one of the four countries where a Tunisian studying at a PRIVATE institution can receive substantial state-backed money — €5,776 to €8,134 a year, because non-EU students are automatically classed 'fuori sede'. Combined with a NABA international scholarship (up to €6,000) — though note the two are INCOMPATIBLE and he must choose — or with Saint Louis's much lower fees, this changes the economics completely. Concrete actions, starting NOW and not in 2027: (1) obtain official Tunisian tax-authority income statements for the whole household for the relevant year, plus property and asset certificates, plus a household-composition certificate; (2) get them translated into Italian by a recognised translator and fully consular-legalised — Tunisia has no Apostille shortcut here; (3) plan to have a registered rental contract in Italy by early December of the entry year, or he is downgraded from fuori sede to pendolare and loses €2,000–4,000; (4) budget to pay the entire first term of fees before any scholarship money arrives; (5) open a SEPA bank account early, since payment is by transfer only.

THE EXCLUSION: for the 2026-2027 academic year the participating institutions number 11 research universities and 24 universities of applied sciences — all PUBLICLY FUNDED (bekostigd) Dutch institutions. Deadlines are set individually by each participating institution — irrelevant to him since none of the relevant audio providers participates. programs.recommendation: On the funding evidence, DROP THE NETHERLANDS from the private-sector shortlist. The €5,000 NL Scholarship cannot follow him to a private institution; Dutch student loans cannot either; SAE Amsterdam publishes no scholarships at all and stays silent on visa sponsorship; and Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states in writing that it cannot help a non-EU resident get a visa. That combination — highest living costs of the four countries, zero funding, and an unresolved or negative visa position — makes the Dutch private sector the worst value in this slice for a Tunisian national. Amsterdam remains the right city for his career; it is simply not accessible to him through a private school. Revisit only if a public Dutch institution comes into scope.

programs.scholarships: THE RULE: to apply for a DGES bolsa de estudo, a candidate must hold Portuguese nationality; OR foreign nationality WITH a PERMANENT residence permit in Portugal; OR be covered by cooperation agreements providing such benefits; OR be a national of a state whose law grants equal treatment to Portuguese students in equal circumstances; OR be stateless or hold political refugee status. THE EXCLUSION: students admitted under 'estudante internacional' status benefit EXCLUSIVELY from INDIRECT social action under Decreto-Lei n.º 36/2014 of 10 March, as amended by Decreto-Lei n.º 62/2018 of 6 August — meaning canteens, facilities and services, but NOT the direct monetary grant. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded from DGES cash support at BOTH public and private institutions. THE ONE EXCEPTION: international students granted 'estudante em situação de emergência por razões humanitárias' status receive the full range of direct and indirect support — not applicable to him. THE IMPORTANT SILVER LINING, STATED BY DGES ITSELF: some PRIVATE higher-education institutions offer their own bolsas to economically disadvantaged students whose nationality is not covered by the DGES scheme — that is, precisely all foreign students without a residence title. This is the door he should push on. Concrete examples found in this research: UCP Porto grants scholarships annually to candidates of non-Portuguese nationality who do NOT reside in Portugal, giving partial exemption from the master's tuition, awarded on application average plus interview (contact ee.bolsas@ucp.pt); UCP's Escola das Artes runs Bolsas de Mérito e Incentivo à Investigação for master's students giving total or partial tuition exemption; and The Social Hub Changemaker Housing Scholarship targets refugee and international students. Lusófona publishes no equivalent on the pages read (UNVERIFIED — ask).
programs.paymentPlans: Not applicable — but note that Portuguese private universities structure tuition as interest-free MONTHLY instalments (Lusófona €365.40/month, UCP €657/month), which is a materially better cash-flow deal than Spain's interest-bearing plans or the Netherlands' instalment premiums. Lusófona requires international students to pay the first TWO monthly instalments at matrícula.
programs.accreditationStatus: Not applicable — but the parallel Portuguese trap is the mestrado/pós-graduação distinction: a 'mestrado' accredited by A3ES is a degree; a 'pós-graduação' is a post-graduate COURSE that is not a degree. ETIC's offerings are neither.
programs.visaEligible: Not applicable directly. Note that DGES also administers the 'Concurso Especial para Estudantes Internacionais', the special admission route for international students — the same status that grants admission is the status that removes grant eligibility.
programs.applicationOpens: Annual, normally summer (the 2025/2026 call opened in the summer of 2025). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027/28 dates. Not relevant to him given the exclusion.
programs.deadline: Set annually by DGES. Not relevant given the exclusion.
programs.reputationSignals: Portugal is the cheapest of the four countries for accredited private master's study by a very wide margin (Lusófona ~€7,300 total tuition; UCP Porto €13,140 total), which substantially offsets the absence of national grant access. The exclusion hurts far less here than it would in Spain.
programs.recommendation: Understand the split clearly: Portuguese NATIONAL money is closed to him, but Portuguese PRIVATE INSTITUTIONAL money is not, and DGES says so explicitly. So in Portugal he should stop looking at government schemes entirely and instead write directly to institutional scholarship offices. The highest-value single action in this whole slice is to email ee.bolsas@ucp.pt and ask for the regulation and the amount of the scholarship for non-Portuguese nationals not resident in Portugal — that award is designed for his exact profile. Then ask Lusófona the same question. Combined with tuition of €3,654/year (Lusófona) or €6,570/year (UCP Porto) paid interest-free monthly, Portugal is the only country in this slice where a self-funding Tunisian can realistically complete an ACCREDITED master's in sound without debt.

No red flags — they simply do not teach music or audio. This is a clean negative, not a quality problem.
programs.recommendation: CONFIRMED NEGATIVE — the prior finding is correct and I verified it independently rather than accepting it. Evidence: (a) ESIC's own master index at esic.edu was fetched and lists only business, marketing, digital marketing, big data, logistics, finance, project management, HR and international trade — no music, sound, audio or audiovisual production programme of any kind, at either the oficial or the título propio tier. (b) UIC Barcelona's own postgraduate study-search was fetched and returns dentistry, architecture, medicine/health sciences, pharmacy and education programmes; a site-restricted search surfaced no music or audio master. The two nearest UIC items are the Máster Universitario en Gestión Cultural (Arts and Cultural Management — an OFICIAL humanities master) and the Postgraduate Degree in Management of Cultural and Creative Industries; both are arts-MANAGEMENT/administration programmes that touch the music industry as a sector to be managed. Neither teaches production, mixing, sound design or live electronics, and neither would give him studio hours, a portfolio or DJ/producer craft. They are the wrong instrument for his goal and should not be treated as substitutes. (c) Universidad Villanueva's master catalogue was fetched: MBA, marketing digital, HR, risk prevention, LLM, tax, abogacía, teacher training, psychopedagogy, ed-tech, several psychology masters, sports journalism and event management. Its only audiovisual offering is the undergraduate Grado en Comunicación Audiovisual — a bachelor, and a general audiovisual-communication one at that, not music production. He already holds a bachelor, so it is doubly irrelevant. Rule all three out and spend no further time on them. Related negative finding, also verified: Universidad Loyola (private, Seville/Dos Hermanas and Córdoba) does run a Creación y Producción Musical programme with the University of San Francisco, and it is genuinely production-focused and portfolio-driven — but it is a GRADO PROPIO, i.e. a BACHELOR-level qualification AND the university's own title rather than an ANECA-official grado. It is out of scope on both counts for a graduate seeking a September 2027 master. The practical takeaway for this slice: mainstream Spanish private universities do not serve music production at master level. The real Spanish options for him sit either in specialist audio academies (SAE Madrid/Barcelona, Microfusa, TAI) — which mostly issue títulos propios with the visa caveat above — or in public universities (notably UPF Barcelona's Máster en Tecnologías del Sonido y de la Música, which is ANECA-official but heavily engineering/research-oriented rather than DJ/producer craft). Those belong to other slices, but this slice's conclusion is firm: nothing here.
programs.verificationNotes: Verified August 2026. Method: fetched ESIC's master index (https://www.esic.edu/madrid/master-y-postgrado/master) — programme list returned, no music/audio entry at any tier; fetched UIC Barcelona's international-student postgraduate page and its filtered study-search (https://www.uic.es/en/studies/study-search?f%5B0%5D=class%3A976) — no music/audio/sound programme, nearest matches are Arts & Cultural Management (oficial) and Management of Cultural and Creative Industries (postgraduate certificate), both management not production; fetched Universidad Villanueva's master catalogue (https://www.villanueva.edu/masteres/) — no music/audio master, only an undergraduate Grado en Comunicación Audiovisual. Cross-checked with Spanish-language web searches for each institution plus music/audio/sound keywords: every hit returned OTHER providers (SAE Spain, Escuela TAI, UDIMA, UNIR, ENTI-UB, UPF, Microfusa-type schools), never these three. The Loyola cross-reference was also checked against uloyola.es and confirmed as a 'grado propio' (bachelor, own-title) rather than a master. The Spanish ES-side sourceUrl was fetched successfully and did not need correcting. No fee, deadline, portfolio or English-test data exists to verify because no qualifying programme exists — all such fields are correctly N/A rather than UNVERIFIED. No PRIOR CYCLE date issues arise here.

NONE of these figures appear on a VIU-owned page — treat as indicative only, NOT verified.

programs.entryRequirements: Verified wording on the live page: applicants must be "Titulados Superiores de Música", or hold a degree in Historia y Ciencias de la Música / Musicología, or an equivalent music-education qualification. The published requirement is a music qualification ("Titulados Superiores de Música", Historia y Ciencias de la Música, Musicología "o titulaciones equivalentes"). programs.auditionSpec: Recorded video audition (15–20 min, two contrasting works, classical string instrument or piano) for the Interpretación track. None for the Investigación track.
programs.englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is taught and assessed entirely in Spanish. IELTS is irrelevant here; what would be required is Spanish proficiency. He would need Spanish, not English, and no Spanish-level requirement is published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling, per intake. No fixed opening date published.
programs.deadline: Rolling until the cohort fills. No published deadline for October 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Promotional cut-offs observed (31 July, 14 August) are marketing deadlines for the discount, not application deadlines.

PRIOR CYCLE. FUNDAE-subsidised places exist but require employment by a Spanish company and are unavailable to him. Nothing targeted at non-EU or Tunisian applicants was found. Negative and decisive for him: online-only (no visa, no facilities), Spanish-only, hard music-qualification entry bar, classical/academic orientation, no published price anywhere, and the companion Composición Musical master has quietly disappeared — a sign the music portfolio is contracting, not growing.
programs.verificationNotes: VERIFIED from the live VIU programme page and the VIU master catalogue: award type (Máster Universitario Oficial, ANECA), 60 ECTS structure, two specialities, Spanish language, 100% online, October/April intakes, entry requirements, audition spec, admission weighting. (1) He is ineligible: entry is restricted to holders of a Superior Music diploma, musicology or music-history degree; a BSc in Software Engineering does not qualify, and the Interpretación track additionally demands a 15–20 minute classical video audition on violin, viola, cello or piano worth half the admission score. (2) It cannot get him to Spain: 100% online delivery cannot support a Spanish student visa or residence permit, so the ANECA-official status — genuinely real here — buys him nothing he actually wants. (3) The content is wrong: classical interpretation and musicology, in Spanish, with zero production, mixing, sound design or electronic music. Additionally, correct the record he may be working from: VIU's Máster en Composición Musical has been withdrawn, so if he found that programme in a search, it no longer exists. Included so he does not lose weeks on the VIU adverts that dominate searches for "máster oficial música España".

programs.institutionType: Private university (Madrid), recognised Spanish university.
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — verified verbatim. The programme page carries the literal text "Título propio" in its qualification field, alongside "60 ECTS". This is UAX's own diploma, NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. Confirmed título propio: no ANECA verification, not registered in RUCT as an official title, no automatic EHEA recognition, no PhD access, no value for Spanish public-sector oposiciones or homologation. NOTE THE NAMING TELL, which he should learn to read across all Spanish private universities: UAX's official awards are named "Máster Universitario en ..." (e.g. the Máster Universitario en Gestión de la Cultura, el Deporte, los Medios y el Entretenimiento launched alongside it), while this one is named "Máster en ..." with no "Universitario" — that word is the difference between an official degree and a school certificate. Some UAX marketing and press coverage loosely calls the whole Live Nation family "official degrees"; the programme page itself says título propio, and the programme page governs.
programs.visaEligible: PROBABLE but UNVERIFIED — must be confirmed in writing before he pays anything. Positive factors, all verified from the page's own metadata: fully presencial ("academic_mode":"presencial"), 9 months full-time, 60 ECTS, at a recognised Spanish university on a Madrid campus. Spanish estancia por estudios normally accepts full-time in-person study at a recognised university leading to a diploma, including títulos propios. But it is NOT automatic for a non-official title, the page makes no visa statement, and UAX publishes no international-admissions guarantee. He must get written confirmation from UAX international admissions that they issue the carta de admisión required for a student visa for THIS specific título propio.
programs.focus: Live music BUSINESS: concert and festival production, artist management, touring, logistics, budgeting, negotiation with artists and promoters, ticketing, sponsorship, marketing and legal frameworks. This is management, not production and not sound craft.
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified from the live page: concert production, artist management, logistics and operations, budgeting, negotiation with artists and promoters, legal aspects, marketing and creativity applied to marketing, sponsorship and audience development, ticketing, and project management — delivered through real projects. Masterclasses by Live Nation, Ticketmaster and Superstruct Entertainment executives, plus practical workshops on negotiation and event production. Faculty verified to include working industry figures (e.g. Pedro Martínez-Vega, of Resonance Projects, previously involved in the Grupo Pacha/Trilantic transformation and the Woomoon and Toyroom brands — genuinely relevant to the electronic-music/Ibiza economy). ZERO studio, DAW, mixing, mastering, synthesis or DJ-technique content.
programs.durationEcts: 60 ECTS, 9 months, presencial. Confirmed in the page's own analytics metadata: duration 9 meses, mode presencial, campus Madrid Chamberí.
programs.language: Spanish. Confirmed — the programme is served from the Spanish site with Spanish faculty and Spanish industry partners; no English-taught route for this title.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, starting October, Madrid Chamberí. October 2027 is the realistic target but is not yet published — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. UAX publishes NO price on the programme page, and its prices-and-scholarships page returns 404. The only monetary statement is a rotating promotional "25% de ayuda hasta el 15 de agosto". For a 60-ECTS presencial título propio at a Madrid private university, the realistic market band is roughly EUR 9,000–16,000, but this is a market inference, NOT a verified UAX figure — do not treat it as a quote.
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED. Must be requested from UAX admissions in writing, with the non-EU price specifically confirmed.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. No application fee, reserva de plaza, enrolment fee, materials fee or insurance figure is published anywhere on the UAX site. Spanish private universities typically charge a separate non-refundable reserva de plaza; assume one exists until told otherwise.
programs.equipmentRequired: A laptop. Nothing else identified — this is a management programme with no studio or software requirement. UNVERIFIED formally.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — no price is published, so no honest total can be given. On top of tuition he must budget Madrid living costs (realistically EUR 1,000–1,400/month) and satisfy the Spanish student-visa proof-of-funds requirement, which is pegged to 100% of IPREM (approximately EUR 600/month, i.e. roughly EUR 7,200 for a year, held in his own name).
programs.entryRequirements: NOT PUBLISHED on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. The page describes the audience as professionals and graduates seeking to work in live music production and event management, but states no formal degree requirement, no grade threshold and no language requirement. The normal standard for a UAX título propio is a university degree in any discipline plus an admissions interview. He must obtain the written requirements from admissions.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: ALMOST CERTAINLY YES, but the formal wording is UNVERIFIED because no entry requirements are published. The page's own framing is occupational rather than disciplinary — it addresses people who want to "liderar proyectos reales desde dentro de la industria: producción de conciertos, management, logística, presupuestos, negociación" — with no reference to musical training, an instrument, or a music degree. Live-music management programmes routinely admit business, law, marketing and technology graduates, and a software-engineering background is an asset for ticketing and data roles. This is the one programme in this batch whose admissions bar he plausibly clears today.
programs.portfolioSpec: None published. No portfolio, no demo reel, no track submission required — consistent with a management programme.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no performance test, no instrumental requirement.
programs.englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is in Spanish, so IELTS is irrelevant. The real language barrier is SPANISH: he would be studying negotiation, contracts and legal frameworks in Spanish, in a Spanish-language cohort. No Spanish-level requirement is published (UNVERIFIED), but functioning in this programme without solid Spanish (realistically B2) would be very difficult.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling. No published opening date.
programs.deadline: No published application deadline — admission is rolling until the cohort fills. UNVERIFIED for the 2027 intake. The "15 de agosto" date is a discount cut-off, not an application deadline.
programs.scholarships: No true scholarship identified for a non-EU applicant. The advertised "25% de ayuda hasta el 15 de agosto" is a rotating promotional discount (a price cut, not a merit award), and it belongs to the current cycle — PRIOR CYCLE for his purposes. UAX separately advertises excellence scholarships and continuity-of-studies aid of up to 25%, but neither their criteria nor their availability to non-EU or título-propio students is published — UNVERIFIED. Assume he pays close to full price with at most a promotional discount.
programs.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED. Spanish private universities almost always offer monthly instalments across the academic year, but UAX publishes nothing for this programme. Confirm in writing, and confirm whether instalments are available to a student without a Spanish bank account or guarantor.
programs.facilities: Campus Chamberí in central Madrid. The real asset is not facilities but access: verified industry partners are Live Nation (co-developer of the programme), Ticketmaster, Sony Music, Superstruct Entertainment and Mad Cool Festival, with internships at sector companies and masterclasses delivered by their executives. There are no recording studios, no consoles and no Atmos rooms attached to this programme, and none would be relevant to it.
programs.reputationSignals: STRONG for the live-music sector: Live Nation is the world's largest concert promoter and co-developed the programme; Ticketmaster, Superstruct and Mad Cool are named partners; faculty includes practitioners with genuine electronic-music-economy credentials (Grupo Pacha, Woomoon, Toyroom). UAX also runs one of Spain's longest-established university music faculties and, in April 2026, expanded the Live Nation partnership with three further programmes (verified live on https://www.uax.com/musica-live-nation): an MBA in Music Business (título propio — the English page states "Own degree" — 60 ECTS, 9 months, blended learning, Madrid Chamberí), a Grado en Composición y Creación Musical Aplicada (official 4-year degree, ONLINE), and a Máster Universitario en Gestión de la Cultura, el Deporte, los Medios y el Entretenimiento (this one genuinely OFFICIAL, Málaga campus, November start). RED FLAGS: título propio sold at master-level positioning; no price published anywhere; no entry requirements published; prices-and-scholarships page 404s; marketing that blurs the official/propio distinction. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE: none of the four UAX Live Nation programmes teaches music production, mixing, sound design or DJ craft.
programs.verificationNotes: VERIFIED directly from the live UAX page source: the literal string "Título propio"; 60 ECTS; and the page's embedded metadata giving academic_mode "presencial", academic_duration "9 meses", campus "madrid chamberí", academic_area "musica". VERIFIED from https://www.uax.com/musica-live-nation: the full four-programme Live Nation family and their award types, including that only the Gestión de la Cultura master is a "Máster Universitario" (official). VERIFIED partner list. NOT VERIFIED, because UAX publishes none of it: tuition, application fee, enrolment fee, any other fee, entry requirements, language requirement, application deadline, payment plans, non-EU scholarship eligibility, and visa sponsorship. The 25% discount and its 15 August cut-off are current-cycle promotions and will not apply to a September/October 2027 entry. CONFLICT RESOLVED: press coverage and the Live Nation hub page loosely describe these as official degrees; the programme page's own qualification field says "Título propio" and is authoritative.
programs.recommendation: AVOID as a route to becoming a DJ/producer — the decisive reason is that it teaches none of the craft he asked for. Nine months and (probably) five figures buy him concert logistics, contracts, ticketing and sponsorship; he would not touch a DAW, a console or a studio. Two further problems compound it: the award is a título propio, so he would pay master-level money for a school certificate with no ANECA verification, no EHEA recognition and no PhD access; and UAX publishes no price at all, which for a budget-sensitive self-payer is disqualifying on its own — never commit to a programme that will not tell you what it costs. FLAG IT TO HIM ANYWAY, honestly, as a strategic alternative, because it solves the two problems no production school solves for him: it needs no portfolio and no musicianship proof, so his admissions weaknesses vanish; and the Live Nation, Ticketmaster, Superstruct and Mad Cool relationships are the most commercially valuable industry links anywhere in this Spanish slice, with faculty drawn from the Pacha/Woomoon/Ibiza electronic economy. If his true goal is "work in international electronic music" rather than "be the person at the desk", this is a real door — and his software-engineering degree is a genuine asset in ticketing and music-data roles. Two hard conditions before he would ever consider it: get the total non-EU price in writing, and get written confirmation that UAX will issue a carta de admisión supporting a student visa for a título propio. Also note he would be studying negotiation and contract law in Spanish, which without B2 Spanish is not survivable. If the official-degree route matters to him more than the subject, the sister Máster Universitario en Gestión de la Cultura, el Deporte, los Medios y el Entretenimiento (Málaga) is the one genuinely ANECA-official title in this family.

programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
programs.institution: Berklee College of Music — Valencia Campus
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — US private conservatory operating an authorised Spanish higher-education centre (Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música)
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.M.) — a UNITED STATES degree awarded by Berklee College of Music, delivered on Spanish soil. It is NOT a Spanish 'Máster Universitario Oficial' and NOT a 'Título Propio' — it is a foreign (US) degree.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL IN SPAIN — CONFIRMED VERBATIM on Berklee's own accreditation page (https://www.berklee.edu/institutional-research-assessment/valencia-spain-campus-accreditation). That page states 'All Berklee degrees are accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE)' and that, additionally, 'the Master of Arts in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the Master of Music in Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games are accredited in Spain' — each of those two carries an 'ANECA Verified Report (2017)'. MPTI carries NO ANECA report and appears ONLY under NECHE institutional accreditation. PRACTICAL MEANING: MPTI is a genuine, regionally accredited US master's degree with excellent industry recognition, but in Spanish/EHEA terms it is a foreign title. It does NOT automatically give Spanish PhD access or public-sector recognition; that would require 'equivalencia/homologación' through the Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades — slow and uncertain. THIS IS THE TRAP TO AVOID: 'a Berklee master in Spain' is not a Spanish master.
programs.visaEligible: YES. The Valencia campus is an authorised Spanish higher-education centre and runs a full international-admissions pathway; non-EU/EEA/Swiss students are expected to obtain a Spanish student visa and the campus issues the acceptance letters used for it. The mandatory $1,600 comprehensive fee explicitly covers 'registration into the Spanish educational system' and compulsory health insurance. This is the safest visa route in this slice — a one-year, full-time, on-campus programme at an authorised centre.
programs.focus: Music production, studio and hybrid recording, electronic music production and performance, sound design, music video, interactive media, DJing, music technology and innovation.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED on the official programme page. Core Module (required): Audio Engineering; Studio Music Production; Music Video Production; Interactive Media; Electronic Music Production and Performance; Career Preparation — plus two required proficiencies in Pro Tools and Analog Audio. Final Project Module (required): three seminars covering the past, present and future of music production technology, plus the Culminating Experience Project (proposal, development, defense). Elective Module: 4 credits chosen from audio engineering, studio production, theory/songwriting, DJing, video production, interactive media and electronic music. Optional: ensembles, music research, rhythm studies, and an optional internship. Labs run Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools and Adobe Premiere.
programs.durationEcts: One full academic year / three consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer — summer is a 6–7 week term). 32–38 US credits total depending on internship and electives. Credits are US semester-hours, NOT ECTS — there is no published ECTS equivalence for this programme. Minimum B- grade and 3.00 GPA required.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, starting in the autumn (fall semester). No spring entry.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree; official transcripts (for non-US/Canadian institutions a third-party credential evaluation is required — SpanTran or Educational Credential Evaluators recommended, a real extra cost and lead time for a Tunisian transcript); statement of purpose 400–500 words in English; résumé/CV; ONE letter of recommendation, written in English and signed by the recommender, from a professional collaborator or supervisor. AN INTERVIEW IS REQUIRED — see auditionSpec.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CORRECTION — CONDITIONAL, NOT UNCONDITIONAL. The official Entrance Requirements page states verbatim: 'Music production, technology, and innovation applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music,' and 'Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship.' So a BSc Software Engineering is NOT disqualifying, but it is explicitly the exception route, and the burden shifts entirely onto proving 'a high degree of musicianship'. The same page names the desired traits as 'technological proficiency, musical excellence in performance and/or composition, leadership, motivation, intellectual curiosity'. His software-engineering background covers 'technological proficiency'; nothing in his file currently covers 'musical excellence'. This is a materially higher bar than a plain 'any bachelor's degree accepted'.
programs.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED on the official How to Apply page. Two components: (1) a self-produced video, MAXIMUM THREE MINUTES, 'describing three projects you feel passionate about'; (2) 'three recorded musical projects, audio or video files', with a description of his role in each. Everything must be 'organized in one PDF document with all links properly embedded' and sections clearly labelled — the page explicitly says 'Do not submit the materials as separate links'. Statement of purpose 400–500 words and one recommendation letter accompany this.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition — but an INTERVIEW IS MANDATORY. The official Interviews page states: 'An interview is required for entry into all of our graduate programs; applicants to the contemporary performance (production concentration) program must also complete an audition.' Interviews are held online, mid-November to early December for Early Action and end-January to early March for Regular Action. The admissions board probes four areas: readiness for the curriculum and alignment with Berklee's mission, professional and career goals, why Berklee, and how he will contribute to the Berklee network. (CORRECTION: the 3-minute video does NOT replace an interview.)
programs.englishTest: IELTS IS ACCEPTED and is the recommended test: IELTS 7.5 or higher. Also accepted: Pearson PTE Academic 73, Duolingo 120 (CORRECTION — the Duolingo bar is 120, not 130), Cambridge CAE / C1 Business Higher or above. TOEFL iBT: 100 for exams taken before 21 January 2026, and 5 on the new scale for exams taken on or after 21 January 2026 (per Berklee's central graduate eligibility page; the Valencia-specific page shows a lower TOEFL line of 80 / 4 — THIS DISCREPANCY IS UNRESOLVED and must be confirmed in writing with admissionsvalencia@berklee.edu before he books a test). Berklee institution code 3107. The requirement may be waived if the bachelor's was taught in English — he should check whether SMU MedTech's English-medium instruction qualifies, as that could remove the test entirely. He has NOT sat IELTS; 7.5 is a demanding target and must be booked and prepared for well before autumn 2026. NOTE: the published score set is now presented as a single institution-wide standard, NOT differentiated by programme.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the September-2027 entry cycle. Berklee does not publish an application-opening date; the portal normally opens in the late summer preceding the November Early Action deadline — so around August/September 2026 for a 2027 start.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The official deadlines page lists the recurring structure WITHOUT naming an entry year: Early Action — application 1 November, scholarship 15 November, decisions by 15 December. Regular Action — application 15 January, scholarship 1 February, decisions by 15 March. Extended Action — application 10 March, scholarship 10 March, decisions by 20 April. For a September 2027 start he would apply roughly November 2026 – March 2027. CRITICAL: the page states 'Scholarship application deadlines are different from the Program Application deadlines for Early and Regular action' — missing the separate scholarship date forfeits the money even if admitted.
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD $50,430 for the full one-year (three-semester) programme, academic year 2026/2027 — VERIFIED on the official tuition page. Per-credit rate $1,615.
programs.tuitionTotal: USD $50,430 total tuition for the entire programme (2026/2027 published figures). Berklee Valencia prices in US dollars, so he carries FX risk on a Tunisian-dinar or euro income. There is no separate non-EU rate — non-EU students pay the same tuition as everyone else.
programs.otherFees: ALL VERIFIED on the official tuition page: Application fee $150 (non-refundable; waived for Berklee alumni only). Non-refundable tuition deposit $2,500 to accept the offer (credited against the first tuition bill). Comprehensive fee $1,600 — mandatory, covers registration into the Spanish educational system, compulsory health insurance and campus services. Required software bundle for MPTI specifically: $800 (CORRECTION — the $200–$850 figure was the range across all four masters; MPTI's own line is $800; GEMB $200, Scoring $700, Contemporary Performance $850). The $2,990 Professional Recording Services fee applies to the SCORING programme ONLY — it does NOT apply to MPTI. Optional GradGuard tuition insurance is offered. Credential-evaluation fee for the Tunisian transcript (SpanTran / ECE) — amount UNVERIFIED, payable to the third-party evaluator, typically a few hundred dollars.
programs.equipmentRequired: Laptop — Berklee budgets $3,000 as an estimated indirect cost, and the page notes it 'may be waived' if he already has an adequate machine. Required MPTI software bundle $800. Books $300–$800. The curriculum runs Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools and Adobe Premiere.
programs.totalCostEstimate: CORRECTED. Building from Berklee's own published lines: tuition $50,430 + comprehensive fee $1,600 + MPTI software bundle $800 + laptop $3,000 (may be waived) + housing $10,000–12,000 + books $300–800 + local transport $300–600 + personal expenses $1,000 = approximately USD $67,430–$70,230 for the year, plus the $150 application fee. (The previously stated $69,380–$73,370 range was slightly overstated for MPTI because it used the top of the software range.) If the laptop is waived the floor drops to about $64,400. Roughly €58,000–€65,000 depending on the exchange rate. Add the credential-evaluation fee. This is by a very wide margin the most expensive option in this slice.
programs.paymentPlans: Tuition is divided into three equal parts and billed three times per year (once per semester) to his Berklee.edu address. The $2,500 deposit is credited against the first instalment. No published early-bird, referral or sibling discounts — all discounting at Berklee happens through scholarships.
programs.scholarships: VERIFIED on the official graduate scholarships page. Open to him: (1) Berklee General Scholarship — all master's applicants, amount varies, AUTOMATIC consideration via the Berklee Graduate Scholarship Application in the portal, deadline 15 November (EA) or 1 February (RA). (2) Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship — UP TO 50% OF TUITION, for 'demonstrated leadership or support for historically underrepresented or culturally diverse communities', explicitly including first-generation students; requires a SEPARATE submission — a video of max 3 minutes OR an essay of max 500 words to scholarshipsvalencia@berklee.edu via the portal — deadline 1 FEBRUARY (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). Combined awards are capped at 90% of tuition. (3) Berklee Outstanding Women Scholarships with Mentorship — up to 70% of tuition, one per programme including MPTI; the published eligibility is to 'support the musicianship and leadership of women in the music industry' — the programme name and framing indicate it is for women applicants, so he should not count on it; confirm with admissions if he wants certainty. NOT open to him: Alumni Scholarship $18,000 (Berklee alumni only); Global Partners Scholarship $18,000 (Berklee Global Partner schools only); Groove Scholarship (Contemporary Performance only); CACSA–Palau de les Arts (Valencian students only, deadline 1 April). REALISTIC BEST CASE: General Scholarship + Diversity Scholarship, up to 50% of tuition, and the Diversity award requires a separate essay/video on a separate earlier deadline.
programs.facilities: Purpose-built campus inside the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía in the Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències. Multiple state-of-the-art recording studios, a scoring stage, production suites, technology labs running Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools and Adobe Premiere, DJ/electronic performance facilities, and a strong programme of visiting industry artists. Berklee's brand recognition among producers, labels and festivals is the strongest of any institution in this slice.
programs.reputationSignals: Strongest global brand in contemporary music education; NECHE-accredited US degree. Positive structural signal: two sister programmes on the same campus DO carry ANECA verification via Universidad Politécnica de València, proving the campus can meet Spanish quality standards — but MPTI is not one of them. Extensive alumni network in production and electronic music. RED FLAGS for this candidate: (a) the price — roughly $70k all-in for one year; (b) the accreditation asymmetry, which is easy to misread; (c) the entry wording expects a music bachelor and admits others only on proven musicianship, which he does not yet have on paper.
programs.recommendation: The best programme in this slice on craft, network and visa safety, and the one most likely to actually launch an international DJ/producer career. But three verified facts sharpen the picture against him. First, the entrance wording is not the open door it looked like: 'applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music' and other disciplines are considered only 'provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship' — his three recorded projects must carry the entire application against a stated musicianship bar. Second, IELTS 7.5 is the recommended standard and he has not sat the test; he should first check whether an English-medium bachelor waives it outright, which would save months. Third, at ~$67,400–$70,230 for the year this is only defensible with a large scholarship. My candid verdict: apply ONLY if he (a) resolves the English-test question now and, if needed, books IELTS early and clears 7.5; (b) spends the next 12 months producing three genuinely strong recorded projects — this is the single highest-value thing he can do with 2026; (c) applies EARLY ACTION and submits the Diversity Scholarship video/essay by the SEPARATE 1 February scholarship deadline. Treat a full-price offer as a decline. And he must go in understanding that MPTI is a US degree, not a Spanish official master.
programs.valueVerdict: CONDITIONAL — outstanding craft, network and visa security, but a ~$70k one-year outlay for a US degree that is NOT an official Spanish/EHEA master; only worth it with a 50% Diversity Scholarship or better.
programs.verificationNotes: Tuition page, accreditation page, entrance requirements, how-to-apply, interviews, auditions, deadlines and scholarships pages all fetched and cross-checked. CORRECTIONS MADE: (1) acceptsNonMusic — official wording expects a MUSIC bachelor and admits other disciplines only on demonstrated 'high degree of musicianship'; the prior claim of no subject stipulation was wrong. (2) An INTERVIEW IS MANDATORY for all graduate programmes — the 3-minute video does not substitute for it. (3) MPTI software bundle is $800 specifically, not a $200–850 range. (4) Duolingo bar is 120, not 130. (5) Total cost estimate corrected down to $67,430–$70,230. (6) English requirements are now published as one institution-wide standard, not per-programme. OUTSTANDING ITEM: Valencia page shows TOEFL 80/4 while Berklee's central graduate page shows 100/5 — unresolved, confirm in writing. Entry-year for the deadline structure is not published, hence PRIOR CYCLE.

programs.program: Máster en Producción de Música Electrónica
programs.institution: SAE Institute Spain (SAE Creative Media Education)
programs.institutionType: Specialist audio academy — international chain (SAE Institute global network). SAE Barcelona additionally holds status as an authorised private higher artistic-education centre in music (Generalitat de Catalunya / AQU) — but that status attaches to its undergraduate degree, not to this master.
programs.qualification: DUAL AWARD, both non-official — CONFIRMED on the official course page: (1) 'Máster de Formación Permanente (25 ECTS)' accredited by UDIMA (Universidad a Distancia de Madrid, a private university), OR a 'Máster Profesional' route for applicants without a degree; plus (2) a Diploma Profesional from SAE Creative Media Education. Also includes an official Ableton Live certification via SAE's Ableton certifier partnership.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — this is a TÍTULO PROPIO. It is a 'Máster de Formación Permanente' issued under UDIMA's own authority: NOT a 'Máster Universitario Oficial', NOT ANECA-verified, NOT an EHEA official master, and it gives NO access to a Spanish doctorate. THE ECTS COUNT IS THE TELL: 25 ECTS. An official Spanish master is 60–120 ECTS. Marketing a 25-ECTS course as a 'máster' is legal in Spain for a título propio, but 25 ECTS is roughly a third of the smallest official master — this is a substantial certificate, not a degree. SEPARATE AND DO NOT CONFUSE: SAE Barcelona's UNDERGRADUATE Título de Grado en Música (240 ECTS, four specialities including Composición de Música Electrónica) IS official — authorised by the Generalitat de Catalunya and validated by AQU Catalunya, recognised within the EHEA. That is a genuine official award, but it is a BACHELOR-level degree he already has the equivalent of, and it is a completely different product from this master.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED — AND LIKELY PROBLEMATIC AS SOLD. SAE Spain publishes an international-students section covering 'Admisiones Internacionales' and 'Tu visa de estudiante', and the sister Audio Production page explicitly states a student visa is required for non-EU citizens, so the institution does handle international applicants. BUT: a 25-ECTS, 8-month, non-official título propio is a weak basis for a Spanish student visa, which normally expects a substantial full-time programme at a recognised centre. The programme's own accreditation status does not come from the officially authorised part of SAE Barcelona. HE MUST OBTAIN WRITTEN CONFIRMATION from SAE that THIS SPECIFIC programme generates a visa-supporting acceptance letter (carta de admisión) before paying anything. Do not accept a verbal assurance from an 'asesor educativo'.
programs.focus: Electronic music production, synthesis, sound design, live electronics, mixing and mastering, artist/industry management — the closest published match in Spain to this candidate's stated goal of DJ/electronic producer.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED on the official course page. First semester (fundamentals): sound theory, music theory, MIDI protocol, audio processing, synthesizers, sampling, recording, and mixing in Ableton Live and Logic Pro X, plus four practical projects. Second semester (advanced): advanced mixing and production, hardware and modular synthesis (Moog, Prophet/Dave Simth-lineage, Doepfer and similar), sound design, live performance, mastering, industry operations, and artist management and marketing. Includes the official Ableton Live certification.
programs.durationEcts: 8 months full-time, across two semesters. 25 ECTS on the Formación Permanente route.
programs.language: SPANISH. Instruction is in Spanish and the course page states Spanish-language proficiency is required. There is no English-taught route. This is a hard blocker for a Tunisian applicant with no Spanish — he would need roughly B1–B2 before an October 2027 start, i.e. about a year of dedicated language work starting now. (His French would help the learning curve considerably, but it does not substitute.)
programs.intakes: Two intakes per year. Currently published on the official page: Madrid — February 2026 and October 2026; Barcelona — October 2026 and February 2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the autumn 2027 intake is not yet published, but the pattern (February and October each year) makes an October 2027 start the realistic target, which is slightly later than his September 2027 goal.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED. For the UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente route: an official university degree — 'una titulación universitaria oficial (Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Arquitectura o Diplomatura)' or equivalent. Alternative 'Máster Profesional' route for those without a degree: 'al menos, 2 años de experiencia profesional' (at least 2 years of professional experience). Minimum age 16 for domestic students, 18+ for international students. Spanish-language proficiency. Process: complete an admission questionnaire and an interview with an educational advisor.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY. The published requirement is 'una titulación universitaria oficial (Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Arquitectura o Diplomatura)' with NO subject restriction whatsoever — an 'Ingeniería' is named directly, so a BSc in Software Engineering satisfies it head-on. No music degree, no conservatory training, no prior audio experience and no portfolio is demanded. This is by a wide margin the most accessible entry route in this slice for his exact profile, and the contrast with Berklee (which expects a music bachelor absent proven musicianship) is stark.
programs.portfolioSpec: NONE. No portfolio is published as a requirement. Admission is by an online admission questionnaire plus an 'entrevista de acceso' with an educational advisor. programs.englishTest: No IELTS or English test required — and no English-language route either. Instruction and admission are in SPANISH, and Spanish proficiency is a stated requirement for international students. His untaken IELTS is irrelevant here; the language cost is Spanish instead.

programs.scholarships: VERIFIED on SAE's official Becas y Ayudas page — and the finding is bad for him. The institutional discount schedule is: Excellence 60% (9.0+ average in Spanish Bachillerato, or 9.0+ across all first-year SAE modules); Active/Alumni students 40%; Gender-violence survivors 40%; Disability ≥33% 30%; Family members of enrolled students 20%; Large-family status 10%; Unemployment/ERTE 10%; Ukrainian refugee families 100%. NONE of these is stated to apply to master's/postgraduate programmes — the page's scholarships target non-university studies and the undergraduate Música degree. The government routes are also closed: MEC scholarships and the Generalitat de Catalunya 2026-2027 non-university grants (income €1,700, relocation €2,700, basic €300–350, academic merit €50–125) require Spanish residency/eligibility and are tied to SAE's Grado en Música, not this master — they are not open to a newly arrived non-EU student. The Yamaha Europe Foundation grant (€1,000–€2,000/year, musicians under 25 developing a professional music career) is the one award realistically open to him. NET REALISTIC SCHOLARSHIP: effectively zero beyond a possible Yamaha grant.
programs.facilities: Genuinely strong. Barcelona: 2,700 m², seven professional audio studios, a production studio with an ICON D-CONTROL digital console, three post-production suites with colour correction, MIDAS F-16 analogue routing stations, MIDI stations with analogue and digital synthesizers, and a cinema mixing suite with 7.1 JBL monitoring and surround panner. Madrid: Solid State Logic 4000G+ console and a RAVEN MTX II Slate Digital console. Official certification partnerships with Ableton, Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Cubase, Wwise, Autodesk and Adobe.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: SAE is a large, long-established international audio-school chain with serious studio infrastructure — the equipment list is among the best in this slice, and SAE Barcelona's undergraduate Título de Grado en Música is officially authorised by the Generalitat de Catalunya and validated by AQU, proving the institution can meet Spanish quality standards when it chooses to. RED FLAGS: (1) NO published price anywhere for a master-branded programme; (2) a 25-ECTS award marketed as a 'máster' — a third the size of the smallest official master; (3) UDIMA título propio branding that a non-Spanish applicant can easily mistake for an official university degree; (4) a generous-looking discount architecture that is, on inspection, almost entirely inaccessible to a non-EU newcomer and not stated to cover postgraduate programmes at all; (5) no portfolio and no selective admission, which caps the peer-group quality.
programs.recommendation: The best CRAFT fit in Spain for his stated goal, and the easiest door to walk through: it is literally an electronic-music-production master taught on Ableton Live, Logic and hardware synths, it demands no portfolio, and it names 'Ingeniería' as an accepted entry degree so his BSc qualifies outright. Three verified problems keep it out of first place. First, it is a 25-ECTS TÍTULO PROPIO, not an official Spanish master — he must never be sold it as a degree, and it will not support a PhD or any recognition process. Second, the price is published NOWHERE, which for a budget-sensitive self-payer is a serious governance problem: get the full written fee schedule, Offer Letter, Payment Plan and cancellation terms before engaging, and treat continued vagueness as a reason to walk. Third, it is taught in SPANISH and he has none — that is a year of language work before an October 2027 start, on top of the visa question. My verdict: pursue as a strong second option behind Berklee MPTI, but treat the unpublished fee AND written visa confirmation as hard blockers to clear before he invests any time in Spanish.
programs.valueVerdict: CONDITIONAL — the best craft match and the easiest admission for his exact profile, but the decisive reason for caution is that SAE publishes no price at all for a 25-ECTS non-official título propio, so he cannot know what he is buying.

RED FLAGS: complete absence of published pricing for a two-year, certainly five-figure commitment; UDIMA título propio branding easily misread as an official university master; a near-identical product name ('Programa Producción de Audio') at a published €14,000–€16,000 that is actually a different, undergraduate-level qualification; and a discount schedule that reaches neither postgraduates nor non-EU newcomers.

But it is the wrong craft for him. It trains studio, post-production, live-sound and game-audio engineers; it points at a career behind a console, not at the international DJ/producer career he says he wants. Add the unpublished price, the requirement to reach four-skill Spanish proficiency, and a two-year commitment that would not end until autumn 2029, and it ranks below the Electronic Music Production master on goal fit and below Berklee MPTI on career leverage.
