programs.program: Máster en Producción Musical Profesional
programs.institution: DJP Music School (título propio issued by UDIMA — Universidad a Distancia de Madrid)
programs.institutionType: Specialist DJ/electronic-music academy — independent private school issuing a partner university's título propio
programs.qualification: DJP Music School Diploma PLUS a UDIMA-issued título propio of 60 ECTS. VERIFIED on both DJP's and UDIMA's own pages.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — now verified with the exact legal wording. UDIMA's own programme page states: 'Título propio de la Universidad a Distancia de Madrid "Enseñanza no reglada y sin carácter oficial" (art. 7.c. Decreto 84/2004, de 13 de mayo, de la Comunidad de Madrid)'. DJP's page carries the parallel disclaimer 'enseñanzas no conducentes a la obtención de un título con valor oficial'. This is NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial: no ANECA verification, no EHEA official master status, no PhD access. UDIMA's RUCT registration covers the UNIVERSITY, not this title — the single most common trap in Spanish private education, and DJP's marketing leans on it.
programs.visaEligible: NO, ON HOURS — this is the decisive correction. Spain's estancia por estudios requires a course of MORE THAN 90 DAYS with a MINIMUM OF 20 CONTACT HOURS PER WEEK, delivered at least 50% in person. This programme runs Monday–Thursday 19:00–21:30 = 10 hours per week — exactly HALF the legal minimum. Important nuance that corrects a widespread misconception: títulos propios ARE an accepted study type for estancia por estudios, so the non-official award is NOT itself the problem; the timetable is. DJP does operate a real international-student service (djpmusicschool.com/comunidad/estudiantes-extranjeros) listing passport, 'Carta Certificación de matrícula otorgada por DJP Music School', medical insurance, proof of funds and housing, plus criminal-record and medical certificates for stays over 180 days; it warns 'DJP Music School no se hace responsable del resultado de la solicitud de visado' and refunds 60% of enrolment if the visa is refused. But it also tells applicants to 'confirmes el mínimo de horas que debes estudiar a la semana' with their consulate — DJP itself is pointing at the hours problem. That visa machinery almost certainly exists to serve DJP's FULL-TIME BA (Hons) and HND programmes, not this evening master.
programs.focus: Electronic and contemporary music production, DAW-centred, with live performance and music marketing — the closest content match in this batch to a DJ/producer career.
programs.whatYouStudy: Seven modules, VERIFIED on the programme page: (1) Producción en DAW; (2) Fundamentos Musicales Aplicados; (3) Composición Musical y Songwriting; (4) Síntesis y Diseño Sonoro; (5) Live Performance; (6) Mezcla y Mastering; (7) Marketing y Promoción Musical. Taught across Ableton Live, Logic Pro, FL Studio and Reaper. Includes mentoring, a virtual learning platform, and exclusive masterclasses with working producers.
programs.durationEcts: 9 months; 60 ECTS as issued by UDIMA. Note the ratio: 10 contact hours per week over 9 months is roughly 360 contact hours against a nominal 1,500 hours for 60 ECTS — the credit count is generous relative to actual teaching.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September. Published start for the current cycle: 21 September 2026.
programs.entryRequirements: Effectively none. UDIMA's description targets anyone interested in developing music production skills 'ya sea desde cero o desde un nivel intermedio' (whether from scratch or from an intermediate level), naming musicians, composers, producers, sound engineers and DJs. No degree, audition or portfolio prerequisite is published.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — open access, verified. UDIMA's wording 'desde cero' (from zero) explicitly admits complete beginners, and no prior degree is required. programs.auditionSpec: None.

programs.tuitionTotal: €5,900 (single payment) or €6,100 (instalments) for the entire 9-month programme. No separate non-EU rate is published — a Tunisian pays the same as a Spaniard, which is genuinely unusual and in his favour.
programs.otherFees: The €1,200 matrícula is charged on top of tuition and is already inside both totals above. No application, materials or exam fees are published. programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: an established Madrid DJ/production school that also runs an internationally validated HND and a BA (Hons) Electronic Music Production, which implies genuine external quality assurance; a real, quantified scholarship programme with published selection criteria; a dedicated and honest international-student page that discloses its own non-responsibility and the 60% refund rule; transparent pricing. RED FLAGS: UDIMA itself labels the award 'sin carácter oficial'; the 10-hours-a-week timetable cannot support a Spanish student visa; and 60 ECTS from roughly 360 contact hours is a generous credit-to-teaching ratio.

But do not build an immigration plan on THIS programme: at 10 contact hours a week it is half the 20-hour minimum Spain requires for a study residence permit, and DJP's own international page quietly tells applicants to verify their weekly hours with the consulate. The strategic move is to look at the SAME SCHOOL'S full-time BA (Hons) Electronic Music Production or HND in Music Production instead — same building, same staff, same discounts, same scholarship pool, but a full-time timetable that can actually carry a visa, an internationally validated British award rather than a Spanish título propio, and a much better fit for an applicant with no music degree who needs foundations rather than a postgraduate label. programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — and CEV effectively admits it. The Educaweb listing carries CEV's own programme description stating the master has 'no equiparación en la formación universitaria en España' — NO EQUIVALENCE TO SPANISH UNIVERSITY EDUCATION. That is about as explicit a disclaimer as a Spanish private school ever prints. So: no ANECA verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no EHEA status, no PhD access — a school diploma, a título propio in substance. IMPORTANT distinction he must hold onto: CEV genuinely DOES deliver officially accredited qualifications — its Técnico Superior en Sonido para Audiovisuales y Espectáculos is a real Grado Superior homologated by the Ministerio de Educación y Formación Profesional. But that is a VOCATIONAL, SUB-DEGREE award, and its officialness does not transfer to this master. The school's homepage claim that its qualifications are 'homologados por el Ministerio' refers to the FP catalogue, not to this programme.
programs.visaEligible: PLAUSIBLE ON STRUCTURE, UNCONFIRMED IN PRACTICE — and structurally the best of this batch. At 1,200 hours over one academic year, this works out to roughly 30 contact hours a week over a 40-week year, comfortably clearing Spain's 20-hours-per-week minimum, and it is fully in-person in Madrid, clearing the 50%-presencial rule, over a course far longer than 90 days. Spanish rules accept non-official private courses for estancia por estudios provided the centre is authorised and those thresholds are met, and CEV IS an authorised centre for its FP programmes. However, CEV publishes NOTHING about non-EU student visas, and the Oficina de Extranjería can refuse a visa where the specific course is not homologated — which this one is not. Structurally promising, but he must obtain written confirmation and, ideally, ask CEV to name a current non-EU student on this exact programme.

A candidate with no instrumental training and no conservatory background starts those two modules from zero alongside classmates who do not. Of the five programmes in this batch, this is the most conventionally musician-oriented and the worst match for his profile. programs.program: Máster en Producción Musical Discográfica e Ingeniería de Sonido — Oficial de AVID (MPD)
programs.institution: CICE — La Escuela Profesional de Nuevas Tecnologías
programs.institutionType: Private technology and creative-industries training school; authorised vendor-certification centre (Avid, Waves)
programs.qualification: A CICE private professional certificate branded 'Máster', bundled with software-vendor certifications (Avid Pro Tools, Waves Level A). No university validation, no ECTS, 300 teaching hours.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — and the naming is actively misleading. The word 'Oficial' in the title 'Máster ... - Oficial de AVID' means OFFICIAL AVID CERTIFICATION, a software-vendor credential, NOT Spanish academic accreditation. There is no ANECA verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no EHEA status and no PhD access. Independent confirmation of its nature: the Emagister listing describes the outcome as conferring professional specialisation status 'rather than an academic degree'. It is a private certificate course. The decisive new number is the DURATION: 300 teaching hours (with roughly 600 hours of total student dedication). A genuine 60-ECTS master implies about 1,500 hours. At 300 taught hours this is one-fifth the size of the cheapest real master in this batch — it is a short course wearing the word 'máster'.
programs.visaEligible: NO. At 300 teaching hours with 'fechas a elegir' (self-chosen scheduling), this cannot deliver the 20 contact hours per week over more than 90 days that a Spanish estancia por estudios requires — 300 hours at 20 h/week is only 15 weeks, and CICE's flexible-dates model means it is typically taken at a far lower weekly intensity. It is also offered FULLY ONLINE, and an online course carries no visa value whatsoever (Spain requires at least 50% in-person). Nothing about non-EU student visas is published anywhere by CICE. Treat as a definitive no.
programs.focus: Record production and sound engineering: sound capture, processors, mixing architecture, mastering and genre-specific mixing, wrapped around vendor certification. Studio-engineering oriented, NOT DJ or electronic-music oriented.
programs.whatYouStudy: Ten modules, VERIFIED: (1) Sound and Capture; (2) Processors and Production Phases; (3) Capture History and Advanced Techniques; (4) Analysis Keys for Productions; (5) Introduction to Mixing and Mastering; (6) Mixer History and Studio Performance Optimisation; (7) Mixing Architecture; (8) Dynamic Control and 3D Depth Mixing; (9) Official Waves Level A Certification; (10) Mixing According to Musical Styles. Note what is ABSENT: no synthesis, no sound design, no composition, no live performance, no DJ technique, no music business.
programs.durationEcts: 300 teaching hours, with approximately 600 hours of total student dedication. No ECTS published. NEWLY VERIFIED — the input recorded duration as entirely unknown.
programs.language: Spanish, with 'elementary English competency' listed as an entry requirement.
programs.intakes: 'Fechas a elegir' (dates chosen by the student) — a flexible, rolling model rather than a cohort intake. The Emagister listing currently shows enrolment CLOSED for the in-person Madrid option. Available both in-person in Madrid and fully online.
programs.entryRequirements: Published prerequisites are technical, not academic, and VERIFIED: 'Conocimientos de Sistema Operativo Mac, nivel usuario'; 'Conocimientos de Protools u otra plataforma similar, nivel usuario'; and basic English proficiency. No degree requirement of any kind is stated.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — trivially. No academic or music prerequisite exists at all; the bar is Mac OS and Pro Tools user-level familiarity, which a software-engineering graduate clears immediately. But read this the right way: a programme with NO degree requirement whatsoever is not a postgraduate qualification in any meaningful sense, whatever it is called.

The Emagister listing states the certifications are included, naming both the 'Certificación Oficial de Waves Level A' and official AVID certification as part of the programme. A separate source indicated the price includes Waves Level A but NOT the Avid Pro Tools certifications. As a route to Spain the figure is moot — it cannot support a visa, so Madrid living costs do not arise. As a skills purchase for someone already resident: €4,200–€6,000 all in.

programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: long-established Madrid technology-training school; genuine authorised-certification status with Avid and Waves; forum discussion of its sound programmes is broadly positive on value for money and teaching staff. RED FLAGS, and they are serious: the 'Oficial de AVID' naming reads as academic accreditation and is not; the programme is only 300 taught hours yet is marketed as a 'máster'; published prices are stale and inconsistent across aggregators (one listing still advertises a May 2018 start); the school's own website is not publicly reachable for verification; certification exam inclusion is ambiguous; and an online delivery option is sold under the same 'máster' name with zero visa or campus value.
programs.recommendation: AVOID as anything to do with his move to Spain. This is a 300-hour vendor-certification bootcamp with the word 'máster' attached and the word 'Oficial' borrowed from Avid's marketing rather than from ANECA. It cannot support a student visa — 300 hours cannot produce 20 contact hours a week over 90+ days, and it is sold online as readily as in person. It is also aimed at the wrong craft: pure studio engineering, with no synthesis, no sound design, no composition, no live performance and no DJ content anywhere in the ten modules. For a software engineer who wants Pro Tools and Waves credentials cheaply it has genuine, narrow utility — but that is a €4,000 skills purchase for someone already living in Madrid, not a postgraduate route into Europe for a Tunisian graduate. If he ever does pursue it, insist first on a current written price stating exactly which certification exams are included, because the advertised figure already carries a 17% discount and the exam bundling is contradicted between sources.

programs.program: Postgrado en Producción Musical y Artística (with Warner Music Spain) — NOT A MASTER
programs.institution: Universidad Francisco de Vitoria (UFV) in collaboration with Warner Music Spain
programs.institutionType: Private university postgraduate school with a major-label industry partner
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO of Universidad Francisco de Vitoria — a 30-ECTS POSTGRADO (postgraduate certificate), VERIFIED on UFV's own page. EXPLICITLY NOT A MASTER: at 30 ECTS over 3 months it is half the size of even a minimal 60-ECTS master and a quarter of a 120-ECTS official one.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. A título propio issued by UFV, a private university — not a Máster Universitario Oficial, not ANECA-verified, no EHEA official master status, no PhD access. Credit where due: UFV does NOT oversell it. The programme is correctly and prominently called a 'Postgrado', not a 'Máster', which is more honest naming than CICE, CEV or DJP manage. The risk here is not deception by the school; it is that the Warner Music branding leads an applicant to over-read what a 30-ECTS certificate is worth.
programs.visaEligible: NO — this fails on two independent counts, both now verified. First, the timetable: Monday to Friday 18:00–20:00 is 10 contact hours per week, exactly half Spain's 20-hour minimum for an estancia por estudios. Second, the size: 30 ECTS over three months of evening classes is a certificate, not a course of study an Oficina de Extranjería would treat as full-time. (The programme does run September to January, so it clears the 90-day duration test — but duration alone is not enough.) Note the nuance that matters generally: título propio status would NOT by itself have blocked a residence permit, since Spain accepts títulos propios for estancia por estudios; it is the 10-hour week that is fatal. He must not treat this as a route into Spain under any circumstances.
programs.focus: Music production and artistic direction with direct exposure to Warner Music Spain professionals.
programs.whatYouStudy: Practical training in composition, editing, mixing and artistic direction, with direct collaboration opportunities with Warner Music Spain professionals. VERIFIED inclusions: official Avid Pro Tools certification at PT101 and PT110 levels, a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence for every student, and 6 hours of dedicated Ableton training.
programs.durationEcts: 3 months; 30 ECTS. Monday to Friday, 18:00–20:00 — 10 contact hours a week.
programs.intakes: One published intake: September 2026 – January 2027.
programs.entryRequirements: 'Formación o experiencia previa en música o sonido' — prior TRAINING OR EXPERIENCE in music or sound, stated as preferred rather than absolute. Targeted at musicians, composers, producers and audio technicians, plus audiovisual and media professionals moving into music production. Places are deliberately limited because of the practical, personalised format. Admission runs through the postgraduate team: +34 91 709 14 24 or +34 649 24 00 74, postgrado@ufv.es, named contact Patricia Pérez Merino.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY. The bar is 'training OR experience in music or sound', not a music degree — so a self-taught producer with a credible body of work can qualify, and the requirement is framed as preferred rather than mandatory. But a candidate with neither training nor experience would not clear it. His software-engineering degree is irrelevant either way; what would carry him is a genuinely developed portfolio, which he does not yet have. He would need roughly a year of serious output first.
programs.portfolioSpec: None formally published, but with limited places and a prior-experience expectation, work will be assessed informally at admission.
programs.auditionSpec: None published. Admission is handled by the postgraduate admissions team with a named advisor rather than by audition.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS and no English requirement. Taught in Spanish.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling until the limited places fill.
programs.deadline: No published deadline; limited places for the September 2026 start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for a September 2027 edition, which has not been announced.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €6,100 headline total for the 3-month programme. UFV's own page prints the components verbatim as 'Reserva de plaza: 960€' and 'Honorarios de matrícula: 5.540€'.
programs.tuitionTotal: €6,100 as headlined by UFV. ARITHMETIC DISCREPANCY CONFIRMED, not a transcription error on our side: the two components UFV publishes sum to €6,500, which is €400 MORE than the €6,100 total UFV advertises. Both figures appear on UFV's own page. Ask UFV in writing which number he would actually be invoiced. No separate non-EU rate is published.
programs.otherFees: The €960 reserva de plaza is included in the headline total. No application, materials or exam fees are published. Genuinely and unusually included: Avid Pro Tools PT101 + PT110 official certification, a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence, and 6 hours of Ableton training — collectively worth several hundred euros and unusually transparent.
programs.equipmentRequired: A laptop is implied. Crucially, the two biggest software costs are covered by the fee: Avid Pro Tools PT101+PT110 certification and a perpetual (not subscription) Ableton Live 12 Suite licence. This is the ONLY programme in the batch that bundles a perpetual DAW licence — a genuine asset he would keep permanently regardless of what the certificate is worth.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €6,100 (or possibly €6,500 — see the discrepancy) in fees for three months, plus roughly €3,000–€4,500 in Madrid living costs for that period, plus a laptop. Around €10,000–€12,500 all in — for no visa, no master, and 30 ECTS.
programs.paymentPlans: A €960 reserva de plaza followed by €5,540 in honorarios de matrícula. No instalment schedule, early-bird or referral discount is published. UNVERIFIED whether the reserva is refundable.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published for this postgrado, and nothing specific to non-EU applicants. UFV's page contains no becas section at all for this programme.
programs.facilities: In-person at the UFV Madrid campus, with direct collaboration with Warner Music Spain professionals — the single strongest named industry partnership in this batch, and a genuinely checkable one.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: the Warner Music Spain partnership is a real, verifiable major-label link rather than vague marketing; UFV is an established private university; the inclusion of Pro Tools certification and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence signals a school that expects students to actually work; and the naming ('Postgrado', not 'Máster') is honest, which cannot be said of most competitors here. RED FLAGS: the published cost components (€960 + €5,540 = €6,500) contradict the advertised €6,100 total, confirmed verbatim on UFV's own page; 10 contact hours a week; and 30 ECTS at €6,100 is the highest cost per credit in the batch — roughly €203 per ECTS against DJP's €98.
programs.recommendation: The best industry connection in this batch and refreshingly honest about what it is — but it cannot be his plan. It is THREE MONTHS, 30 ECTS and 10 evening hours a week: it will not carry a Spanish student visa, it is not a master, and at €6,100 it costs almost as much as a full 9-month master elsewhere, at roughly double the cost per credit. He also does not currently meet the stated 'training or experience in music or sound' entry expectation. I have listed it precisely so the Warner Music branding does not tempt him into treating a certificate as a degree. Where it genuinely shines is as a LATER add-on: if he is already legally resident in Spain — say, after a full-time programme that does carry a visa — this is an excellent three-month investment for the Warner-adjacent network, the Pro Tools certification and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence he keeps forever. One thing to do before paying anything: ask UFV to reconcile €960 + €5,540 = €6,500 against the €6,100 they advertise, and get the answer in writing.
programs.verificationNotes: UFV's official programme page fetched twice, including a targeted re-check of the pricing block. CONFIRMED: Título Propio, 30 ECTS, 3 months, Monday–Friday 18:00–20:00, September 2026 – January 2027 intake, Spanish-language, Madrid campus, Warner Music Spain collaboration. CONFIRMED verbatim: 'Reserva de plaza: 960€' and 'Honorarios de matrícula: 5.540€' against an advertised €6,100 total — the €400 arithmetic discrepancy flagged in the input is REAL and reproducible on UFV's own page, not a transcription error. CONFIRMED inclusions: Avid Pro Tools PT101+PT110 official certification, perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence, and 6 hours of Ableton training (the 6-hour training detail is new). CONFIRMED entry requirement wording and named admissions contact (Patricia Pérez Merino, postgrado@ufv.es). VISA ASSESSMENT HARDENED from a general judgement to a specific legal test: Spain requires >90 days AND ≥20 contact hours per week with ≥50% in-person delivery for estancia por estudios; at 10 h/week this fails on hours regardless of its título propio status — and the título propio status alone would NOT have been disqualifying, which corrects a common misreading. UNVERIFIED: refundability of the €960 reserva, any scholarships, and whether a September 2027 edition will run.

programs.program: Máster Profesional en Producción Musical (título propio, delivered in person by DJP Music School)
programs.institution: UDIMA — Universidad a Distancia de Madrid
programs.institutionType: Private online university that badges private specialist schools' programmes (DJP Music School, SAE Institute Spain) with its own título propio
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO. CONFIRMED VERBATIM on udima.es: the award is a "Título propio de la Universidad a Distancia de Madrid", classified as "Enseñanza no reglada y sin carácter oficial" under Decreto 84/2004 of the Comunidad de Madrid. DJP's own page repeats it: these are "enseñanzas no conducentes a la obtención de un título con valor oficial". 60 ECTS are awarded, but they are título-propio ECTS.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — and stated as such by the awarding university itself, in plain Spanish, on its own programme page. This is NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial, is NOT ANECA-verified, carries no EHEA official status, and gives no access to a Spanish or European doctorate. VERIFIED that the same UDIMA badge sits behind several Madrid private-school 'masters', including SAE Institute Spain's four music/audio masters (SAE-UDIMA agreement confirmed on sae.edu) and DJP's Máster en Producción Musical. THE DECODER RULE, now confirmed at source: when a Spanish 'máster' is described as accredited/awarded by UDIMA, or as a 'Título Propio', or as a 'Máster de Formación Permanente', it is the institution's OWN diploma. Only the exact phrase 'Máster Universitario Oficial' denotes an official Spanish degree.
programs.visaEligible: NO / VERY WEAK, and unchanged after verification. Two independent problems. (1) UDIMA is a distance university and the award is expressly non-official, so the UDIMA route offers nothing a consulate would treat as full-time official study. (2) The actual teaching is done by DJP Music School, a private academy, on an evening schedule of Monday to Thursday 19:00–21:30 — CONFIRMED on DJP's page. That is roughly 10 contact hours a week, far below the ~20 h/week full-time threshold Spanish practice expects for an estancia por estudios. Neither UDIMA nor DJP publishes anything about non-EU student visa support. A Tunisian applicant should treat this as not a viable visa basis.
programs.focus: Music creation, music theory and composition, sound design, implementing music in live performance, an introduction to mixing and mastering, and digital marketing for music promotion.
programs.whatYouStudy: Seven modules, CONFIRMED on both the UDIMA and DJP pages: music creation; musical theory and composition; sound design; implementation of music in live settings; introduction to mixing and mastering; and digital marketing / music promotion. Note the wording — mixing and mastering is an 'introduction' only. For someone who wants to work as a producer this is broad-but-shallow, and the technical depth a software engineer would find satisfying is not there.
programs.durationEcts: 9 months, 60 ECTS (título-propio credits) — CONFIRMED on the DJP page. UDIMA's own page still does not state duration or ECTS, which is itself telling.
programs.language: Spanish. In-person delivery at DJP's Madrid premises, Monday to Thursday 19:00–21:30.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, in September. The DJP page gives a start date of 21 September 2026 for the current cycle. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 target: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (expect a comparable mid/late-September 2027 start, but it is not published).
programs.entryRequirements: No formal academic prerequisite is published. UDIMA describes the audience as anyone "interesado en desarrollar habilidades en la producción musical, ya sea desde cero o desde un nivel intermedio" — from scratch or from an intermediate level — naming musicians, composers, producers, sound engineers and DJs. DJP publishes no entry requirements at all. Open access.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — unambiguously. The published wording "ya sea desde cero o desde un nivel intermedio" ("whether from scratch or from an intermediate level") explicitly admits complete beginners. His BSc in Software Engineering is no obstacle; equally, no academic screening happens at all, which is a quality signal in itself.
programs.portfolioSpec: None published by either UDIMA or DJP. No portfolio is required — convenient given his portfolio is unfinished, but it also means no selection is taking place.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, interview or practical test is published.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS and no English-language route. Teaching is entirely in Spanish, so functional Spanish is the real language barrier. Nothing about DELE or any Spanish-proficiency evidence is published either.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published. DJP operates rolling enrolment until the September cohort fills. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for 2027.
programs.deadline: No published deadline — enrolment runs until places are filled for the September start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionPerYear: VERIFIED on the DJP page (UDIMA publishes no price at all): €1,200 matrícula/enrolment, PLUS EITHER €4,700 in a single payment OR 10 monthly instalments of €490. Single-payment route: €5,900. Instalment route: €1,200 + €4,900 = €6,100.
programs.tuitionTotal: €5,900 paying in full, or €6,100 across instalments, for the whole 9-month programme. UDIMA itself publishes no price — every figure here comes from DJP Music School.
programs.otherFees: No application fee, materials fee or insurance charge is published. The €1,200 matrícula is separate from and additional to the tuition figure, so do not read €4,700 as the total. UDIMA contact: informa@udima.es, (+34) 918 561 699. DJP contact: info@djpmusicschool.com, (+34) 91 819 5390.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published. Assume a capable laptop and a DAW licence at minimum; headphones and a controller in practice. Budget €1,000–€2,000 on top if he arrives with nothing.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €5,900–€6,100 in fees, plus roughly €1,000–€2,000 for laptop/DAW/hardware, plus Madrid living costs of about €900–€1,200 per month over 9 months (€8,100–€10,800). Realistic first-year outlay: €15,000–€19,000 — for a certificate with no official status and no visa basis.
programs.paymentPlans: CONFIRMED: after the €1,200 matrícula, either a single payment of €4,700 or 10 monthly instalments of €490. No early-bird discount, no scholarship and no non-EU concession is published.
programs.scholarships: None published, by either UDIMA or DJP. Nothing available to a Tunisian or other non-EU applicant.
programs.facilities: Taught in person by DJP Music School at Calle Pilar de Zaragoza 63, Madrid. Compulsory for international students, per ESCAC's own guide: medical insurance, repatriation insurance and civil liability insurance. Budget several hundred euros a year for those. Contact for the programme: Nacho Moliné, nacho.moline@escac.es; general info@escac.es, +34 937 361 555.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published. ESCAC provides the professional facilities, so the personal outlay should be limited to a capable laptop and headphones — unusually, the school's own equipment is the selling point rather than something he must buy.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €27,000 tuition over two years, plus insurance, plus Barcelona-area living costs of roughly €1,000–€1,300 per month over two years (€24,000–€31,200). Realistic all-in total: €52,000–€60,000. First year alone: €26,000–€30,000.
programs.paymentPlans: None published. No instalment schedule, early-bird discount or scholarship appears on the programme pages — a notable omission at €13,500 a year. Ask directly.
programs.scholarships: None published. Nothing identified for a Tunisian or other non-EU applicant.
programs.facilities: GENUINELY EXCELLENT and the strongest facilities in this batch by a distance: Dolby Atmos mixing stages in 7.1.4 and 9.1.4, Pro Tools Ultimate suites, AVID S4 consoles, a dedicated music, foley and ADR recording studio, and a recording complex with analogue consoles and high-end monitoring. Students work on real ESCAC productions from year one. Campus at Plaça de la Farinera 9, 08222 Terrassa — a commuter town roughly 30 km outside Barcelona, not the city itself, which matters for living costs, nightlife and the electronic-music scene he wants to be part of.
programs.reputationSignals: ESCAC is genuinely prestigious in Spanish cinema, is attached to the Universitat de Barcelona and holds several real ANECA-accredited official masters — a strong institution by any measure, and the facilities here are the real thing rather than marketing. RED FLAGS specific to this programme: it is a título propio at official-degree prices; it is absent from ESCAC's published masters index and marketed only through separate landing pages, which makes it hard to verify and is why it was previously thought dormant; no payment plan or scholarship is published at €13,500 a year; and no visa pathway for direct-entry non-EU students is documented anywhere.
programs.recommendation: The input treated this as possibly discontinued and unverifiable. That is now CORRECTED — the programme is live, current and considerably bigger and more expensive than assumed: two years, €13,500 a year, €27,000 total, starting 14 September 2026, with Dolby Atmos 7.1.4 and 9.1.4 stages and Pro Tools Ultimate. It is a serious film-sound school with facilities that outclass everything else in this batch. My verdict is still AVOID, for four reasons that stack. It is FILM sound — location recording, ADR, foley, post-production mixing — not music production, and after two years and €27,000 he would be qualified for exactly the career he is not pursuing. It is a título propio, so €27,000 buys ESCAC's own diploma, not an official Spanish degree, with no PhD access and an undocumented visa position. It requires a portfolio of projects and a 3-minute video pitch that he cannot currently produce. And it is taught only in Castellano, in Terrassa rather than Barcelona. Worth knowing it exists: if he ever pivots to film and audiovisual sound — a field with far steadier employment than DJing — this is one of the best-equipped places in Spain to learn it, and he should email nacho.moline@escac.es. For an international DJ and electronic-music producer, it is the wrong €27,000.

programs.program: Máster de formación permanente en Música y Sonido para Experiencias del Entretenimiento
programs.institution: ENTI-UB — Escola de Noves Tecnologies Interactives (centro adscrito a la Universitat de Barcelona)
programs.institutionType: Private school operating as an attached centre (centro adscrito) of the Universitat de Barcelona. Legal operator: U.COLLEGE OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES, S.L.
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO de máster issued by the Universitat de Barcelona. Exact published name: 'Máster de formación permanente en Música y Sonido para Experiencias del Entretenimiento'. 60 ECTS. VERIFIED nuance, quoted verbatim from ENTI's own live page: 'Al finalizar los estudios del Máster de Música se obtiene un título propio de máster expedido por la Universitat de Barcelona, el único en el ámbito de la producción musical en Cataluña. En caso de no disponer de un título de grado oficial, al finalizar el máster se obtendrá un certificado.' He holds a BSc, so he would receive the máster diploma, not the lesser certificate.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — confirmed explicitly. This is a 'Máster de formación permanente' / 'título propio' of the Universitat de Barcelona. Under the Spanish system a máster de formación permanente is by definition NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial: no ANECA/AQU verification, no official EHEA master status, no automatic access to a Spanish doctorate, and no automatic professional recognition. What it does carry is the Universitat de Barcelona's name — a major public university — which places it at the strong end of the título propio spectrum, well above a pure private-school certificate. But the legal standing gap versus La Salle's Máster Universitario in this same batch is enormous, and he must not confuse the two.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED. Structurally a strong case — 1 year, 60 ECTS, in-person, afternoon schedule, at a UB-attached centre — and Spanish student visas can be granted for título propio programmes at recognised centres. However ENTI publishes NOTHING on non-EU student visas, and its 'Relaciones internacionales' section does not address visa sponsorship. This must be confirmed in writing before any payment.
programs.focus: Music and sound for entertainment experiences: video games, apps, serious games, newsgames, gamification, simulators, theme-park music, music for live shows and performances, scenic devices, and music/sound in virtual reality. The most technology-forward music master in this batch and the closest to his software-engineering background.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED full module list from ENTI's live plan de estudios — substantially richer than previously recorded: Notación musical; Guion interactivo y musical; Técnicas de grabación; Logic Pro; Unity & Unreal (audio integration for AAA and indie projects); Música en el cine; Audio inmersivo (physics of spatial sound plus a creative immersive recording/production project); Pro Tools; Diseño sonoro (complete game audio pipeline — dialogue, ambience, effects, music, through to implementation in a real game); MIDDLEWARE — FMOD and Wwise, taught to the official course syllabi so the student can act as audio editor on any project using these engines; Luthería digital (designing and building digital musical instruments); Mezcla y masterización (including broadcast standards); Historia de la música interactiva; Ableton; Proyecto (compose an original string-quartet work, optionally with electronics, PREMIERED BY PROFESSIONAL PERFORMERS in a major Barcelona auditorium); Propiedad intelectual (record industry, publishing, licensing, self-management); TFM; Prácticas (professional internships). The FMOD/Wwise middleware and luthería digital modules were not previously captured and are exactly where his programming background becomes an asset.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year; 60 ECTS. In-person, afternoon schedule (horario de tarde). Runs October to June.
programs.language: Spanish — '100% español' per the UB masters portal. This is the hard gate: there is no English track.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, October. VERIFIED on the live page: 'Inicio: octubre del 2026'.
programs.entryRequirements: ENTI's own live page states: 'Si bien no hay requisitos mínimos de estudios previos, sí que es necesario pasar una entrevista con el director académico del máster para acceder.' A mandatory interview with the academic director is the gate; the interview is requested by email. NOTE A DISCREPANCY: the Emagister listing states a prior degree (Grado, Licenciatura, Diplomatura, Máster, Posgrado, Doctorado) IS required. ENTI's own wording is the authority — no minimum prior study, but without an official bachelor's you receive only a certificate. He has a bachelor's, so this is moot for him.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, emphatically. VERIFIED quote from the live page: 'Los perfiles recomendados son diversos: graduados/des y estudiantes con conocimientos de música, DESARROLLADORES/SE, productores/se musicales, técnicos de sonido, estudiantes de cine, artistas multimedia, compositores/se, intérpretes musicales y creadores/se de espectáculos vinculados a la música.' Developers are named as a target profile in second position. Of every programme across this slice, this is the one whose stated intake most directly matches a software engineer moving into audio — his BSc is a differentiator here, not a gap to excuse.
programs.portfolioSpec: No formal portfolio specification is published anywhere on the official page. The academic director's interview is the sole assessment mechanism. He should nonetheless arrive with production work, since the interview is the only filter.
programs.auditionSpec: Mandatory personal interview with the master's academic director, requested by email. No performance audition.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS and no English requirement — the programme is taught 100% in Spanish. Spanish proficiency is the real and only language gate, and no specific DELE level is published. He should confirm what Spanish level the director expects at interview.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling / matrícula abierta, via interview request to the academic director by email. No formal opening date is published.
programs.deadline: No published deadline; admission runs until places are filled. The October 2026 cycle is live now. For a SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 start: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note the previously recorded concern that the listing showed a stale October 2023 date is now RESOLVED and INCORRECT — ENTI's live page reads 'Inicio: octubre del 2026' and the site footer reads '© 2026 ENTI-UB'. The programme is unambiguously still running, and a graduating-cohort news item confirms it.
programs.tuitionPerYear: NOT PUBLISHED by ENTI. VERIFIED refusal to publish — the official page says only: 'Para consultar el precio del Máster de formación permanente en Música y Sonido para Experiencias del Entretenimiento, se puede hacer rellenando este formulario y se recibirá toda la información sobre precios, tasas y formas de pago.' INDICATIVE THIRD-PARTY FIGURE: the UB-affiliated masters portal unportalmasters.barcelona lists €7,570. This is a SINGLE third-party source, unconfirmed by ENTI, and every other aggregator (Educaweb, Emagister, Aprendemas) says 'precio a consultar'. Treat €7,570 as an order-of-magnitude estimate only, not a quotable price.
programs.tuitionTotal: Approximately €7,570 for the full 60-ECTS programme IF the single third-party figure is accurate — UNCONFIRMED by the institution. Refusing to state this as verified.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. No application, enrolment, materials, insurance or exam fees are published. ENTI's own wording promises information on 'precios, TASAS y formas de pago' on request — the explicit mention of 'tasas' (fees) implies charges beyond tuition exist. He must ask for the itemised list.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED as a hard requirement. The syllabus spans Logic Pro, Pro Tools, Ableton Live, Unity, Unreal, FMOD and Wwise. Unity, Unreal, FMOD and Wwise all have free/indie tiers, so the real cost is a capable laptop (Mac strongly implied by Logic Pro) plus Logic (~€230 one-off), Ableton Live (~€350-€600) and Pro Tools (subscription ~€300/yr). Budget €2,000–€3,500 for laptop plus licences unless the school provides lab machines — ENTI does state school workstations and studios are available to students.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIABLE with confidence. IF the €7,570 third-party figure holds: roughly €7,570 tuition + unknown tasas + €2,000–€3,500 equipment + Barcelona living costs of approximately €12,000–€15,000 for the year = an indicative first-year outlay of €22,000–€26,000. Every element of this except living costs needs written confirmation from ENTI.
programs.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — none published. ENTI's contact form promises 'formas de pago' details on request, so plans do exist; the terms are simply not public. Emagister notes third-party coaching to help 'financiar tu matrícula en cómodos plazos', which implies instalments are available.
programs.scholarships: NONE — this is now a VERIFIED NEGATIVE, upgraded from unverified. ENTI's becas page states its scholarship plan is expressly for the GRADOS UNIVERSITARIOS only ('disponemos de un plan de becas para los grados universitarios (videojuegos, producción musical y ciberseguridad)'). The four awards — ENTI Excelencia €2,500, ENTI Solidario €2,250, ENTI Comunidad €2,000, ENTI Movilidad €450 — are NOT available to master's students. They also require empadronamiento and family financial documentation, which is structurally aimed at residents in Spain. Deadline for the grado awards is 14 June, 23:59. Bottom line: he should assume ZERO scholarship support from ENTI for this master and budget full self-pay.
programs.facilities: Barcelona, Campus Diagonal. Software stack: Logic Pro, Pro Tools, Ableton Live, Unity, Unreal, FMOD, Wwise. School workstations and studios are available to students for practice ('Las estaciones de trabajo de la escuela y los estudios están disponibles'). Named faculty of twelve including four PhDs (Enric Guaus PhD, Israel David Martínez Espinosa PhD, Serena Russo PhD) — an unusually credentialed teaching staff for a título propio. All students undertake internships at partner companies; Sony Music and Medusa Estudio are named among them. The final project is premiered by professional performers in a major Barcelona auditorium. Detailed studio inventory still UNVERIFIED.
programs.reputationSignals: STRONG POSITIVES: the Universitat de Barcelona affiliation is the single best institutional signal of any título propio in this slice; a named faculty including four PhDs; guaranteed internships with named industry partners (Sony Music, Medusa Estudio); a professionally-performed final project in a major auditorium; and genuinely distinctive, commercially current content (FMOD/Wwise middleware and immersive audio are exactly what the games audio industry hires for). ENTI itself claims it is 'el único en el ámbito de la producción musical en Cataluña' and 'único a nivel europeo'. RED FLAGS, all real: (1) the price is deliberately not published, which is a negotiating-asymmetry tactic and makes budgeting impossible; (2) NO scholarships whatsoever for master's students — confirmed, not merely unfound; (3) it is a título propio, so it will not get him into a PhD and carries no official EHEA status; (4) Spanish-only instruction; (5) no published visa guidance. The previously flagged concern about a stale 2023 date is RESOLVED — the programme is current and running.
programs.recommendation: This is still the best INTELLECTUAL fit for him in Spain, and verification made the case stronger on content and weaker on money. The curriculum is richer than it first appeared — FMOD and Wwise middleware taught to official syllabi, digital instrument building, immersive audio, full game-audio implementation pipeline — and it explicitly recruits developers. His software-engineering degree would be a genuine differentiator here rather than something to explain away, and as a bachelor's holder he gets the full UB diploma rather than the certificate. But three verified facts should temper his enthusiasm. First, ENTI will not publish a price; the only figure in circulation (€7,570) comes from one third-party portal. Second, and this is new and firm: there are NO scholarships for master's students at ENTI — the entire becas programme is restricted to undergraduate degrees. He should plan for full self-pay with no institutional support. Third, it is a título propio, so it closes the PhD door and carries no official standing. Practical advice: email ENTI first, before anything else in this batch, and ask four specific questions — the 2027-28 total price including all tasas, the payment plan terms, whether they will support a non-EU student visa application, and what Spanish level the director expects. If the price lands near €7,500 and the visa answer is yes, this is a serious contender. Be aware it leans toward games, film and immersive/screen audio rather than club and DJ culture — it will make him an employable audio professional, not an international DJ.
programs.verificationNotes: ENTI's own page blocked WebFetch with HTTP 403 but was retrieved successfully via direct HTTP request with a browser user-agent, so ALL programme facts here are now first-party and current, not second-hand. Verified directly from ENTI: título propio / máster de formación permanente wording, the certificate-vs-diploma distinction, 60 ECTS, October 2026 start, the full module list, the developer-inclusive target profile, the mandatory director interview, no minimum prior study, the price-on-request policy, and the scholarship restriction to grados. Cross-checked against Educaweb, Emagister, Aprendemas and unportalmasters.barcelona. The €7,570 tuition figure comes from unportalmasters.barcelona ALONE and is explicitly NOT confirmed by ENTI. Prior-cycle concern about a 2023 start date is disproven. Visa policy, itemised fees and payment plans remain genuinely unpublished.

programs.program: Máster en Diseño de Sonido Cinematográfico (film and audiovisual sound design)
programs.institution: ECIB — Escuela de Cine de Barcelona
programs.institutionType: Private film school
programs.qualification: A PRIVATE SCHOOL CERTIFICATE. The award described on the Educaweb listing is 'Curso de Diseño de Sonido Cinematográfico por ECIB' — a CURSO, not a máster — even though ECIB markets the programme under the name 'Máster en Diseño de sonido de cine y sonido audiovisual'. No ECTS, no validating university and no official award are published for this programme.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. No ANECA or AQU verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no official Spanish award of any kind. This is ECIB's own certificate. The gap between the marketing name ('Máster') and the award actually described ('Curso ... por ECIB') is precisely the discrepancy pattern he must learn to spot. NOTE A FURTHER UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY: the Docenzia aggregator describes ECIB 'máster' programmes generically as 1 year / 60 ECTS, but does not list the sound design programme at all, and no ECTS figure appears on any listing specific to this course. Two sources also give conflicting durations — Educaweb says 248 hours plus filming practice, while ECIB's own marketing says 500 hours including internships. Neither is reconcilable with a 60-ECTS master (which implies roughly 1,500 hours of student workload).
programs.visaEligible: NO / VERY DOUBTFUL. The published schedule is Mondays and Tuesdays, 16:00–20:00 — eight contact hours per week. Spanish student visas for long-stay study generally require a full-time programme of at least 20 hours per week. A part-time evening course of 248 contact hours cannot reasonably support a Spanish student visa for a non-EU national, and ECIB publishes no visa guidance.
programs.focus: Narrative sound design for film, television series, animation and documentary — from script analysis through location recording to final mix. This is film post-production sound, not music production.
programs.whatYouStudy: Five theory-practice modules following the phases of film sound: initial treatment of sound in the script; selection of materials and technical equipment in pre-production; capture and recording of sound on set; and editing and mixing in final post-production. Includes hands-on work on professional-standard short films and documentaries plus internships on real film productions. VERIFIED addition: students work with Avid Pro Tools as the reference program, and ECIB states it guarantees an INDIVIDUAL ANNUAL LICENCE for each student — a genuine and quantifiable benefit worth roughly €300.
programs.durationEcts: CONFLICTING SOURCES. Educaweb: 248 hours of classes plus filming practice hours. ECIB's own marketing: 500 hours including internships. No ECTS published under any source. Schedule: Mondays and Tuesdays, 16:00–20:00 — eight contact hours per week, part-time.
programs.language: Spanish (castellano). Taught entirely in person in Barcelona.
programs.intakes: UNVERIFIED — no start dates are published on any accessible page. ECIB's own site blocked all automated access.
programs.entryRequirements: Deliberately open. VERIFIED from the Educaweb listing: students aged 17 and over, from Spain or internationally, with or without prior audiovisual or sound experience; cinema enthusiasts welcome. No degree of any kind is required.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — completely open access. No degree, no music background and no prior experience required. But note the flip side: open access means the qualification carries no selection signal whatsoever, and therefore no market value as a credential.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. No portfolio and no prior experience are required.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS and no English requirement. Taught in Spanish, so Spanish proficiency is the real gate.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published deadline anywhere. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for any 2027 start.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. Listed as 'Consultar precio' / 'A CONSULTAR' on every aggregator checked (Educaweb, Docenzia, Aprendemas). ECIB's own site returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and a direct browser-user-agent request, so the price could not be read at source. NO price figure exists in the public domain for this programme. Refusing to estimate.
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED — no published figure from any source.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. Note that the Pro Tools annual licence is stated to be INCLUDED, which is a genuine cost offset of roughly €300 per year.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED as a hard requirement. Pro Tools licence is provided by the school. A laptop should be assumed. ECIB states it provides access to sound software, direct-sound recording equipment, audio control systems and its studio.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — no price is published anywhere in any source read, and the school actively blocks automated access to its own pages. This opacity is itself a warning sign for a programme with no accreditation.
programs.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — none published.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published, and nothing specific to non-EU applicants.
programs.facilities: VERIFIED and better than expected: ECIB provides access to a range of sound software, direct-sound recording equipment, audio control systems, and a NEW SOUND STUDIO WITH A DOLBY ATMOS 7.4.1 SYSTEM. Each student is guaranteed an individual annual Avid Pro Tools licence. Practical work on professional-standard short films and documentaries plus internships on real film productions. ADDRESS DISCREPANCY RESOLVED: ECIB's current published address is C/ Roger de Flor 7, Barcelona (metro L1 Arc de Triomf). The older C/ Girona 54 address appears only in stale listings and should be disregarded.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVES: ECIB is an established Barcelona film school; the Atmos 7.4.1 studio is a real, high-spec facility that few private schools have; the included per-student Pro Tools licence is concrete value; and the on-set and internship components are genuine practical experience. RED FLAGS, and they are serious: (1) 'Máster' marketing against a 'Curso' award; (2) NO price published anywhere, and the school blocks automated access to its own site; (3) no ECTS and no accreditation of any kind; (4) a part-time 8-hours-per-week schedule with no student-visa value for a non-EU national; (5) conflicting published durations (248 vs 500 hours); (6) only 2 aggregator reviews of the school overall, averaging 3.0/5, one of which reads 'No está preparado'.
programs.recommendation: Wrong discipline, wrong structure, wrong level — skip it. This is film post-production sound, not music production or DJing, and nothing in it moves him toward an international DJ or producer career. Structurally it is disqualifying regardless of content: eight contact hours a week cannot support a Spanish student visa, so as a non-EU national he could not legally relocate to Barcelona on this programme at all. Add no accreditation, no ECTS, no published price, a school that blocks its own pages from being read, and marketing that calls a 'curso' a 'máster', and the verdict is straightforward. The Atmos 7.4.1 studio and the free Pro Tools licence are real assets and would matter to someone already living in Barcelona who wanted film sound — that person is not him. Keep it on the list only as a worked example of the 'private certificate marketed as a máster' pattern he must learn to recognise before he spends money.
programs.verificationNotes: The programme EXISTS and the sourceUrl is CORRECT and live — confirmed via search result titles ('Máster en Diseño de sonido de cine y sonido audiovisual | ECIB'). However ECIB's own site returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch AND to a direct request with a full browser user-agent, on both the primary and the alternate URL, so no first-party page could be read. NEWLY RESOLVED: the address ambiguity — Roger de Flor 7 is current. STILL UNRESOLVED: price (nowhere in the public domain), start dates, ECTS, and the 248-vs-500 hour conflict. Rated Partial rather than Verified because no first-party source could be opened and the single most decision-relevant fact — the price — remains completely unavailable.

programs.program: Diploma de Producción Musical (2 years) — NOT A MASTER, undergraduate level
programs.institution: Escuela Microfusa (Microfusa Formació, S.L.)
programs.institutionType: Specialist audio, music production and DJ academy, with UK university progression partnerships
programs.qualification: Microfusa's own DIPLOMA — an UNDERGRADUATE-LEVEL award, not a master and not a postgraduate qualification. Its function is to feed into Level 6 (the third and final year) of a UK BA/BSc (Hons) at Solent University or the University of Winchester. VERIFIED: Microfusa's current catalogue also offers 'Diploma + Bachelor of Science in Popular Music Production (Solent)' and 'Diploma + Bachelor of Arts in Music and Sound Production (Winchester)' as packaged routes.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL in Spain. A private school diploma with no ANECA verification, no ECTS and no Spanish official status. Its recognised value derives entirely from the UK progression agreements with Solent University and the University of Winchester, which are genuine and checkable — but the end product of that route is a BRITISH BACHELOR'S DEGREE, not a Spanish master. DECISIVE FOR THIS CANDIDATE: he already holds a BSc. Spending two years and roughly €12,700–€13,500 to earn a route into the final year of ANOTHER bachelor's degree is a lateral or backwards move, not progression.
programs.visaEligible: LIKELY on structure, but UNVERIFIED in fact. This is a two-year, full-time, in-person programme (Monday to Friday, 5–6 hours per day) at an established school, which is exactly the profile Spanish student visas are designed for. However Microfusa publishes NO visa guidance on any page read, and as a non-accredited private school it has no automatic authority to host non-EU students. Must be confirmed in writing.
programs.focus: Music production, DAW craft, songwriting, studio recording, mastering, sound design and music business, with an explicit electronic and contemporary orientation.
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1: fundamentals of digital creation — DAWs (Ableton Live, Logic Pro), music production, songwriting, production analysis and branding. Year 2: advanced studio techniques, mastering, Pro Tools, sound design and music-business fundamentals. Specialisation tracks exist: the catalogue lists Diploma plus artistic, technological, or music-business specialisations. School workstations and studios are available to students for practice, allocated according to coursework needs.

The craft content and the Pioneer DJ / Ableton orientation sit close to what he wants, the school is reputable, and the pricing is published with unusual honesty. But he already holds a BSc, and this diploma exists to route students into the FINAL YEAR of a UK bachelor's. Spending two years and roughly €13,000 in tuition (€39,000–€47,000 all-in with living costs) to end up with a qualification at or below the level he already has makes no sense as a primary plan. Three corrections he should carry forward. First, the real 2026-27 prices are €6,360 advance or €6,760 monthly per year — not the figures previously circulating. Second, there is NO 8.6% APR; the cost of paying monthly is simply the €400 discount he forgoes. Third, the monthly plan needs a Spanish bank account he will not have on arrival, so he must ask for the unpublished 3-payment route. Separately CONFIRMED: the Microfusa 'Máster en Producción Musical' that still circulates on aggregator sites does NOT appear anywhere in Microfusa's current catalogue — the full product listing shows diplomas, courses, certifications and UK bachelor's routes, but no máster at all. As a portfolio-building step ahead of a real master's application in a later cycle, the Curso de Producción Musical is the smartest cheap option in this slice.

programs.program: Máster Universitario en Acústica, Audio y Vibraciones (Master of Science in Acoustics, Audio and Vibrations)
programs.institution: La Salle Campus Barcelona — Universitat Ramon Llull (URL). Legal entity: Fundació Privada Universitat i Tecnologia (FUNITEC).
programs.institutionType: Private university — Universitat Ramon Llull is a private but fully official Spanish university
programs.qualification: MÁSTER UNIVERSITARIO OFICIAL — an official Spanish university master's degree. 60 ECTS, structured as 10 modules of 5 ECTS each plus a 10-ECTS final thesis.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — and this is the decisive distinction in this entire batch. This is a Máster Universitario of Universitat Ramon Llull, a private but fully official Spanish university whose degrees are ANECA/AQU-verified. It is valid across the EHEA, gives access to a Spanish doctorate, and carries full official professional standing. It is the direct counterexample to every título propio and private certificate in this batch: same private sector, completely different legal standing. Of the five programmes here, this is the ONLY one that is a real degree.
programs.visaEligible: YES — and now backed by documentary evidence rather than inference. An official Máster Universitario at a recognised Spanish university is the cleanest possible basis for a Spanish student visa and subsequent residence permit. VERIFIED CORROBORATION: La Salle's admissions terms contain an explicit visa-denial clause — 'Visa denial: the reservation of the place will be reimbursed, except for €300 for administrative expenses. The presentation of supporting documentation is required.' A school only writes that clause if it routinely admits non-EU students who apply for visas. The admissions process also explicitly requires a PASSPORT 'for international students'. This is as safe as it gets.
programs.focus: Acoustics, audio engineering, audio signal processing and vibrations — an ENGINEERING master, not a creative music-production one. Covers noise and vibration control, environmental acoustics, sound quality enhancement and audio system optimisation.
programs.whatYouStudy: 60 ECTS across 10 modules of 5 ECTS plus a 10-ECTS thesis. Verified module examples: 'Métodos numéricos para bajas frecuencias: FEM y BEM' (5 ECTS), 'Métodos numéricos para altas frecuencias' (5 ECTS), and 'Temas avanzados en acústica, audio y vibraciones' (5 ECTS). This is finite-element and boundary-element numerical modelling, applied physics and signal processing — mathematically demanding engineering work. Taught partly at the IASLab (Interactive Laboratory of Arts and Sciences). Classes are held on weekday afternoons with some online sessions.
programs.durationEcts: 10 months, 60 ECTS. In-person, weekday afternoons, with some online sessions. 30 places available.
programs.language: ENGLISH — now VERIFIED, resolving the previous uncertainty. The programme is taught entirely in English. (One aggregator, Lectiva, implies Spanish; La Salle's own page and its launch announcement both confirm English. The official source is authoritative.) This is a major advantage for him: no Spanish requirement, unlike every other programme in this batch.
programs.intakes: One intake per year. VERIFIED start date: 19 October 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED — and this is a significant correction that works AGAINST him. La Salle publishes a closed list of accepted bachelor's degrees: Mechanical Engineering, Telecommunications Systems Engineering, Industrial Technology Engineering, Audiovisual Systems, Physics, Aerospace Vehicle Engineering, Mathematics, and Civil Engineering — 'or equivalent'. SOFTWARE ENGINEERING AND COMPUTER SCIENCE ARE NOT ON THE LIST. His BSc in Software Engineering would have to be argued in under the 'or equivalent' clause, and admission is NOT assured. Admissions process: register at admissions.salleurl.edu, submit passport plus a copy of the university degree (compulsory for university masters) and optionally a CV; a personal interview may be required at the committee's discretion; decision within 8 days of complete documentation; place reservation payable within 15 days of acceptance.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, and inverted from the rest of this batch: this programme WANTS an engineering, physics or mathematics background and has no interest in a music one. No portfolio, no audition, no musical training required. BUT — see entryRequirements — 'engineering' here means mechanical, telecom, industrial, aerospace or civil engineering, physics or mathematics. Software engineering is conspicuously absent from the published list. He is closer to the target profile than any musician would be, but he is NOT automatically eligible, and the heavy FEM/BEM numerical-methods content suggests they expect strong applied-physics and continuum-mechanics preparation that a software engineering curriculum typically does not provide.
programs.portfolioSpec: None — no portfolio is required for an engineering master. Documents are passport, university degree certificate, and an optional CV.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.englishTest: UNVERIFIED — and this is a genuine gap. The programme is taught entirely in English, but La Salle's requirements page publishes NO English proficiency threshold and names no accepted test. IELTS is therefore neither confirmed nor excluded. Given he has not yet taken IELTS, he must ask admissions directly what English evidence they require and what minimum score. Do not assume none is needed.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling — 'The admission process is kept open until the number of places available is covered.' With only 30 places, early application matters. No fixed opening date.
programs.deadline: No fixed application deadline; admission closes when the 30 places fill. Binding downstream deadlines once accepted: place reservation payable within 15 days of acceptance; 14 calendar days of statutory withdrawal rights from contract; cancellation requests must be made at least 90 days before the programme starts. Current published cycle starts 19 October 2026. For a 2027 intake: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date and new prices.
programs.tuitionPerYear: VERIFIED EXACTLY — €11,940 for the full programme, published in La Salle's official 2026-27 price list under ICT Engineering and Computer Science: 'Master of Science in Acoustics, Audio and Vibrations: 11.940 €'. This was previously UNVERIFIED and is now a hard figure. For context within La Salle's own 2026-27 on-site range (€10,380 to €17,940), this sits at the lower-middle end. NOTE: Spanish private universities charge non-EU and EU students the same tuition, unlike public universities, so €11,940 is his actual price.
programs.tuitionTotal: €11,940 total for the whole 60-ECTS programme (it is a single 10-month year). Before any scholarship — see below, since a scholarship could cut this substantially.
programs.otherFees: Place reservation fee — amount not separately published, but it FORMS PART OF the total master's cost and is not an extra; the visa-denial clause retaining €300 implies it is at least €300. €500 surcharge if he changes his start date to a different intake ('change of call'), payable within 15 days of written notification. No separate application fee is published. Payments can be made internationally via Flywire. Materials, insurance and exam fees are not published — ask admissions for the itemised list.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED. A laptop should be assumed. Acoustics measurement software and the IASLab facilities are presumably provided; specialist FEM/BEM software licences are normally supplied by the university under academic licence. Confirm whether any purchase is expected.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €11,940 tuition (before scholarship) + a €500 contingency if he changes intake + laptop, say €1,500–€2,500 + Barcelona living costs of roughly €12,000–€15,000 for 10 months. Realistic first-year total: approximately €26,000–€30,000. WITH a 40% Academic Excellence or Impulso scholarship, tuition drops to about €7,164 and the all-in figure falls to roughly €21,000–€25,000 — which would make it competitive with ENTI's título propio while delivering an actual official degree.
programs.paymentPlans: YES, verified in principle though not in detail. After the place reservation, the balance is payable as: a first pre-enrolment payment before the course starts, a second payment, then either a single lump sum before the start or 'payments in instalments, according to the schedule set by the University'. The exact instalment schedule and amounts are not published and must be requested. International payments are handled through Flywire. Statutory 14-day withdrawal with full refund; refunds outside that window exclude the reservation fee except on visa denial or course cancellation.
programs.scholarships: YES — REAL, SUBSTANTIAL AND PLAUSIBLY AVAILABLE TO HIM. This is a major upgrade from the previous 'UNVERIFIED / none found'. La Salle runs 30+ aid schemes; the ones relevant to a non-EU self-funding applicant are: ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE — 50% for a GPA of 9.5 or above (max 2 per programme), 40% for GPA 8.5 or above (max 4 per programme), 20% for GPA 8.0 or above (max 3 per programme); IMPULSO ('Boost') — 10% to 40% based on academic record combined with financial need; PARTNER UNIVERSITY — 15% for graduates of any of 90+ partner institutions (he should check whether SMU MedTech Tunisia is among them); LASALLIANS — 10% for alumni of any La Salle school or university worldwide. Nothing in the published terms restricts these to EU citizens, though the two 100% foundation awards (Massó, Casa de México) are nationality- or programme-restricted and would not apply to him. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: 'Different scholarships, discounts, and financial aid options cannot be combined' — he gets one, not several. Applications are made during the admission process, with decisions following programme acceptance. ACTION: he should convert his Tunisian BSc grades to the Spanish 10-point scale before applying; if he lands at 8.0 or above, a 20–40% reduction on €11,940 is realistically in play, worth €2,388–€4,776.
programs.facilities: La Salle Campus Barcelona, C/ Sant Joan de La Salle 42, 08022 Barcelona. Teaching at the IASLab (Interactive Laboratory of Arts and Sciences). Acoustics and audio laboratories. Only 30 places, so small-cohort teaching. Detailed equipment inventory still UNVERIFIED. Admissions contacts for this programme: Sardor Abdullaev +34 937 372 093, Iona Marie Lafont Amado +34 937 372 082; general admissions admissions@salleurl.edu, +34 93 290 24 19.
programs.reputationSignals: Universitat Ramon Llull is one of Spain's most respected private universities, and La Salle Barcelona has a long track record in audiovisual and telecommunications engineering, including an established Grado en Ingeniería Audiovisual. The official Máster Universitario status is the key signal and is what separates this from everything else in the batch. Institutional maturity is evident in the admissions terms — statutory withdrawal rights, a formal visa-denial refund clause, Flywire international payments, published price lists, and a 30+ scheme scholarship programme. NEW RED FLAG, and he should weigh it: this is a BRAND-NEW PROGRAMME launching in the 2026-27 academic year — La Salle announced it alongside two new AI masters. He would be in the first or second cohort ever, which means no graduate outcomes data, no alumni network, no track record, and the usual first-run teething problems. SECOND RED FLAG: he may not meet the published entry requirements at all (see entryRequirements). Neither is a quality concern about the institution; both are real risks for him specifically.
programs.recommendation: This remains the ONLY programme in the private-sector Spanish audio landscape that would give him an official, ANECA-standing, EHEA-valid, PhD-eligible master's degree with a clean student-visa path — and verification has made it considerably more concrete and, in one respect, more doubtful. THE GOOD NEWS: the price is now known and is more reasonable than feared at €11,940, only modestly above ENTI's indicative €7,570 for a qualification in a completely different legal class; it is taught entirely in ENGLISH, so his lack of Spanish is not a barrier here as it is everywhere else in this batch; real scholarships of 20–50% exist and are plausibly within reach if his GPA converts to 8.0 or above, which could bring tuition to €7,000–€9,500; and the formal visa-denial refund clause is documentary proof they routinely handle non-EU students. THE BAD NEWS, and he must not skip it: Software Engineering is NOT on the published list of accepted bachelor's degrees. La Salle names Mechanical, Telecommunications Systems, Industrial Technology, Audiovisual Systems, Physics, Aerospace, Mathematics and Civil Engineering 'or equivalent'. The previous assessment that his degree makes him a natural fit was too confident — he would be arguing his way in under an equivalence clause, against a syllabus heavy in FEM/BEM numerical methods and applied physics that a software engineering curriculum does not typically prepare him for. He should email Sardor Abdullaev or Iona Lafont with his transcript BEFORE investing any hope here, and ask three questions: does a BSc in Software Engineering qualify, what English evidence and minimum score do they require, and what scholarship would his converted GPA attract. Note too that this is a brand-new programme with no graduates yet. MY CANDID VERDICT IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE: this is the safest qualification and the worst match for his stated dream. It is acoustics and audio ENGINEERING — noise control, environmental acoustics, numerical modelling — and it will not, by itself, make him an international DJ. It is worth serious consideration only if he decides he wants an official credential and a legal foothold in Europe first and a music career second. That is a legitimate strategy and deserves to be put to him explicitly — but he should now also know he might not be eligible for it.

programs.qualification: VERIFIED from the official studies page. Official awards: Grado en Enseñanzas Artísticas Superiores de Música; Máster en Interpretación Musical; Máster en Composición Dramática y Ensemble Instrumental; Máster en Interpretación Musical Avanzado; Advanced Artist Diploma; Diploma de Postgrado en Estudios Avanzados de Dirección de Orquesta. programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL for the Grado and the Másteres — but note this is NOT ANECA. Reina Sofía's official titles are 'enseñanzas artísticas superiores', authorised and supervised through the Ministerio de Educación / Comunidad de Madrid artistic-education framework, and are legally equivalent to Grado/Máster within the EHEA. Its school-issued Diplomas de Postgrado and Estudios Preliminares are explicitly flagged by the school itself as NON-OFFICIAL. Since no programme here is in this candidate's subject area, the distinction is moot for him — but it is worth knowing the school is transparent about which of its awards are official and which are not, which is more than many Spanish private schools manage.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an official Grado/Máster at an authorised Spanish higher-education centre supports a student visa/residence permit. MOOT here: he cannot pass the audition because he has no classical instrument.
programs.focus: Elite classical instrumental, vocal, composition and orchestral-conducting performance training.
programs.whatYouStudy: Not applicable. VERIFIED ABSENT: no production, mixing, sound design, electronic music, live electronics or studio-engineering curriculum of any kind. The entire provision is cátedra-based classical instrumental/vocal tuition plus chamber music and orchestra.
programs.durationEcts: Not applicable to this search. (Grado is 4 years; the Másteres are official artistic-education masters.)
programs.language: CORRECTED — the draft said 'Spanish/English'. The school's OFFICIAL LANGUAGE IS SPANISH. Non-Spanish speakers receive an intensive Spanish course in their first year, and for the official Grado and Máster students must have Spanish sufficient to follow the curriculum. English is not an alternative medium of instruction.
programs.intakes: One audition cycle per year, auditions held in person in Madrid.
programs.entryRequirements: Three phases: (1) online registration; (2) preselection — a Selection Committee reviews the academic record plus submitted audiovisual material; (3) in-person audition in Madrid. 'El único criterio de selección es el talento del candidato' — talent is the sole stated criterion. Documentation required: two academic references (instrument professor and academic director), motivation letter, artistic biography (max 900 characters), repertoire pieces, language certificates if held. Approximately 6% admission rate. Open to candidates of all nationalities.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — categorically not, and there is no wording to quote because the concept does not arise: entry is by cátedra audition on a classical instrument or voice, with two academic references required from an instrument professor and an academic director. A BSc Software Engineering graduate with no conservatory training and no classical instrument has nothing to submit at the preselection stage.
programs.portfolioSpec: Preselection requires two RECENT recordings in contrasting styles, at least one accompanied by live piano, plus an optional third video showing other musical activities. Composition applicants additionally submit previous works with scores and recordings. This is a classical-repertoire video submission, not a production portfolio — a DJ mix or Ableton project would not be assessable.
programs.auditionSpec: In-person audition at the school's Madrid headquarters before the professors of the relevant cátedra, after passing preselection. ~6% admission rate.
programs.englishTest: Not applicable — no IELTS requirement. The relevant language barrier is SPANISH, not English.
programs.applicationOpens: For the 2026/2027 cycle registration ran 23 October to 17 December 2025. PRIOR CYCLE — expect the 2027/2028 window to open around late October 2026 and close mid-December 2026; confirm on the school's Inscripción page.

programs.otherFees: CORRECTED — the draft omitted two real fees. A TUNISIAN NATIONAL IS NOT ELIGIBLE for this stream.
programs.facilities: Elite conservatory facilities in Madrid with internationally distinguished faculty, cátedra system, chamber-music and orchestral programmes.

Entry is by in-person cátedra audition at roughly a 6% admission rate, preceded by a preselection that requires two classical recordings with live piano accompaniment and two academic references from an instrument professor and an academic director — none of which he can produce. The extraordinary finances (free tuition, €45,000 scholarships) are irrelevant to him.
