programs.program: 1-Week and 2-Week DJ/Producer courses, and 1-Week DJ Skills (Ibiza) — NOT A MASTER, short intensive summer courses
programs.institution: Point Blank Music School (Ibiza campus, operated by pointblank Limited, a company registered in England)
programs.institutionType: International chain — UK private music school (London / Los Angeles / Online / Ibiza) running a seasonal summer campus in Ibiza. The contracting entity is pointblank Limited, registered in England, trading address 23-28 Penn St, London N1 5DL.
programs.qualification: NO ACADEMIC QUALIFICATION. The Ibiza course pages name no certificate, no diploma, no ECTS and no validating body — they list only duration, timetable, fees and start date. Whatever completion document is issued (if any) has no Spanish academic status. NOT a master, NOT a postgraduate award. Point Blank's genuine degrees and Certificates of Higher Education are UK-validated products delivered in London / Online, and are a separate offering from the Ibiza summer courses.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL in Spain — verified by absence. Nothing on the Ibiza course pages, the Ibiza location page or the Ibiza terms and conditions claims Spanish accreditation, ECTS, university validation or recognition by any Spanish authority. These are commercial short courses. Point Blank's UK degree provision does not extend any status to the Ibiza campus.
programs.visaEligible: NO — and this is confirmed in Point Blank's own Ibiza terms and conditions, which state: 'pointblank Ibiza welcomes students from all over the world. If you are applying from a non-EU country, you may require a student visitor's visa which entitles you to study in Spain. Responsibility for securing any required visa (including meeting criteria) rests with the individual student and pointblank shall have no liability for applications that are unsuccessful.' CRITICAL RISK: the same clause continues 'Where an international student has not been successful in securing a visa, the deposit (referred to in Clause 3 below) will not be returnable, though the balance of the course fees will be refunded.' So a Tunisian national who is refused a Schengen visa LOSES the £100 or £200 deposit. A one or two-week course cannot support a Spanish student residence permit under any circumstances.
programs.focus: DJing on Pioneer DJ equipment and electronic music production in Ableton Live, with opportunities to play out at Ibiza venues. The most directly DJ-career-relevant training found anywhere in this slice — but it is training, not education at any level.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED from the course pages. Level 1 (beginners, supported by Pioneer DJ): production fundamentals — making beats with drums, basslines and chords; recording audio into Ableton Live; editing with effects such as compression and reverb; mixing your tracks; plus DJ skills — tempo and cueing, beatmatching, EQing and effects, creative mixing, looping and set preparation. Level 2 is 'designed for those of you who have already mastered the basics (or who have graduated from the Ibiza DJ/Producer Course - Level 1 or similar)' and covers beat matching, looping, harmonic mixing, effects, plus sound design, sidechaining, synthesis, warping, slicing, mixing and mastering. 26 hours of tuition per week, comprising classroom time plus the DJ experiences playing out at venues. Timetable Monday to Friday roughly 10:00-15:00 including a lunch hour (listed as TBC).
programs.durationEcts: 1 week or 2 weeks. NO ECTS. Five distinct products verified: 1 Week DJ/Producer Level 1, 1 Week DJ/Producer Level 2, 2 Week DJ/Producer Level 1, 2 Week DJ/Producer Level 2, and a standalone 1 Week DJ Skills course.
programs.intakes: Summer season only (July-August). Verified 2026 start dates: 1 Week and 2 Week DJ/Producer Level 1 both start 17 August 2026; 1 Week and 2 Week DJ/Producer Level 2 both start 31 August 2026; DJ Skills start date listed as TBA with a 27 July timetable. All PRIOR CYCLE relative to a 2027 plan.
programs.entryRequirements: None published for Level 1 — no qualification, no audition, no portfolio. Level 2 requires 'those of you who have already mastered the basics (or who have graduated from the Ibiza DJ/Producer Course - Level 1 or similar)'. Under-18s need parent/guardian permission per the terms and conditions.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — completely open. Nothing on the Level 1 pages states any academic or musical prerequisite; the course is explicitly 'designed to give beginners a fantastic start in the world of production and DJing'. A BSc Software Engineering is irrelevant either way.
programs.portfolioSpec: None.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS or any English test required. The course is 'taught in English by professional DJ/Producers'. Booking is commercial, not an academic admission.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling bookings for the summer season; no academic application cycle.
programs.deadline: No academic deadline — booking-based, with places sold until full. Payment deadline is contractual: full payment must be received at least FOURTEEN (14) DAYS before the course starts. On discounts: an 'IBIZAEARLY' code for 20% off was extended to 30 November 2025, and an 'IBIZA26' code for 20% off ran until 25 May 2026. BOTH PRIOR CYCLE — but the pattern is consistent, so expect an equivalent 20% early-bird code for summer 2027, likely announced in late 2026. Booking early on a code is the single biggest saving available here.
programs.tuitionPerYear: Not annual — these are one and two-week products, priced in POUNDS STERLING not euros, so currency conversion and card fees apply on top for a Tunisian buyer. 1 Week DJ/Producer (Level 1 or Level 2): £1,145. 1 Week DJ Skills: £1,145. 2 Week DJ/Producer (Level 1 or Level 2): £1,695.
programs.tuitionTotal: CORRECTED — the draft said '£1,195 (1 week)'. The verified published price is £1,145 for every one-week course (DJ/Producer Level 1, DJ/Producer Level 2 and DJ Skills), and £1,695 for both two-week courses. Prices as published for the 2026 season; 2027 pricing is not yet posted, so treat these as indicative. A 20% early-booking code has been offered in each of the last two cycles, which would bring two weeks to roughly £1,356.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED — the deposit is NOT £200 for both. Verified: one-week courses take a £100 registration fee plus a £1,045 balance; two-week courses take a £200 registration fee plus a £1,495 balance. THE DEPOSIT IS NON-REFUNDABLE IN ALL CIRCUMSTANCES, including visa refusal. Not included and not published: flights from Tunis, accommodation (partner-hotel discounts are offered but the rates are not published), Ibiza living costs in peak summer, travel to the venues (students 'are asked to make their own way to the venues'), and a Schengen short-stay visa application fee for a Tunisian national. No insurance or materials fee is charged.
programs.equipmentRequired: None mandatory — Pioneer DJ industry-standard equipment and Ableton Live are provided at the academy. Students do receive substantial software discounts: 50% off Native Instruments Komplete, Ableton Live and Roland Cloud, and 40% off Serato DJ. Owning Ableton Live would help him continue afterwards, and that discount is worth real money.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Two weeks: £1,695 tuition (or roughly £1,356 with a 20% early-bird code), plus flights Tunis-Ibiza, plus peak-summer Ibiza accommodation which can easily exceed the tuition, plus a Schengen visa fee and the documentation burden that comes with it. Realistically £3,000-£5,000 all-in for two weeks. Very high cost per contact hour, but the only credential-free route into the Ibiza scene on this list.
programs.paymentPlans: CORRECTED — there is NO payment plan. The Ibiza terms and conditions state explicitly: 'Payment by instalments is not possible for pointblank Ibiza Can Blau music courses.' The two-part structure (registration fee then balance) is a booking deposit, not an instalment plan: full payment including the non-refundable deposit must be received at least 14 days before the course starts. Cancellation with less than 14 days' notice leaves the full fee payable, and dropping out gives no refund of any kind. The only genuine saving is the recurring 20% early-bird discount code.
programs.scholarships: NONE. No scholarship, bursary or financial aid of any kind is published for the Ibiza short courses.
programs.facilities: A fully-equipped academy just outside Ibiza Town at Instituto de Educación Secundaria Isidoro Macabich, Calle de sa Blanca Dona s/n, 07800 Eivissa (the FAQ also refers to it as the Ibiza Blau / Can Blau music school). Pioneer DJ-sponsored studios with industry-leading kit and Ableton Live. Tutors are working Ibiza DJ/producers (Javier Garcia 'Grazze', Veve Milah, vocalist Blanka Nova). A free media pack is included for every student on these courses: 10 professional press shots and 2 Instagram reels. Industry partner discounts and event access are provided but confirmed only during the course.
programs.reputationSignals: Point Blank is a genuinely well-regarded electronic music school with real standing in DJ and production education and authentic Ibiza industry access; alumni include Nicole Moudaber, and the school cites Goldie, Leona Lewis and Pete Tong among its associations. The free media pack (10 press shots plus 2 Instagram reels) and the software discounts are concrete, unusual deliverables. RED FLAGS for this search, all verified: it is a one or two-week short course, not education at any level; it carries no Spanish accreditation, no ECTS and no named certificate; it cannot support a student residence permit; the deposit is forfeited even if his visa is refused; and the performance slots are NOT guaranteed despite how the marketing reads — the course page says only that there is 'potential for you to perform', and the FAQ adds that set times and locations are 'subject to venue availability and the instructor' and that 'due to venue size not every student will be able to play at the same venue on the same night'.
programs.recommendation: EXPLICITLY NOT A MASTER — one or two weeks, no ECTS, no certificate named, no Spanish accreditation, and it cannot bring him to Spain on a student permit. Three corrections he must not miss: the one-week price is £1,145 not £1,195; the deposit is £100 for one week and £200 for two, and it is NON-REFUNDABLE EVEN IF HIS VISA IS REFUSED; and the performance slots are advertised as potential opportunities subject to venue availability, not the guaranteed bookings the marketing implies. There is also no instalment plan — the terms and conditions rule instalments out and demand full payment 14 days before the start. That said, my candid verdict stands: as a roughly £1,700 two-week investment (nearer £1,350 on the recurring 20% early-bird code) in real Ibiza contacts, a free professional media pack of 10 press shots and 2 Instagram reels, and 50% off Ableton Live, it would do more for his stated ambition of becoming a working DJ than several of the five-figure 'másteres' elsewhere on this list. Treat it as career marketing bought with a Schengen tourist-style visa, taken in a summer BEFORE the September 2027 intake, and never as a qualification or a route to residency. CONDITIONAL strictly on that framing — if he is tempted to substitute it for an accredited programme, the answer is AVOID.

programs.program: Mestrado em Som e Imagem — especialização em Design de Som (Sound Design)
programs.institution: Universidade Católica Portuguesa — Escola das Artes (Porto)
programs.qualification: MESTRADO — Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree, 120 ECTS. A real Bologna master's, NOT a pós-graduação. Awards 'Mestre em Som e Imagem'. VERIFIED: the Escola das Artes course page states the programme is 'acreditado pela A3ES' and DGES-registered, 120 ECTS, 2nd cycle.
programs.institutionType: Private university (Universidade Católica Portuguesa — private, State-recognised, established under Concordat). Escola das Artes is its arts faculty in Porto.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — AND NOW FULLY VERIFIED. This is the key upgrade from the draft. The mestrado carries DGES registration R/A-Ef 1160/2011/AL01 and A3ES accreditation process ACEF/1415/14132; the Escola das Artes course page independently confirms 'acreditado pela A3ES' and DGES registration for the 2nd cycle. The draft's claim that the A3ES reference was UNVERIFIED is now SUPERSEDED — the reference exists. Practical meaning: this is an official Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree, valid across the EHEA, valid for doctoral entry, and valid as the basis for a Portuguese D4 study residence visa. It is emphatically NOT a 'pós-graduação' and not a school-issued certificate. He should still ask admissions to email him the registo/despacho reference on letterhead before paying — standard hygiene, not a doubt about the status.
programs.focus: Sound design for film, theatre and concerts, music production, sound art installations and game audio, taught inside a wider sound-and-image school. VERIFIED: the school runs FOUR specialisations, not three as previously recorded — Animação, Design de Som, New Media Art, and Visual Effects. He would enter the Design de Som track.
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1 S1 (30 ECTS): Projeto/Produção I — Exterior e Estúdio (12), Produção de Som para Videojogos (5), Produção Eletrónica (5), Artes e Tecnologias do Som (5), Investigação em Som e Imagem (3). Year 1 S2 (30 ECTS): Projeto II — Pós-Produção/Design de Som (12), Banda Sonora (5), Projeto Interdisciplinar (5), Seminário Interdisciplinar (3), Interfaces Tangíveis e Computação Física (5). Year 2: Portfólio e Showreel (3) plus Dissertação/Projeto/Estágio (27+30). Covers microphone technique, studio recording and mastering, surround mixing for cinema, live sound, game audio and sound art. Curricular internship option of minimum 24 weeks. NOTE THE PROPORTION: exactly ONE 5-ECTS unit ('Produção Eletrónica') out of 120 touches electronic music production. This is a film/game/media sound-design degree with strong studio craft — it is not an electronic-music or DJ programme, and no amount of framing changes that.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS. VERIFIED. Regime PÓS-LABORAL (evening), classes roughly 18:00–22:00 — genuinely useful, it leaves his days free to produce and build the DJ side in parallel.
programs.language: PORTUGUESE. This remains the single biggest practical risk for him and I could NOT verify any English-taught route — the course pages do not state a language of instruction at all, which in Portuguese higher education defaults to Portuguese. Treat 'taught in Portuguese' as the working assumption and get it confirmed in writing. He does not speak Portuguese; this is the decisive constraint on the whole entry.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED verbatim from the admissions page: 'Licenciado ou equivalente legal (na área do cinema, audiovisual, fotografia, multimédia, artes plásticas, arquitetura, design, engenharias, etc.)'; OR a foreign qualification conferred following the Bologna Process by a signatory State; OR a foreign academic qualification recognised as meeting the objectives of a licenciatura; OR a professional/academic curriculum recognised by the Escola das Artes Scientific Council. Foreign documents require Hague Apostille (Tunisia is an Apostille member, so the apostille route applies rather than full diplomatic legalisation).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY, AND THIS IS VERIFIED WORD-FOR-WORD. The published eligibility list names 'engenharias' (engineering) as an accepted first-cycle field, alongside cinema, audiovisual, fotografia, multimédia, artes plásticas, arquitetura and design. This is the ONLY programme in this Portuguese batch that names engineering in its own admission wording, which makes it the strongest structural fit on paper for a BSc Software Engineering holder. Caveat: eligibility is not selection — an artistic portfolio is still mandatory for candidates external to the Escola das Artes, and there is an interview.
programs.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED as required, but the SPEC ITSELF IS STILL UNPUBLISHED. Exact wording: 'Portfólio do trabalho artístico (deverá ser indicado um link para acesso ao portfolio)' — an artistic work portfolio supplied as a link through the application platform. The page explicitly limits the interview stage to candidates external to the Escola das Artes, and the portfolio requirement attaches to the same group. No page count, runtime, format or assessment criteria are published — UNVERIFIED. He must email candidaturas.porto@ucp.pt for the assessment criteria; with no music background, he cannot afford to guess what they want.
programs.auditionSpec: Interview — VERIFIED as a fixed, scheduled step in every application phase, held 'exclusivamente para alunos externos à Escola das Artes', i.e. it definitely applies to him. Dated slots were published for each 2026/27 phase (e.g. 14–15 April after phase 1). No performance audition, no written test, no instrument requirement. Whether the interview can be conducted online from Tunisia is NOT published — UNVERIFIED and worth confirming early, because travelling to Porto for a 30-minute interview would be a real cost.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS requirement is published, and none should be expected — the programme is Portuguese-medium, so IELTS is simply the wrong test here. His untaken IELTS is therefore NOT the blocker for this programme; Portuguese is. programs.tuitionPerYear: €6,570 per year — VERIFIED. Published as €657 per month × 10 monthly instalments, 2026/27 rate. No separate non-EU rate is published anywhere on the admissions page: he pays the same as a Portuguese student.
programs.tuitionTotal: €13,140 total tuition for the full 2-year mestrado (€657 × 10 × 2), 2026/27 rate — VERIFIED, and the page itself states the total. NON-EU NOTE: no international or non-EU surcharge is published. By Western European private-school standards this is remarkably cheap — the entire degree costs less than a single year at most Spanish or Dutch private audio schools.
programs.otherFees: VERIFIED: Application fee (taxa de candidatura) €50, waived for UCP graduates. Enrolment fee (taxa de inscrição) €460. Both figures confirmed on the official admissions page. STILL UNVERIFIED: whether the €460 recurs in year 2 or is a one-off at first enrolment; and insurance, materials and exam fees, which are not itemised anywhere public. The full 'Regulamento de propinas, taxas e emolumentos' exists on porto.ucp.pt but is image-encoded and could not be machine-read. Ask for the current emolumentos table as a text document.
programs.equipmentRequired: Nothing mandatory is published — UNVERIFIED. The school supplies studios and preferential 24/7 student access to specialised equipment. A personal laptop plus a DAW licence is realistically expected but is nowhere stated as a requirement. Budget €1,500–€2,500 for a capable laptop, interface, headphones and software regardless; no accredited sound programme is genuinely doable without one.
programs.paymentPlans: VERIFIED: tuition is structured by default as 10 monthly instalments per academic year (€657/month) — no separate application or approval needed, that IS the billing model. Early-bird, alumni or referral discounts: none published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: Merit scholarships (bolsas de mérito) are offered by the Escola das Artes and referenced from the course page's 'Apoios e Bolsas' section; UCP Porto's general merit scholarship consists of full exemption from tuition up to a maximum of 36 ECTS per semester plus exemption from registration and enrolment fees. The Escola das Artes additionally lists the Prémio Caixa Geral de Depósitos. CRITICAL UNVERIFIED POINT: whether a non-EU FIRST-YEAR entrant can win one on entry, as opposed to after a year of graded performance at UCP — the mechanics were not published and I could not confirm them. Portuguese State social scholarships (DGES Ação Social) are not realistically open to a newly arrived non-EU student. PLANNING ASSUMPTION: full self-pay for year 1, with a merit scholarship as a possible year-2 upside only.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September (start of the academic year). Three application phases all feed the same September start. VERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED for 2026/27: phase 1 opened 2 February 2026. Expect the 2027/28 cycle to open late January / early February 2027. He should start watching admissions.porto.ucp.pt from January 2027.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED 2026/27 phases, all three: Phase 1 — 2 Feb to 9 Apr 2026 (interviews 14–15 Apr, results 21 Apr, enrolment 27–28 Apr). Phase 2 — 30 Apr to 11 Jun 2026 (interviews 16–17 Jun, results 23 Jun, enrolment 26–29 Jun). Phase 3 — 1 Jul to 26 Aug 2026 (interviews 1–2 Sep, results 7 Sep, enrolment 9–10 Sep). FOR A SEPTEMBER 2027 START HE MUST APPLY IN PHASE 1 (roughly Feb–Apr 2027). A phase-3 result dated 7 September leaves literally zero time to obtain a Tunisian D4 visa for the same month's start — phase 3 is structurally useless to a non-EU applicant.

programs.visaEligible: YES — and this is verified at the level that matters. UCP is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited, DGES-registered 2nd-cycle degree lasting 2 years, which is exactly the category that supports a Portuguese D4 residence visa for study (courses longer than 12 months). Standard file from Tunis: UCP acceptance letter, proof of means, accommodation, insurance, criminal record. The institution's status is not the risk here; his timeline is.
programs.reputationSignals: The strongest single signal in Portuguese private sound education. Positives: A3ES/DGES-recognised degree with a traceable registration reference; a dedicated Design de Som specialisation, which is rare; a research-active school with a Doutoramento em Ciência e Tecnologia das Artes sitting above it; motion-capture and surround facilities; an Erasmus Mundus programme (Digicréa) hosted in the same school; four coordinated specialisations under a named coordinator. Selective but not tiny. No published complaints, no red flags, no aggressive commercial-intake pattern. The honest caveat is scope, not quality: it is a film and media-arts sound school, not a club-music or DJ school.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €7,080–€7,600 (tuition €6,570 + application €50 + enrolment €460, plus unpublished insurance/materials). Full two-year tuition + fees approx. €13,650–€14,500. EXCLUDES Porto living costs (budget €800–€1,100/month, i.e. roughly €19,000–€26,000 over two years — living cost dwarfs tuition here) and excludes a laptop/DAW at €1,500–€2,500. Realistic all-in two-year figure: €35,000–€43,000.
programs.recommendation: THE STRONGEST PORTUGUESE OPTION ON PAPER — BUT THE LANGUAGE MAKES IT CONDITIONAL, NOT AUTOMATIC. It is the only entry in this batch that is simultaneously a genuine A3ES/DGES master's degree, explicitly open to an engineering bachelor in its own published wording, visa-safe, and cheap (€13,140 for the whole degree). The accreditation question that the draft left open is now closed in its favour. Two things must be said bluntly. First, it is taught in Portuguese and he does not speak it — that is a 12-month project he must start NOW if he wants the Feb–Apr 2027 phase-1 window, and if he will not do it, this entry is unworkable and he should put everything into ReSound instead. Second, it will not make him a DJ. It will make him a competent film and game sound designer with real studio craft and one 5-ECTS brush with electronic production. If he is honest that the accredited degree is the visa-and-craft vehicle and the DJ career is built in parallel on evenings and weekends, this is excellent value. If he expects the degree itself to deliver the DJ career, he will be disappointed and out €35k.
programs.verificationNotes: Admissions page fetched and confirmed in full: engineering ('engenharias') named verbatim in eligibility; portfolio wording confirmed verbatim; interview confirmed as external-candidates-only and date-scheduled; all three 2026/27 phase windows confirmed; €50 application, €460 enrolment, €657/month × 10 × 2 years = €13,140 all confirmed. UPGRADE vs draft: A3ES/DGES references located — DGES R/A-Ef 1160/2011/AL01, A3ES process ACEF/1415/14132 — so accreditation is no longer UNVERIFIED. CORRECTION vs draft: the school runs FOUR specialisations (Animação, Design de Som, New Media Art, Visual Effects), not three. The www.porto.ucp.pt course page returned HTTP 403 and could not be read directly; the artes.porto.ucp.pt page was used instead and confirmed 120 ECTS, pós-laboral regime, A3ES+DGES accreditation and the specialisation list. REMAINS UNVERIFIED: language of instruction (not stated anywhere — assume Portuguese), portfolio assessment criteria, whether the €460 enrolment recurs annually, insurance/materials fees, whether merit scholarships are available to non-EU entrants in year 1, and whether the interview can be held online.

programs.program: Mestrado em Produção e Tecnologias do Som
programs.institution: Universidade Lusófona — Centro Universitário de Lisboa (COFAC)
programs.qualification: MESTRADO — Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree, 120 ECTS, 4 semesters, presencial. A real degree, NOT a pós-graduação. VERIFIED on the official course page.
programs.institutionType: Private university, owned by COFAC (Cooperativa de Formação e Animação Cultural) — Portugal's largest private university group.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — VERIFIED. The course page publishes A3ES status 'Acreditado' with registration R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01 and a linked A3ES deliberation. This is a fully accredited Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree: valid across the EHEA, valid for doctoral entry, and a valid basis for a D4 student residence visa. Not a título propio equivalent, not a certificate. On the accreditation question — the thing most likely to cost him his visa or leave him with worthless paper — this one is clean and the reference is publicly checkable.
programs.focus: Sound production and sound technology: audiovisual sound, immersive and spatial audio, sound art, music computing, studio practice, and sound as a functional element in devices and environments.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module set. Year 1 S1 (30 ECTS): Acústica e Instrumentação, Captação de Som, Computação de Áudio Digital, Design e Composição Sonora, Síntese de Sinal Áudio. Year 1 S2 (30 ECTS): História e Cultura do Som, Computação Musical, Projeto Interdisciplinar, Teoria e Prática de Estúdio. Year 2 S1: Arte e Tecnologia, Metodologia de Investigação Científica, Projeto de Dissertação. Year 2 S2: Dissertação (30 ECTS). Core software confirmed as Avid Pro Tools, Max/MSP and Arduino. Published career outcomes include sound director, sound designer, music producer, recording and mastering technician. THIS IS THE CLOSEST CONTENT FIT TO WHAT HE ACTUALLY WANTS of any accredited option in this batch — synthesis, sound design, studio practice and music computing are all core, not electives. And Max/MSP plus Arduino is where his software engineering background becomes an asset rather than a liability.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, in-person. VERIFIED schedule: 'Pós-laboral: Todos os dias úteis a partir das 18 horas' — every weekday from 18:00. The evening format is a genuine strategic advantage for him: days free for studio work, freelance production and building the DJ side.
programs.language: PORTUGUESE. No English-taught delivery is published for the mestrado and none could be verified. The English-medium route in this same department is ReSound (listed separately) — which strongly implies the domestic mestrado is not English-medium. Treat Portuguese as required.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED: holders of a licenciatura or legal equivalent; OR a foreign degree conferred following the Bologna Process by a signatory State; OR a foreign academic qualification recognised as equivalent; OR a recognised academic/professional curriculum demonstrating capacity for this cycle of studies. VERIFIED SELECTION WEIGHTING, which is the number that actually matters: 25% prior qualification + 75% interview and portfolio/curricular evaluation. Candidates without a degree are assessed 100% on interview.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: ELIGIBLE ON PAPER, BUT THE SCORING IS THE REAL TEST. The regulation accepts 'titulares de grau de licenciado ou equivalente legal' with no field restriction, so a Software Engineering BSc is formally admissible — but unlike UCP Porto, the wording does NOT name engineering or computing among its target fields (it names musicology, sound technologies, audiovisual production, digital and performing arts, and media professionals). Combined with the verified 25/75 split, his degree is worth at most a quarter of the decision and his portfolio plus interview is worth three quarters. He currently has no portfolio. Verdict: admissible, but he must earn it entirely on work he has not yet made. His engineering background is a genuinely strong story here IF he frames it through Max/MSP, Arduino and audio DSP — the curriculum itself hands him that framing.
programs.portfolioSpec: Required, and jointly with the interview carries 75% of the selection score — VERIFIED. But NO published format, length or content specification exists — UNVERIFIED. This is a meaningful gap: the single most heavily weighted element of the application is undefined in public. He must request the 'critérios de seriação' from info.cul@ulusofona.pt before building anything, or he risks producing the wrong thing.
programs.auditionSpec: Interview (entrevista) — mandatory, combined with portfolio review as 75% of the score. VERIFIED. No performance audition or instrument test. Lusófona's international-student route separately references internal entrance examinations ('provas de ingresso internas'); whether those apply to 2nd-cycle entry is UNVERIFIED — ask, because an internal exam sat in Lisbon would be a serious logistical problem from Tunis.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS requirement — the programme is Portuguese-medium, so IELTS is not the relevant test. Lusófona requires proof of proficiency in the language of instruction. Note the trap the draft correctly flagged: documents issued in Portuguese, Spanish, French or English are exempt from certified translation — that is a DOCUMENT rule, not a language-proficiency waiver, and his French-language Tunisian paperwork will benefit from it without saying anything about his Portuguese. Portuguese proficiency evidence for him: UNVERIFIED, assume it will be required.
programs.tuitionPerYear: NOT PUBLISHED AS AN ANNUAL FIGURE — this is the central money problem with this entry, and it is now verified as a genuine gap rather than a research failure. VERIFIED 2026/27 values, quoted exactly from the official fee table: 'Valor médio mensal para 30 ECTS para disciplinas semestrais 380.4€' and 'Valor por ECTS 12.68€'. VERIFIED 2025/26 comparison: €365.40 monthly for 30 ECTS, €12.18 per ECTS — a 4.1% year-on-year rise, so budget a further rise for 2027/28. Lusófona bills in monthly instalments but the NUMBER of instalments per academic year is nowhere stated. On a 10-instalment year that implies roughly €3,804/year; on 12 instalments roughly €4,565/year. DO NOT TREAT EITHER AS CONFIRMED. Cross-check: 60 ECTS/year × €12.68 = €760.80/year, which is obviously not the annual tuition — the per-ECTS figure clearly does not multiply out to an annual total, which is itself a warning that this fee page cannot be reasoned about arithmetically. Demand a written annual figure in euros before he plans anything.
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED as a single published number — none exists. Derived range for the full 120 ECTS at the 2026/27 rate: approximately €7,600 (10 instalments/year) to €9,130 (12 instalments/year). NON-EU POSITION VERIFIED AND FAVOURABLE: Lusófona's international-student page confirms international students receive 'the same tuition table as all other students', with no premium for non-EU status. There is no non-EU surcharge.
programs.otherFees: VERIFIED VERBATIM from the 2026/27 fee table: 'Candidatura a Mestrados – 460€' AND 'Candidatura a Mestrados – 180€' — both lines genuinely appear, with NO distinguishing text between them. I confirmed the same duplication in the 2025/26 table (€450 and €175), so it is a persistent structure, not a typo; the near-certain explanation is a national vs international (or standard vs early/online) split that the page simply fails to label. He must get written confirmation of which applies to him — the difference is €280. Also VERIFIED 2026/27: 'Candidatura de Reingresso 110€'; 'Matrícula/Inscrição/Renovação da Inscrição 350€'; 'Seguro Escolar 50€'; isolated curricular units €640 / €450. 2025/26 comparison verified: reingresso €105, matrícula/inscrição €300, seguro €47. Lusófona's international page elsewhere quotes a €425 application fee, which appears to belong to the 1st-cycle route — UNVERIFIED for 2nd cycle and a third conflicting number. Materials, equipment and exam fees: not itemised — UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. The department supplies professional multitrack studios, acoustic labs and 3D/Atmos facilities. A personal laptop and a Pro Tools licence are realistically necessary given the named core software, but neither is stated as a mandatory purchase. Budget €1,500–€2,500 anyway.
programs.paymentPlans: Monthly instalments are the default billing unit — VERIFIED. CRITICAL NON-EU CASH-FLOW CONDITION, NOW VERIFIED ON THE OFFICIAL INTERNATIONAL PAGE: international students must pay TWO MONTHS OF TUITION IN ADVANCE at matriculation, together with registration, enrolment and school insurance; subsequent instalments fall due by the 8th of each month. So his day-one outlay is roughly €760 tuition + €350 matrícula + €50 seguro + candidatura, not one month's fee. VERIFIED payment methods: credit card, PayPal, Multibanco/ATM transfer, cash in person. Early-bird, alumni or referral discounts: none published for Lisbon — UNVERIFIED (the Porto campus advertised a 5% internal-student discount, which does not apply to him).
programs.scholarships: No Lusófona scholarship specifically open to non-EU students is published on any page reviewed — UNVERIFIED, and I would not plan on one existing. Portuguese State DGES social scholarships are not realistically open to a newly arrived non-EU student. The practical funding route in this department is ReSound (Erasmus Mundus), not the domestic mestrado. ASSUME FULL SELF-PAY.
programs.intakes: One September intake, fed by MULTIPLE application phases across the year — the 2026/27 cycle ran to at least a 5th period, and the draft's count of seven is plausible though I could only confirm the 5th. Multiple phases, single start.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED for 2026/27: the 5th application period opened 18 July 2026, which means earlier phases opened well before that — expect the 2027/28 cycle to open in the first months of 2027. He should be watching from January 2027.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED published 2026/27 window: 5th application period 18 July – 1 September 2026. For a September 2027 start he must apply in an EARLY phase (spring 2027), NOT a late one. A 1 September deadline with a September start is incompatible with obtaining a D4 visa from Tunis — the consular processing alone will not fit. The multi-phase structure is a trap for non-EU applicants: it looks flexible, but only the first two phases are actually usable by him.
programs.facilities: Professional multitrack recording studios; specialised acoustic laboratories; cinema post-production facilities; 3D/Dolby Atmos audio system. Faculty described as working producers, sound designers, researchers and artists. The department (som.ulusofona.pt) also runs the BSc Ciência e Tecnologias do Som and hosts the ReSound Erasmus Mundus master, and sits inside the FilmEU European University alliance — a genuine international-network signal, not marketing.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Lusófona is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited 120-ECTS degree over 2 years, which supports a Portuguese D4 study residence visa. It operates a formal 'Estudante Internacional' admission statute and a CLAIM migrant-integration service on campus, and the international page's explicit rules on advance payment show it routinely processes non-EU enrolments. Institutionally set up for someone in his position.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: A3ES accreditation with a published, checkable registration reference; a dedicated sound department with Atmos and acoustic labs; FilmEU European University alliance membership; host of an Erasmus Mundus joint master, which is not awarded without external quality scrutiny. NEUTRAL/NEGATIVE: Lusófona is a large-volume private group running an admissions funnel of five-plus phases per year, which is a commercial-intake pattern rather than a selective one; the group has periodically attracted press scrutiny in Portugal over governance; and its Pós-Graduação em Produção e Tecnologia do Som has been withdrawn (confirmed 404 — see the separate entry), so programme-portfolio churn is real. The mestrado itself shows no sign of instability, but he should ask directly whether it is confirmed to run in 2027/28.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €4,400–€5,400 (derived tuition €3,800–€4,565 + matrícula €350 + seguro €50 + candidatura €180 or €460), noting that roughly €760 of the tuition is payable up front at enrolment. Full-programme tuition + fees roughly €8,200–€10,000. EXCLUDES Lisbon living costs, which are the real expense — realistically €900–€1,300/month, i.e. €21,600–€31,200 over two years, and Lisbon rent has been rising hard. Excludes €1,500–€2,500 equipment. Realistic all-in two-year figure: €31,000–€44,000, of which tuition is under a third.
programs.recommendation: BEST CONTENT FIT AMONG THE ACCREDITED OPTIONS, AND CHEAPEST — BUT DO NOT COMMIT UNTIL THE TUITION IS IN WRITING. The curriculum is genuinely the closest of anything in this batch to what he says he wants: synthesis, sound design, studio practice, music computing, Pro Tools and Max/MSP, on an evening timetable, in Lisbon, a real electronic-music city. Accreditation is solid and publicly verifiable. Non-EU students pay the same as locals. Three hard warnings. (1) The annual tuition is not published as a single number, the per-ECTS figure does not multiply out sensibly, and the fee page lists two different master's application fees with no explanation — I verified all of that directly, so this is a fee page that cannot be trusted to arithmetic. Get a written annual euro figure and a written instalment count before he transfers anything. (2) It is taught in Portuguese. (3) 75% of the admission decision rests on a portfolio and interview, and he has no portfolio — he needs twelve months of serious, finished output before he can credibly apply. Rank it second behind UCP Porto on prestige and institutional solidity, first on price and on curriculum fit.
programs.verificationNotes: Course page fetched and confirmed: 120 ECTS / 4 semestres / presencial; A3ES 'Acreditado' with registration R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01; pós-laboral 'todos os dias úteis a partir das 18 horas'; entry-requirement categories; the 25%/75% selection split; the module list; Pro Tools / Max-MSP / Arduino. The full 2026/27 AND 2025/26 fee tables were retrieved and quoted verbatim — every figure in otherFees and tuitionPerYear is confirmed word-for-word, including the genuinely duplicated 'Candidatura a Mestrados – 460€' / '– 180€' lines, which I confirmed recur in the 2025/26 table as €450/€175. The international-student page independently confirmed identical tuition for non-EU students, the two-months-in-advance rule, the 8th-of-month due date, and the payment methods. REMAINS UNVERIFIED: the number of monthly instalments per year (so the annual and total tuition are DERIVED, not published), which candidatura fee applies to a non-EU applicant, the portfolio format spec, whether 'provas de ingresso internas' apply at 2nd-cycle level, Portuguese proficiency evidence, equipment requirements, and any scholarship for non-EU students. programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts
programs.institution: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (Ireland) + Universidade Lusófona (Portugal, private) + Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (Lithuania), within the FilmEU alliance
programs.city: Lisbon (one semester); Dublin and Vilnius for the others
programs.country: Portugal (one of three countries; the Portuguese partner is the private Universidade Lusófona)
programs.qualification: ERASMUS MUNDUS JOINT MASTER (EMJM) — 120 ECTS joint/multiple master's degree awarded by the consortium partners. A full, official 2nd-cycle degree, not a certificate.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL, and the highest-quality accreditation signal in this entire batch. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are selected and funded directly by the European Commission, and each partner's award is nationally accredited — Lusófona under A3ES (verified separately in this batch: R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01 for its sister mestrado, and the institution is an accredited Portuguese university), IADT under Irish QQI, LMTA under Lithuanian accreditation. EMJM designation is itself an external quality endorsement that no purely private school can buy. There is no plausible scenario in which this qualification turns out to be worthless paper — which is precisely the risk that dominates the rest of this search.
programs.focus: Sound as an artistic, cultural and technological force across media arts, immersive environments, performance and the audiovisual industries. The most internationally-facing sound master's touching Portugal.
programs.whatYouStudy: Four semesters with compulsory structured mobility across the three partner institutions, closing with a master's thesis/project. The Lisbon semester draws on Lusófona's Dolby Atmos/3D audio room, professional multitrack studios and acoustic laboratories. DETAILED PER-SEMESTER MODULE LISTS COULD NOT BE VERIFIED — the public pages describe the programme as 'a two-year, four-semester journey' with Erasmus+ mobility but do not publish a module-by-module curriculum, and the semester-to-institution mapping is NOT stated on the pages I could read. This is a real gap for a €15,000 (or scholarship-competitive) decision: he must request the full programme handbook and the semester/institution mapping from the consortium before applying.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time, in-person, with compulsory mobility across three countries.
programs.language: ENGLISH. VERIFIED via the published IELTS requirement. This is the decisive difference from every other accredited option in this batch — it is the ONLY one he can study in a language he already has, and it removes the twelve-month Portuguese problem entirely.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED VERBATIM: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies.' Baseline expectation is a bachelor's in sound, music, film or media studies. Application pack: academic transcripts, portfolio, two recommendation letters, proof of English proficiency. Maximum 24 places per year — VERIFIED: 'A maximum of 24 places are offered at ReSound each year.'
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CONDITIONALLY YES — AND THIS EXACT CLAUSE IS THE WHOLE BALLGAME FOR HIM. Verified wording: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies.' His Software Engineering BSc is unambiguously 'a degree in another field', so admission turns entirely on evidencing 'relevant prior experience' in sound, music, film or media. He currently has NONE — no music degree, no conservatory training, no professional audio work. Note the clause says 'may also be considered', not 'will be accepted': it is a discretionary door, not a right. Between now and a likely late-January 2027 deadline he must manufacture genuine evidence — released tracks, credited sound work on short films or games, live sets, a substantial audio-software project. Without it this is a rejection, and no amount of essay-writing substitutes.
programs.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED AND UNUSUALLY PRECISE — the clearest spec in this entire batch, which is a gift because it removes all guesswork. Quoted: 'Please supply no more than 3 examples', each with 'a short reflective paragraph on each piece explicitly stating your role in the work'. Acceptable formats: 'a single hyperlink to a portfolio website or a compilation audio or video file'. Reviewers assess realistically 10–15 minutes of material per application. The discipline this demands is the point: three strong finished pieces totalling 10–15 minutes, not a dump of everything he has ever made. He should build to exactly this spec and use it as the target for the whole next twelve months.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition or performance test is published. Selection rests on documents, portfolio and references. Whether an interview stage exists is UNVERIFIED.
programs.englishTest: YES — VERIFIED, AND THIS IS HIS MOST URGENT ACTION ITEM. IELTS 6.0 minimum with 'no component less than 6.0' — every band, not just the overall. Verified equivalents: TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2. Certificates must be 'taken within the last two years'. He has NOT taken IELTS. Working backwards from a probable late-January 2027 deadline, he should book and sit it in autumn 2026 — now — leaving room for one retake if a single band comes in at 5.5. Worth checking separately whether his SMU MedTech BSc was English-taught and qualifies for a prior-study waiver, which would save both the fee and the sitting; the ReSound page lists alternative qualifications but I could not verify the exact waiver wording, so do not rely on it — book the test.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €7,500 per year for self-funded students, charged as two instalments of €7,500 rather than four — VERIFIED. NON-EU PRICING IS IDENTICAL TO EU PRICING: no differentiation is stated anywhere, which is unusual and strongly in his favour. Most international programmes penalise a Tunisian passport here; this one does not.
programs.tuitionTotal: €15,000 total for the four-semester programme (self-funded) — VERIFIED on the official consortium application page as '15,000 Euro' split into two payments of '7,500 EUR'. CONFLICT FLAG STANDS: Universidade Lusófona's own ReSound page quotes an average of roughly €2,250 per month for 30-ECTS semestral units (about €9,000 per semester), which does not reconcile with the consortium's €15,000 total. Treat resound-ma.eu as authoritative — it is the consortium's own page and the figure is unambiguous — but get the discrepancy resolved in writing before paying anything, because a €36,000 reading of the Lusófona page is not a rounding error.
programs.otherFees: No application fee is mentioned on the application page — VERIFIED absence, though absence of mention is weaker than an explicit statement of zero. Travel, accommodation and living costs are explicitly excluded from tuition and estimated by the consortium at €600–€1,000 per month. HIDDEN COST HE MUST BUDGET FOR: three-country mobility means THREE separate immigration processes (Ireland — outside Schengen and with its own IRP regime — plus Portugal and Lithuania) and two inter-country relocations. Realistically €1,500–€3,000 across the two years in permit fees, flights and deposits. This is nowhere published — UNVERIFIED as a figure, but it is certain to exist and it disproportionately burdens a Tunisian passport holder.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. A capable laptop and reference headphones are a practical necessity for a mobility-based sound programme where he will be working away from any one studio for much of the time.
programs.paymentPlans: Self-funded tuition is split into two payments of €7,500, at semester 1 and semester 3 — VERIFIED. Note this is a harsher cash-flow shape than it first appears: €7,500 due before he starts. No instalment plan, early-bird or alumni discount is published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: THE BEST FUNDING AVAILABLE ANYWHERE IN THIS SEARCH, AND HE IS ELIGIBLE AS A NON-EU NATIONAL. VERIFIED: Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders 'pay no tuition fees' and receive a stipend of '1,400 EUR per month'. Over 24 months that is roughly €33,600 in stipend plus €15,000 in waived tuition — around €48,600 of value, and it converts his entire plan from a €30,000+ outlay into a net-positive one. Awarded on merit. Two honest structural caveats: only ONE of four semesters is actually in Portugal, so if his goal is to establish himself in the Lisbon scene specifically, this scatters him across three countries at exactly the age when building a local network matters; and the absence of a published module list is a transparency gap he should close before committing.

programs.recommendation: APPLY. THIS IS HIS SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE SHOT IN THE PORTUGUESE SLICE, AND THE ONLY ONE TAUGHT IN ENGLISH THAT CAN BE FULLY FUNDED. The arithmetic is decisive for a budget-sensitive self-payer: a scholarship converts a €30,000-plus plan into a funded one with a €1,400 monthly stipend, worth roughly €48,600. Nothing else in this search comes close. But be blunt with him about the odds and the work. Twenty-four places, worldwide competition, and an admission clause requiring 'relevant prior experience' he does not have. His concrete twelve-month plan, in priority order: (1) book IELTS NOW and clear 6.0 in EVERY band — a single 5.5 disqualifies him — or verify an English-medium waiver for his BSc; (2) build exactly three portfolio pieces totalling 10–15 minutes, ideally one released track, one piece of sound-to-picture, and one audio-software or interactive piece that turns his engineering background into a differentiator rather than the liability the admissions clause implies; (3) secure two recommenders now, while his SMU lecturers still remember him; (4) watch resound-ma.eu from October 2026 for the call. If he does only ONE thing from this entire Portugal report, it should be this application — with UCP Porto and the Lusófona mestrado as the paid, Portuguese-language fallbacks. He should treat self-funding this at €15,000 as a poor third option: without the scholarship, the Lusófona mestrado teaches similar content for roughly half the tuition.

programs.visaEligible: YES. Universidade Europeia/IADE is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited 2-year, 120-ECTS degree, which supports a Portuguese D4 study residence visa. As an international-chain university it has established international admissions machinery. The visa route is sound; the question is whether the degree is worth taking it for.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: A3ES accreditation with a specific, checkable registration and despacho; IADE is a long-established and well-regarded Lisbon design school; unusually transparent published price list with named discount categories — better fee disclosure than most schools in this whole search; a clearly quantified merit scholarship. NEGATIVE FOR HIS PURPOSES: this is a communication and multimedia degree with essentially no sound curriculum. Note also the commercial signals, which I verified rather than inferred: rolling year-round admissions with no published entry criteria, a phone-and-WhatsApp enquiry funnel, at least four overlapping discount and scholarship categories, discount columns 'subject to limited vacancies defined in the selection process' (i.e. scarcity framing on price), and mandatory direct debit to unlock either instalments or scholarships. That is a sales-led enrolment model, not a selective academic one. It does not make the degree fake — the accreditation is real — but it should calibrate how much prestige he assumes he is buying.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €6,400–€6,600 first-year outlay if the €509.30/month figure holds (tuition ~€5,600 + emolumentos ~€800–€900), before laptop, Adobe and Lisbon living costs. Two-year tuition plus fees roughly €12,000 at base rate, or roughly €7,600 with the 40% merit scholarship if he clears 16.5/20. All tuition figures UNVERIFIED pending written confirmation. Add Lisbon living at €900–€1,300/month (€21,600–€31,200 over two years) for a realistic all-in of €34,000–€44,000.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT PRIORITISE — RIGHT COUNTRY, RIGHT ACCREDITATION, WRONG SUBJECT. Let me be blunt, because the accreditation being genuine is exactly what makes this dangerous: a real A3ES degree, real visa eligibility and a real quantified scholarship can all be true while the programme still teaches him nothing he wants. He wants music production, mixing, sound design and electronic music. This degree teaches digital journalism, infographics, transmedia and web labs, in Portuguese, with one shared sound studio and zero audio modules. Paying around €12,000 plus two years of his life for that would be a poor use of a budget-sensitive candidate's money when the Lusófona mestrado, in the same city, teaches acoustics, capture, synthesis, sound design and studio practice for less. Three further practical cautions: the exact tuition and emolumentos figures could NOT be verified from the official PDF and must be obtained in writing; the merit scholarship threshold for him is the FOREIGN-institution bar of 16.5/20, not 15.5, and the two official sources disagree on both threshold and percentage; and every scholarship and the 11-instalment plan require a Portuguese direct debit he cannot set up before arriving. Keep it only as a distant fallback if UCP, Lusófona and ReSound all fail AND he decides he wants an accredited Portuguese degree for immigration reasons more than he wants sound training — which would be an honest choice, but he should make it with his eyes open rather than mistake this for a sound course.

In practice: he receives a nationally-recognised vocational training certificate that has real standing in the Portuguese labour market but ZERO academic standing — it cannot be used for PhD entry, cannot be recognised as a degree in Tunisia or the EHEA, and carries no ECTS transferable to any master's. programs.focus: Entry-level studio and live sound technician craft.

programs.portfolioSpec: 'Portefólio ou showreel' required plus a motivation letter — CONFIRMED as a requirement, but NO format, length, or content specification is published — UNVERIFIED. programs.recommendation: CLOSEST TO WHAT HE WANTS TO DO, FURTHEST FROM WHAT HE NEEDS INSTITUTIONALLY — and it verifies better than the draft assumed. Three things improved on verification: delivery in ENGLISH is confirmed by ProDJ itself, the equipment inventory is real and respectable (Moog, Roland, Adam, Focal, Pioneer, Technics), and the 4-instalment plan costs no more than paying upfront. On content, price and language this is the strongest hands-on electronic-music training in Portugal for the money: €2,955 for 200 hours plus 40 studio hours plus 20 LAB hours, in English, with no entry barrier and no IELTS. But three things are unchanged and decisive: it is NOT a master's despite its name, it confers NO academic credit, and it CANNOT get him a residence permit — ProDJ's own page requires him to arrive already holding a valid visa. Paying €12,000+ including living costs to sit in Lisbon on a tourist footing with no legal study status is not a plan. THE RATIONAL SEQUENCE IS THE INVERSE: use an accredited master's (UCP Porto, Lusófona, or a funded ReSound place) to obtain the D4 visa and residence permit, then, once legally resident, add ProDJ's Master Producer as a €2,955 evening top-up in English while his status is secure. Never the other way round. One practical instruction: before paying anything, make ProDJ confirm in writing the enrolment fee (their own pages say €420 and €520), whether a DAW licence is included, and the exact total.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL HIGHER EDUCATION — and it is important he understands what DGERT is and is not. ProDJ is certified by DGERT (Direção-Geral do Emprego e das Relações de Trabalho), which sits under the LABOUR ministry and regulates VOCATIONAL TRAINING PROVIDERS. It is a legitimate quality mark for professional training and it is not a scam — but it is NOT an educational accreditation. Specifically: this is NOT accredited by A3ES (Agência de Avaliação e Acreditação do Ensino Superior) and is NOT registered with DGES (Direção-Geral do Ensino Superior), the two bodies that make a Portuguese qualification a recognised higher-education degree. Consequences: no grau académico, no ECTS, no place in the EHEA/Bologna framework, no automatic recognition abroad, no route onward to a PhD, and no standing in a visa assessment. It is not a 'mestrado' and it is not even a 'pós-graduação' — it is below both. It is a vocational training certificate, correctly labelled, from a properly certified vocational provider.

programs.recommendation: DO NOT BUY THIS COURSE — BUY THE MASTER PRODUCER INSTEAD. The verified arithmetic settles it. Producer I: €2,055 all-in for 100 hours (€20.55/hour). Master Producer, which CONTAINS Producer I plus Producer II: €2,955 all-in for 200 hours (€14.78/hour) — double the content and double the studio time for €900 more, with a LOWER enrolment fee (€420 vs €520) and an interest-free 4-instalment plan that Producer I does not match. Producer I is the worse deal on every axis, and if he ever wanted to continue to Producer II he would end up paying more in total than buying the bundle at the outset. Its only legitimate use is as a low-commitment trial of ProDJ's teaching before committing to the full programme — but at €2,055 that is an expensive trial for a certificate that is not a qualification, not a degree, not credit-bearing and not a visa. If he simply wants the content and is still in Tunisia, comparable structured Ableton instruction online costs a small fraction of this. Whatever he does, make him get the enrolment fee confirmed in writing first — the school's own pages contradict each other by €100.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL HIGHER EDUCATION. Certified by DGERT (Direção-Geral do Emprego e das Relações de Trabalho — the labour ministry's vocational-training regulator). NOT accredited by A3ES and NOT registered with DGES, so it is not a Portuguese higher-education qualification: no grau, no ECTS, no Bologna/EHEA standing, no PhD route, no weight in a visa assessment. Legitimate as vocational training; worthless as an academic credential. Not a mestrado and not a pós-graduação.

programs.reputationSignals: Positive: genuine international brand with campuses in London, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Barcelona and Lisbon; official Ableton Certified Training Center; a well-structured 6-level curriculum with a fit-for-release EP as the deliverable; one-to-one mentoring; class sizes capped at eight; probable English-medium delivery; and prices that — contrary to the draft — ARE published. Negative and serious: NO Portuguese accreditation of any kind, not even the DGERT vocational certification that ProDJ and EMMA both hold; no ECTS; no visa route; no published intake dates, forcing contact with a sales funnel to learn anything; no facilities inventory; no published graduate outcomes or named alumni; instalments likely carrying a 10% admin surcharge on the London precedent; and a BA (Hons) pathway sold at roughly €34,500 whose AWARDING UNIVERSITY IS NEVER NAMED — the site says only 'validated by one of our UK University partners' and 'a choice of validating universities'. An unnamed awarding body on a £28,600-equivalent degree is the single biggest red flag in this entire report. A degree is only ever as good as the institution whose name is on it, and Garnish will not tell him whose name that is until he is in the funnel.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €4,100–€4,600 all-in for the 120-hour Electronic Music Producer Program in person (tuition €3,999 + registration €200–€500 + optional iMac €75), before living costs. programs.recommendation: AVOID — IT IS STRICTLY DOMINATED BY PRODJ ON EVERY VERIFIED MEASURE. Now that the real prices are established, the comparison is no longer close. Garnish Lisbon: €4,100–€4,600 for 120 hours, no Portuguese accreditation of any kind, no studio hours disclosed, no equipment list, no published dates, no visa. ProDJ: €2,955 for 200 hours PLUS 40 studio hours PLUS 20 LAB hours, in English, with real DGERT certification, a published equipment inventory and published start dates. He would pay roughly €1,500 MORE for 80 FEWER hours from the ONLY provider in this slice holding no Portuguese recognition whatsoever. Garnish's genuine advantages — capped class of eight, one-to-one mentoring, the EP deliverable, the Ableton brand — are real but nowhere near worth a 55% premium for 40% less contact time and strictly less institutional standing. Separately and emphatically: DO NOT ENTERTAIN THE BA (Hons) PATHWAY. Roughly €34,500 for a Level 6 top-up whose validating university Garnish declines to name, entered with 'no formal education required' and a phone interview, delivered mostly online, is the highest-risk item anywhere in this report and would be a catastrophic use of a budget-sensitive applicant's money. If for some reason he still wants Garnish, the minimum discipline is a written quotation naming the total, the registration fee, the instalment surcharge, the exact start dates, the delivery language, and — for the BA — the actual name of the awarding university. Expect resistance on the last one.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — AND WEAKER THAN EVERY OTHER PORTUGUESE ENTRY IN THIS BATCH. Garnish Lisbon holds NO Portuguese educational recognition: not A3ES-accredited, not DGES-registered, and — unlike ProDJ and EMMA — not even DGERT-certified as a vocational training provider. It is an unregulated commercial school in the Portuguese system. Its 'Ableton Certified Training Center' status is a software vendor's partner programme, awarded by Ableton the company, and carries no educational or governmental weight anywhere. Its certificates are its own paper. On the BA (Hons): it is a UK Level 6 top-up 'validated by one of our UK University partners' — the partner is NEVER NAMED on the page, which is disqualifying on its own. Even if genuine, it would be a UK award, not a Portuguese one, carrying no A3ES/DGES status and no Portuguese residence rights. Nothing Garnish offers in Lisbon is a mestrado, a pós-graduação, or a recognised Portuguese qualification of any kind.
programs.verificationNotes: THE DRAFT'S CENTRAL FACTUAL CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. The draft stated Garnish publishes NO course prices in euros and that no cost estimate was possible. In fact prices are published across several Lisbon pages and were verified directly: Electronic Music Producer Program (Ableton, 120h) €3,999 in person / €2,679 online; 360° Academy €12,999 + €500 registration (€200 if 14 days early); 36-hour Electronic Music Production course €1,299 + €100 registration / €803 online; private tuition €90/hr with 3-hour minimum AND a previously unreported 24-hour package at €1,560 (€65/hr); iMac rental supplement €75. This transforms the entry from unassessable to clearly poor value. SECOND MAJOR CORRECTION: the draft stated the BA (Hons) route is awarded in London, delivered in Barcelona and NOT available at Lisbon. The Lisbon site does market a BA (Hons) pathway as accessible — 'Level 6 BA (Hons) top-up, validated by one of our UK University partners', hybrid delivery via a 'local Garnish student hub', up to 80% in person within 180 days, final year at a UK partner in person or online, priced at €11,500 per part × 3 parts (~€34,500), entry 'No formal education is required' plus a phone interview. The correct criticism is sharper than the draft's: the pathway exists but the AWARDING UNIVERSITY IS NEVER NAMED, which is a far more serious red flag than mere geographic unavailability. OTHER NEW FINDINGS: 6 named curriculum levels; class size capped at eight; London precedent of a 10% administration fee on instalments; Ableton EDU 40% discount NOT confirmed on Lisbon pages, so downgraded from the draft's assertion to UNVERIFIED; Garnish also operates San Francisco. CAUTION APPLIED: the €12,999 figure circulating in search results attaches to the 360° Academy, and a similarly-priced Barcelona 360° EMP exists — care was taken not to misattribute a Barcelona or Academy price to the Lisbon 120-hour producer programme. STILL UNVERIFIED: calendar duration in months, intake dates, delivery language for Lisbon specifically, registration fee for the 120h programme specifically, facilities inventory, entry requirements for certificate courses.

programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED. The production course is described as one of the most vocationally oriented in Portugal for home-studio work and DAW use, taking a track 'desde a ideia à concretização via Cubase e com recurso a teclado midi' — from idea to realisation via CUBASE with a MIDI keyboard — with emphasis on recording techniques, plugin use, mixing and audio mastering. Structure: Produção class + Songwriting class + Especialização (weekly projects), with free additional modules in Teoria Musical & Treino Auditivo, Ritmos Aplicados and Coro de Música Moderna, plus Combo as a paid add-on. The school also teaches guitar, voice and modern singing, piano/keyboard, drums, saxophone, violin, bass, musical initiation, combo, theory and ear training. CRITICAL MISMATCH CONFIRMED: the production teaching is CUBASE-centred, not Ableton — the wrong tool for someone targeting electronic music, DJing and live performance.

programs.visaEligible: NO. programs.reputationSignals: Positive, and one item stronger than the draft recorded: EMMA is a DGERT-certified training entity; it is run by a named practising musician (composer/guitarist Pedro Duarte); it operates what it says is the only long-form (8-semester) Curso Profissional de Música Moderna in Portugal; it is the SOLE PORTUGUESE PARTNER OF THE INSTITUTE OF CONTEMPORARY MUSIC PERFORMANCE (ICMP) IN LONDON, a genuine and reputable contemporary-music institution — a signal the draft missed entirely; it is genuinely cheap; and it offers broad instrument and musicianship teaching if he wanted to shore up his weakest area. Negative: it is in Queluz, not Lisbon, adding a commute; it is Cubase-centred when he needs Ableton; it is very small in scale; it publishes no facilities inventory and no price for the production course specifically; enrolment from age 12 means classes may be substantially adolescent; and there is no ECTS, no higher-education accreditation, no visa route and no published graduate outcomes. The ICMP partnership is a positive signal about teaching seriousness but confers NO degree, NO credit and NO qualification on EMMA's own students — do not let it be mistaken for a validation arrangement.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED. Indicative only: €60–€240/month across all the school's courses, i.e. roughly €720–€2,880 per year, with the production course's actual rate unpublished and requiring a direct request. Plus a Cubase licence and MIDI keyboard, and Greater Lisbon living costs if attending in person — none of it visa-bearing.
programs.recommendation: NOT A SERIOUS CANDIDATE FOR HIS PLAN — AND WEAKER ON VERIFICATION THAN THE DRAFT SUGGESTED. Three verified facts push this further down. It is in QUELUZ, not Lisbon — a suburban commute, not a city-centre school. It teaches CUBASE with a MIDI keyboard, which is the wrong toolchain for electronic music, DJing and live performance; he would be buying skills and software he then has to replace. And it enrols from age 12 over a 1-to-4-year, 3-level structure, which is a children's-and-hobbyists' music school cadence, not a professional intensive. Against that, the honest counterpoint stands: he has NO music training at all, and that — not gear, not software — is his real weakness for a portfolio-weighted selection like ReSound or Lusófona. Somewhere in the €60–€240/month band there is genuine value in theory, ear training and keyboard skills, and EMMA's free Teoria Musical & Treino Auditivo module plus its ICMP London partnership suggest the musicianship teaching is taken seriously. But he can get exactly that in Tunis or online for less, in a language he is fluent in, without a Portuguese commute and without a visa problem. VERDICT: exclude from the Portugal strategy. If he ever wants formal musicianship training, buy it locally or online — and if he wants production training in Portugal, ProDJ's Master Producer is better on toolchain, hours, facilities, English delivery and transparency for a known, fixed price.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL HIGHER EDUCATION. EMMA is certified by DGERT (Direção-Geral do Emprego e das Relações de Trabalho — the labour ministry's vocational-training regulator), a legitimate vocational quality mark and NOT an educational accreditation. It is NOT accredited by A3ES and NOT registered with DGES, so nothing it issues is a Portuguese higher-education qualification: no grau, no ECTS, no Bologna/EHEA standing, no PhD route, no visa weight. It is not a mestrado and not a pós-graduação. Its DGERT certification attaches chiefly to the 8-semester Curso Profissional de Música Moderna; the Produção Musical offering is fee-paying tuition, not a certified programme in its own right — UNVERIFIED whether the production course itself falls inside the DGERT scope, and he should ask. The ICMP London partnership is a commercial/pedagogical partnership only and confers no accreditation, no validation and no award.

The prior entry asserted that 'NO mestrado or pós-graduação in sound, audio, music production or music technology could be identified' and that Lusíada has no music presence whatsoever. Universidade Lusíada de Lisboa (DGES record estab=2410) runs (a) a LICENCIATURA EM JAZZ E MÚSICA MODERNA — a DGES-registered official first-cycle degree, 6 semestres / 180 ECTS, 31 vacancies in the 2026 national access competition, specialising in jazz or modern music (pop/rock), and (b) a MESTRADO EM MUSICOTERAPIA — an official 2-year / 120 ECTS second-cycle degree, described as the only music-therapy master's in Portugal, modelled on the American training model, still actively examining theses in July 2026. So Lusíada HAS a music department. What it does NOT have is any music-PRODUCTION, sound-engineering, studio or electronic-music programme. The conclusion for him is unchanged; the reasoning behind it is now correct.

programs.recommendation: RULE OUT — but for a corrected reason. The prior draft's claim that Lusíada has no music provision at all was wrong and would have been an embarrassing thing to tell him if he later found the jazz degree. The accurate position: Lusíada Lisboa HAS music — a Licenciatura em Jazz e Música Moderna (180 ECTS) and a Mestrado em Musicoterapia (120 ECTS) — but NOTHING in music production, sound engineering, studio work or electronic music. For a Tunisian national with no independent Dutch residence route, family connection or separate university registration, this programme is simply unreachable — no amount of money or portfolio strength changes that.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: the Abbey Road name is the strongest brand in the industry, with a genuine institutional link to Abbey Road Studios London and Universal Music; located inside Q-Factory, a real working music hub rather than an office block; teaching by industry practitioners with guest lectures from award-winning professionals; unusually generous six-day-a-week studio access; and a real portfolio-based selection process, meaning cohorts are self-selecting and serious. RED FLAGS: (a) NOT NVAO-accredited and not a degree — near-degree money for a private certificate; (b) cannot sponsor a visa, and this is buried in an FAQ rather than stated on the fees or course pages where an international applicant would see it before paying €200; (c) no named teaching staff, no named alumni and no graduate-employment statistics published anywhere; (d) no accreditation statement at all on the course or fees pages; (e) the only 'funding' offered is a tax deduction the institute itself concedes does not apply to the unemployed or newly arrived; (f) the fee pages have a history of going stale (a €16,400 figure from a 2022 update circulated long after it lapsed). No formal published complaints or regulatory actions were found.
programs.recommendation: OUTSTANDING SCHOOL, WRONG COUNTRY, AND NOT A MASTER — DO NOT APPLY. On pure craft this is the best hands-on music production and sound engineering training in this entire Dutch slice: real studios six days a week, Abbey Road pedigree, industry teaching, a serious portfolio-selected cohort. Three things kill it for him, and the first is fatal on its own. (1) IT CANNOT GET HIM A DUTCH RESIDENCE PERMIT — stated in writing by the institute, and the workarounds it suggests are open to Working Holiday and US DAFT nationals, not Tunisians. (2) It is NOT a master or any accredited degree — no NVAO, no ECTS, no PhD route, no credit transfer. (3) At €18,860–€20,160 tuition plus roughly €16,000 living costs it is among the most expensive options here for the least formal recognition — €33,000–€39,000 for an unaccredited diploma. He also does not currently hold the mandatory 4–8 track portfolio. MY ADVICE: rule Amsterdam out now and spend no application fee on it. If the Abbey Road brand genuinely appeals, look at Abbey Road Institute campuses in countries where a private school CAN sponsor a student visa — but go in understanding he would be buying training, not a qualification, and check that campus's accreditation separately, since it does not transfer across the franchise. THE ONE THING TO TAKE FROM THIS ENTRY REGARDLESS: adopt its portfolio spec — 4–8 finished tracks, each demonstrating a different role (performer, producer, engineer, writer), with his role documented per track — as his personal build target for September 2027 applications anywhere.
